titleEn: XRCLOUD ROOM New Features: Fast Entry and Logo Change
contentEn:
Hello. This is Luke from BELIVVR, the creators of XRCLOUD. It's been a while, but I'm here to introduce new features added to XRCLOUD: Fast Entry and the ability to explicitly change the ROOM entry logo.

​

1. Where can I get the Room URL?

Both features can be easily used by adding query parameters to the end of the Room URL. You can find the ROOM entry URL through the ROOM API or the Rooms menu in the XRCLOUD dashboard. For the API, you can develop with more security by using a Private Room URL that expires after 10 minutes.

{{IMG:1}}
                                
                            Room URL in the Rooms menu of the XRCLOUD dashboard

{{IMG:2}}
                                
                            Room URL in the response value of the XRCLOUD get Room API

These changes are related to the entry process. Since XRCLOUD customers primarily connect ROOMs to their own services, these new features were developed to reflect various requirements. The existing ROOM entry process for PC users involves a total of 5 steps, as shown below. First, I will explain this entry process, and then I will tell you about the changes.

2. Understanding the XRCLOUD (Hubs) ROOM Entry Process

{{IMG:3}}
                                
                            Existing ROOM Entry Process

- Loading page - This step involves loading various resources placed in the Room and connecting to the Room.
- Lobby - You can choose to enter, use another device, or spectate.
- Most of XRCLOUD's partners currently only use the "Enter" option, so we haven't focused on other features. "Use another device" provides a shortcut URL to enter with a VR HMD, and "Spectate" allows you to look around the room without directly participating. Spectators are not counted towards the room's connection limit, so they are not subject to the maximum room capacity. XRCLOUD currently supports 10 people for the free version, but we are currently (2024-10-02) providing direct development support, and for partners whose limits have been lifted, we support 100 people. Internal tests have shown that up to 140 people can connect.
- Avatar Viewer - This window shows the avatar connected to the Room. XRCLOUD does not provide an avatar selection feature; as guided in other posts or guides, you can change your avatar via the `avatarUrl` query parameter. You can use the [full-body avatar open source](https://github.com/belivvr/xrcloud-avatar-editor) developed by BELIVVR or the [Hackweek avatar Maker open source](https://mozilla.github.io/hackweek-avatar-maker/), or download an avatar and pass its URL. Similarly, the query parameter for changing the display name is `displayName`.

# avataURL use example 
https://room.xrcloud.app:4000/qkoCp3x/test2?public=04f740f3-b96f-43da-90da-5c99d64e2364
&avatarUrl=https://belivvr.github.io/files/Avatars/cnu_woman.glb
&displayName=GUEST

4. I/O (Input/output) Device Setting - This is the menu for setting up devices like microphones and speakers. If there are multiple microphones or speakers on the device, you can enter after confirming they are working correctly.
5. Room - Congratulations! You have finally entered the Room.
​

3. FastEntry

- That's quite a lot of steps, isn't it? Many users even skip important story parts in games these days, so having so many steps would make users leave. That's why we created the `fastEntry` option.

{{IMG:4}}
                                
                            Gamers these days

- Usage is very simple. Just like `avatarUrl`, if you add a query parameter to `funcs`, all steps are skipped. You can see the difference by copying the example URL above and the example URL below into your browser's address bar. Besides `fastEntry`, the `funcs` option also includes `3rd-view` to see the back of the avatar, and other parameters to control the exposure of menu components. However, I will organize and release information about `funcs` again once the permissions are properly sorted out.

# fastEntry use example
https://room.xrcloud.app:4000/qkoCp3x/test2?public=04f740f3-b96f-43da-90da-5c99d64e2364
&avatarUrl=https://belivvr.github.io/files/Avatars/cnu_woman.glb
&displayName=GUEST
&funcs=fastEntry

{{IMG:5}}
                                
                            fastEntry option

4. logoImg (Logo Image)

- XRCLOUD has been providing the ability to change favicons and logo images per project for free.

{{IMG:6}}
                                
                            XRCLOUD Project Dashboard

- However, a new requirement from a partner recently emerged: they wanted to change the logo for rooms generated for each user of their service. Since XRCLOUD provides features including the Spoke editor, we hadn't anticipated the need for Room or Scene Group management features or associated resource management features.
- So, we added a query parameter, `logoImg`, to directly replace the loading image's logo in the Room. To use it, simply pass the URL of the image as the `logoImg` query parameter, and the loading image and title image will change when connecting to the ROOM.
- The URL for the image below is [https://belivvr.github.io/files/images/posting-241003.jpg](https://belivvr.github.io/files/images/posting-241003.jpg).

{{IMG:7}}
                                
                            [https://belivvr.github.io/files/images/posting-241003.jpg](https://belivvr.github.io/files/images/posting-241003.jpg)

- Let's add the `logoImg` query parameter to the example URL above.

# fastEntry use example
https://room.xrcloud.app:4000/qkoCp3x/test2?public=04f740f3-b96f-43da-90da-5c99d64e2364
&avatarUrl=https://belivvr.github.io/files/Avatars/cnu_woman.glb
&displayName=GUEST
&funcs=fastEntry
&logoImg=https://belivvr.github.io/files/images/posting-241003.jpg

- Then it will appear as below. Easy, right?

{{IMG:8}}
                                
                            Changed logoImg

5. What BELIVVR is currently doing for XRCLOUD

* Updates to the [https://api.xrcloud.app/docs](https://api.xrcloud.app/docs) documentation are also planned.
* The two most urgent tasks currently underway are applying CDN to media uploaded to MyAsset in the Spoke editor and providing Room functionality that can accommodate 1000 users.
* Hubs was originally developed as a community tool for small groups, but XRCLOUD's partners primarily provide services for large audiences, so these requirements are significant.
* In particular, we have recently focused on the fact that `myAsset` uploaded via Spoke is encrypted through Reticulum and downloaded via XRCLOUD's Hubs server. This structure has led to increased costs and performance bottlenecks when handling large-scale connection services. Making the service stable to provide it more scalably is my biggest challenge right now, and I am contemplating how to provide more services with fewer resources. Of course, developing and handling technical support alone, funding issues are my biggest difficulty. Please give us a lot of support. Oh, I'm planning to attend a small exhibition in Korea in mid-October for the first time in a while. To showcase our partners' services at that exhibition, I'll also be doing some work on the front page of the XRCLOUD service page. Also, we fixed the broken feed on the xrcloud news page and improved performance by migrating servers with cloud support from MS FoundersHub due to cost issues. I may not be able to share updates frequently, but I'm working hard, so please give us a lot of support. Thank you.

{{IMG:9}}
For web metaverse, please visit XRCLOUD.app.

XRCLOUD Developer Center: Experience 3D spatial web and metaverse with low cost, fast access, and powerful features. Create your own metaverse in just 15 minutes without any separate installation program. You can build a web metaverse easily, quickly, and at a low cost, just like creating a website. We add necessary additional features for development and operation to the global metaverse open-source Mozilla Hubs, and even provide secure G-Cloud for public institutions. Prepare your web services for the era of XR spatial computing with XRCLOUD. Were you at a loss as to where and how to start when trying to create a metaverse space? All that complicated... xrcloud.app

https://xrcloud.app/

titleEn: VR Webtoon ComicsV, Tokyo Comic Con Attendance Review
contentEn:
This business trip was a busy one, as ComicsV was exhibiting at Tokyo Comic-Con and also on the verge of launching its DPVR HMD in Japan, so I wanted to observe the market closely. Despite the packed schedule, I managed to make time to attend. My daughter told me not to go, calling the Japanese "bad guys"... While Korea-Japan relations aren't great these days, I believe there's no nationality barrier when it comes to loving comics, so I went anyway.

{{IMG:1}} VR Webtoon ComicsV appearing at Tokyo Comic-Con

After attending Comic-Con alone and wandering around, I learned a lot. What are ComicsV's strengths? What should we do?

**1. Comic-Con as a Blockbuster IP Event**
Tokyo Comic-Con is a huge event. It was absolutely packed with people. However, it felt more like a Marvel event than a Japanese manga event. It was like a giant shopping mall consuming large American IPs, perhaps? There were incredibly high-quality figures, life-sized cars and characters from comics... But the overall impression was that Comic-Con is being redefined as an event for major IPs rather than a comic festival. In the past, after experiencing Pirates of the Caribbean at Disneyland, I truly understood the value that large IP-based experiences bring. The upcoming release of Frozen 2 will likely be part of this market trend.

{{IMG:2}} It was incredibly crowded. Sony Pictures was about the only one showcasing technology.

The virtual reality industry I'm involved in also pursues wonderful experiences that don't actually exist. The power of blockbuster IP is immense in terms of immersive, good virtual stories. This seems different from the fancy merchandise brought by Line, Kakao, or character-driven brands like Kakao's Ryan, Line's Moon, or Kitty. IP, or rather, the unique power of a special story, lives and breathes through text and images, and people are willing to open their wallets to experience that content, which aligns with what VR/AR pursues.

These blockbuster IPs also seem to have a characteristic of being continuously spun off or collaborating to generate revenue. I even wondered if the winner-take-all market characteristic of platform businesses also applies to IP. Much like the platform strategy of internet companies, users can get lost within that single worldview without time to explore other stories. Villains and heroes, now used as proper nouns within a massive worldview, are examples of this.

Especially in this market, Disney seems poised to become an incredibly formidable company. Netflix may have interpreted VR merely as a bigger screen, but Disney's immersive experiences at Disneyland felt different. The experience at Disneyland didn't require an HMD or glasses; you rode attractions, and following the content's guided gaze, a pirate ship suddenly emerged from the water, and you entered a vast dome of the underwater world. The boat you were on sailed into a battle between pirate ships and warships seen in movies. Various immersive technologies, often used in robotics and VR/AR, are applied here. And as VR/AR technologies become more widespread, they will bring amusement parks closer to us.

However, conversely... I also worry that the emergence of such large IPs might create a polarization in the content market, making it harder to pursue content diversity.

**2. Small-scale Experience Content at a Ninja Cafe**
On my last business trip, I experienced a Maid Cafe in Akihabara, and this time, I stumbled upon a unique concept called a Ninja Cafe and decided to go in. It certainly wasn't cheap. 1400 yen for a glass of orange juice? After experiencing it, it was essentially a ninja version of a Maid Cafe... More than half of the customers were tourists. It was a very small two-story restaurant, too small to even call a small theater, with only about 7 small tables and 5 female ninjas working. They made each customer awkwardly shout "Nin-nin" and had a "ninja dance" during a showtime. If I were to compare it to something similar in Korea, the content structure might be similar to a bar with hostesses. However, it was different in that it was more wholesome and offered a unique story and cultural experience.

{{IMG:3}} This is called "Ninja-go." I couldn't take pictures of the ninjas.

If I talked about blockbuster IP earlier, this time it felt like content that isn't limited to a specific IP but is genre-flexible for commercial spin-offs, with a small amount of labor "ground in" (to put it nicely, high job creation). In any case, since it's a face-to-face service, it allowed for a more human touch, and I felt like I had an enjoyable experience.

**3. Potential for Combining Small-scale Experience Content with Immersive Technologies like VR/AR**
I connected these two experiences and thought about them. In the case of the Ninja Cafe, it's an offline, labor-intensive service model that isn't easy to scale up. But what if immersive technology were applied here?

There was a place in Tokyo, almost 5-star rated on Google Maps for the keyword "VR," called Ninja VR. Unfortunately, it was sold out, and I didn't have time to go, but I suspect it might be a place that connects such unique experiences with VR to create content.

**The Best Ninja experience in Tokyo! - VR NINJA DOJO**
VR Ninja Dojo is a new Ninja experience facility that can only be experienced in Tokyo. If you are looking for things to do in Tokyo, please come to our dojo! vr-ninja.jp
https://vr-ninja.jp/

In contrast, I think the mistake Korean VR rooms made was precisely that point. Consumers go to consume content, not VR technology. In Korea, there are various VR content production projects, exhibition support, and calls for regional specialization, but I haven't seen many complete content experiences that include the physical space. In fact, through this experience, I even imagined creating a "Joseon Cafe" in Jongno (but I will focus solely on VR webtoons). In Korea, the closest comparable space would be the Folk Village.

**4. What ComicsV Can Do Well**
And now, back to ComicsV... The best reactions at Comic-Con came from the artists. On the first day, I briefly stopped by and let one or two artists try it out. When I explained that it's a platform where anyone who draws 2D can upload content, and that it's great for high-quality art that was difficult to consume on small mobile screens, everyone agreed and showed great interest. While mobile webtoons are indeed gaining attention as next-generation content, high-quality print comics still represent the largest market in both Japan and North America.

So, that very day, I quickly created artist brochures and met with artists one by one the next day.

{{IMG:4}} Hastily made at a cafe that day, printed at Kinko's

As expected, the reaction was very positive. People who love comics recognized its value. With the help of my poor English and a translation app, I explained it to over 20 people individually, and I realized that people who love comics are the same all over the world.

{{IMG:5}}

It was tough, but it also made me realize that this is what we do best, and it was rewarding. In that sense, ComicsV seems more suited for Comic Market than Comic-Con. Although ComicsV's system still needs a lot of development, I felt confident that we are on the right track. When I return to Korea, I'll make sure to greet all the contacts I received and continue to develop diligently.

{{IMG:6}} It was hard getting all these. But it was fun! (Tanoshi-katta desu~)

titleEn: [Ghost in the Shell Movie] Motoko Kusanagi Is Dead.
contentEn:
애니/만화

[Ghost in the Shell Movie] Motoko Kusanagi is Dead.

Luke ・ March 30, 2017. 0:24

Copy URL Add Neighbor

Body Other Functions

Ghost in the Shell

Director Rupert Sanders

Cast Scarlett Johansson

Release 2017 USA

View Details

As a huge fan of Ghost in the Shell, I was actually overwhelmed by the trailer for Ghost in the Shell starring Scarlett Johansson.

Ghost in the Shell GHOST IN THE SHELL 1st Official Trailer (Korean CC)

This is because the trailer successfully brought Mamoru Oshii's 1995 Ghost in the Shell and 2004's Ghost in the Shell: Innocence into the real world.

Ghost in the Shell

Director Mamoru Oshii

Cast Atsuko Tanaka, Akio Ōtsuka

Release 1995 Japan, UK

View Details

Innocence

Director Mamoru Oshii

Cast Akio Ōtsuka, Atsuko Tanaka, Kōichi Yamadera, Naoto Takenaka, Tamio Ōki

Release 2004 Japan

View Details

Although Scarlett Johansson being a Westerner was a bit jarring, her gaze and acting weren't bad. I'm such a huge fan of these incredible works – which I always mention when lecturing on virtual reality and software, are called the definitive cyberpunk works, and predicted many aspects of the current era – that I had vowed to definitely go see it when it came out. So, with a trembling heart, I finally went to see it.

* Note: My old TV series review

Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex

This anime, produced as a total of 26 episodes of Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex, was imported into Korea on DVD. Previously...

fstory97.blog.me

But... since I went to see it without any prior information, right from the start, I thought, "Uh... something's weird."

1. Brain in the Shell

First, an actual human brain, not a cyberbrain, is transplanted. Also, Motoko's original setting is that she was cyberized due to an accident at age 6 (TV series) or as a fetus (Arise), leading to short memories of her human body and constantly questioning her existence, which is then explored through various societal aspects... (Scarlett Johansson, Major. Since the Korean translation in the movie rendered "소령(소좌)" as "Major," I'll just call her Major.) Major is depicted as a human brain trapped in a robot body due to an accidental death caused by terrorists.

This difference in setting is actually a huge one. A cyberbrain means there is no physical body at all. According to recent news a few days ago, Elon Musk, famous for Tesla Motors, even created a company to pursue Neuralink technology, which corresponds to the implementation of such a cyberbrain.

Musk's New Challenge... "Insert Chip into Brain to Upload/Download Thoughts"

(Seoul=News1) Reporter Kim Jeong-han | Elon Musk, founder and CEO of Tesla, has reportedly established and is operating a company dedicated to "combining computers and human brains." On the 27th (local time), the Wall Street Journal (WSJ), citing informed sources, reported that 'Neuralink Corporation' (N...

news1.kr

A movie with a similar concept is not the Ghost in the Shell I'm introducing now, but rather Chappie.

Chappie

Director Neill Blomkamp

Cast Sharlto Copley, Hugh Jackman, Sigourney Weaver, Dev Patel

Release 2015 USA

View Details

The "ghost" is defined as software, but this Ghost in the Shell kept the brain, thus remaining trapped within hardware. It was the moment the original title, "Ghost in the Shell," faded. It should have been changed to "Brain in the Shell."

2. RIP Motoko Kusanagi

Motoko Kusanagi

Parent Document: Ghost in the Shell From top left: Original, Movie, SAC, SSS, ARISE 1. Overview 2. Differences by Series 2.1. Original Manga 2.2. Ghost in the Shell 2.3. Innocence 2.4. Ghost in the Shell: STAND ALONE COMPLEX 2.5. Solid State Society 2.6. Ghost in the Shell: ARISE 2.7. Ghost in the Shell (2017 film) 2.8. Other 1. Overview [Edit] "If you are dissatisfied with the world, change yourself. If you don't like that, cover your eyes and ears, shut your mouth, and live in solitude. If you don't like that either..." (世の中に不満がある

namu.wiki

Towards the end of the movie, Major visits her own grave. Although it was likely used symbolically as the grave of her body since her brain was removed, to me, the phrase "Motoko Kusanagi's grave" felt like the grave of the original character. The original Motoko Kusanagi was absent from this movie; what survived was Major.

In the original Ghost in the Shell, romantic feelings are hard to find, and above all, Motoko is a very strong female character, almost a representative of the "big sister" archetype. In the TV series, Motoko even selects the members of Public Security Section 9. In short, even if Aramaki holds the command authority, she is depicted as the de facto leader of Section 9. However, in the movie, her mental state is constantly supported by those around her.

While it's hard to say there were absolutely no scenes with a slightly ambiguous atmosphere between her and Batou in the original manga and anime, she is entirely an androgynous character. Or, to be precise, it would be more accurate to say she is an ambisexual character. Therefore, she is definitely not a damsel in distress character for Batou to rescue.

In Disney's Moana, she said, "I'm not a princess," but in my opinion, she still hadn't completely shed the princess image. In Ghost in the Shell, an absent princess image was imposed on Major Kusanagi, turning her into Major. Good heavens, the setting is a girl sacrificed to the greed of a mega-corporation!!!!! And her boyfriend from her past life appeared too. (It's ruined. This isn't Motoko Kusanagi.)

I had many complaints about the Korean transliteration "Major," but it even made me wonder if the translator intentionally did it to avoid overlapping the character with Major Kusanagi. Does that say it all?

3. RoboCop

The shell was clearly Ghost in the Shell. The direction, atmosphere, and music were all excellent. The depiction of the multi-legged tank was also cool... But the entire scenario was RoboCop. I never dreamed that this cliché of a human trapped in a robot, gaining a new life, and shedding tears while seeing their old family, would appear in Ghost in the Shell. If they had featured a daughter instead of a mother, and ED209 instead of a spider robot (multi-legged tank), it would have fit perfectly...

One of the unforgettable iconic scenes from Ghost in the Shell for me is the dazed expression of the cleaner when he realized his cyberbrain had been hacked. But here, he commits suicide. It's a quite shocking scene that sweeps through the entire content of Ghost in the Shell, but in this movie, it was reduced to mere emotional fodder about family.

And in the end, she actually meets her family. This was a family movie.

The characters in Ghost in the Shell are actually war mercenaries, seasoned veterans, genius hackers, and a veteran detective with a family who rejects cyberization. Each character's personality is clear and, in fact, cold. The only character connected to family and offering an outsider's perspective is Togusa. But with the Major gaining a family, it feels like Togusa's character is overlapped and everything became a mess.

Moreover, when the word "justice" appeared near the end, I really wanted to scream. The story of Ghost in the Shell actually has ambiguous justice. Section 9 is sometimes depicted as an organization that handles the government's dirty work.

4. The Silver Lining: Visuals and Still Welcome Characters

Looking at the original, many distinctive characters from Public Security Section 9 appear, and they were well-portrayed. (Except for Motoko, the protagonist). It's as if these characters were on an away mission. Batou, who used to be pushed around by the strong Motoko, might actually try to make a move on Major. Even if it's just cosplay, the outward appearance of those characters seems to have been well-preserved. If you forget the original story, it's a pretty decent movie. The only regret is that Fuchikoma or Tachikoma didn't appear... but since it feels like it heavily homaged the '95 film where Tachikoma didn't appear, I guess that's understandable.

If Tachikoma had appeared instead of the bulky multi-legged tank from the '95 film, wouldn't I have been less annoyed and found it cute?

titleEn: I'm More Worried About Parents Who Don't Understand Their Bratty Kids.
contentEn:
I saw a post on my timeline about the webtoon 'Bastard,' rated for all ages, expressing concern that children might watch it. I also raise a child, but because I remember encountering a lot of media and arguing with my parents when I was young, my feeling upon seeing this post was '꼰대' (old-fashioned/boomer).

[**평범한 아빠의 네이버 고소 이유? 웹툰의 전체이용가 진실 – Daum 아고라** m.bbs3.agora.media.daum.net](http://m.bbs3.agora.media.daum.net/gaia/do/mobile/petition/read?bbsId=P001&objCate1=1&articleId=187769&pageIndex=1)

The gist of it is that, based solely on the overall plot and expressions, it's harmful and shouldn't be watched. They mentioned having elementary and middle school children. I also raise a child. If I were to show this webtoon to Saebom, she would probably find it boring at first. There's too much text for children below elementary school age to read. And they might say it's too stimulating and scary. However, big and small stimuli are everywhere. When reading children's books, the range of expression is the issue; there are stories that deal with the death of parents, and children say they are sad.

[**후레자식** '내 집안에 살인마가 산다.' 본격 세대갈등 잔혹 스릴러 comic.naver.com](http://comic.naver.com/webtoon/list.nhn?titleId=628997)

This is not because children don't know about murder or killing, but because it's not within their scope of understanding. The moment it enters their scope of understanding, it can be scary or confusing. **No child will see the title 'Bastard' and think, 'Oh, I should try murdering too.' If they do, you've raised them poorly. You've turned your child into a robot.** It's like thinking that if they play games, they'll go outside and start shooting guns. On the contrary, the more you block external stimuli, the less they can tolerate even small stimuli, or they exhibit overreactions. This phenomenon also occurs with chocolate or games. I wonder if they read the 'Bastard' webtoon from beginning to end. **Demanding an R-rating based only on a captured image from the text is like demanding an R-rating for a wrestling screenshot because it looks suggestive (and it's even a homosexual work!).** **It's about the confrontation with a murderer father and twisted love-hate, not about the child being a bastard because the father is a murderer. I can't give you the detailed plot as it might be a spoiler, but please read it once.** If you want to stop your child, first watch/read it thoroughly yourself. It's a webtoon that offers a lot to think about. **I believe that media which provides food for thought, like this, can be more educational than spoon-fed educational materials. In my case, I actually developed my thinking skills through such media rather than textbooks.** **At the very least, play the game and read the webtoon before making a judgment.** **And, the first thing to do is not to sue, but to have a conversation with your child. Find out what your child felt and learned. If there's a problem with that, then it might truly be an issue with the work itself. (However, don't use leading questions.)** **If you did that without doing this, you've acted 100% like a '꼰대'. You've lost 10 points of trust with your children.**

{{IMG:1}}
TIG One Sound, 'How to Identify a Gamer Child'

Actually, of course, there are webtoons I would want to stop children from seeing. In these cases, it's not professional webtoons, but rather indiscriminate webtoons produced and distributed among children themselves, which sometimes cross the line by only depicting desires. The same goes for games ([http://goo.gl/oBrpPo](http://goo.gl/oBrpPo))

http://www.thisisgame.com/webzine/series/nboard/213/?series=42&page=3&n=47975
[**[TIG Cartoon] How to Identify a Gamer Child** [Warning] This video contains brutal scenes from <The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim>. www.thisisgame.com](http://www.thisisgame.com/webzine/series/nboard/213/?series=42&page=3&n=47975)

At least, the stimuli from webtoons and various media that are processed and provided to us are rarely as harmful as one might think. While it's partly true that we might become desensitized to stimuli, is our society one without stimuli? If I turn on the news, it's often too terrible to watch. Is it as terrible as a society where children speak disrespectfully to their deceased parents? Let's not cover our children's eyes. It's even more regrettable that the plaintiff is an ordinary father. Since when have our fathers become so isolated from their children?

{{IMG:2}}
Princess Mononoke

I will see the world with eyes unclouded.

From Princess Mononoke. Unlike Studio Ghibli's usual style, heads fly off and people die in droves, yet it's rated for all ages. What our children need is not just to have their eyes covered. Consider whether you are raising your child like a hothouse flower. **Becoming a '꼰대' is not a matter of age; it's a matter of empathy. Let them decide on media for themselves.**

**PS. Please refer to my thoughts on alternative education methods.**

http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/220754075458
[**Future Education Methods to Avoid Being a '꼰대'** My blog has been very noisy since yesterday due to the "Bastard" post. Since I've started, let's finish it. I've criticized... blog.naver.com](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/220754075458)

When reading children's books, the range of expression is the issue; there are stories that deal with the death of parents, and children say they are sad.

[**후레자식** '내 집안에 살인마가 산다.' 본격 세대갈등 잔혹 스릴러 comic.naver.com](http://comic.naver.com/webtoon/list.nhn?titleId=628997)

This is not because children don't know about murder or killing, but because it's not within their scope of understanding. The moment it enters their scope of understanding, it can be scary or confusing. **No child will see the title 'Bastard' and think, 'Oh, I should try murdering too.' If they do, you've raised them poorly. You've turned your child into a robot.** It's like thinking that if they play games, they'll go outside and start shooting guns. On the contrary, the more you block external stimuli, the less they can tolerate even small stimuli, or they exhibit overreactions. This phenomenon also occurs with chocolate or games. I wonder if they read the 'Bastard' webtoon from beginning to end. **Demanding an R-rating based only on a captured image from the text is like demanding an R-rating for a wrestling screenshot because it looks suggestive (and it's even a homosexual work!).** **It's about the confrontation with a murderer father and twisted love-hate, not about the child being a bastard because the father is a murderer. I can't give you the detailed plot as it might be a spoiler, but please read it once.** If you want to stop your child, first watch/read it thoroughly yourself. It's a webtoon that offers a lot to think about. **I believe that media which provides food for thought, like this, can be more educational than spoon-fed educational materials. In my case, I actually developed my thinking skills through such media rather than textbooks.** **At the very least, play the game and read the webtoon before making a judgment.** **And, the first thing to do is not to sue, but to have a conversation with your child. Find out what your child felt and learned. If there's a problem with that, then it might truly be an issue with the work itself. (However, don't use leading questions.)** **If you did that without doing this, you've acted 100% like a '꼰대'. You've lost 10 points of trust with your children.**

{{IMG:1}}
TIG One Sound, 'How to Identify a Gamer Child'

Actually, of course, there are webtoons I would want to stop children from seeing. In these cases, it's not professional webtoons, but rather indiscriminate webtoons produced and distributed among children themselves, which sometimes cross the line by only depicting desires. The same goes for games ([http://goo.gl/oBrpPo](http://goo.gl/oBrpPo))

http://www.thisisgame.com/webzine/series/nboard/213/?series=42&page=3&n=47975
[**[TIG Cartoon] How to Identify a Gamer Child** [Warning] This video contains brutal scenes from <The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim>. www.thisisgame.com](http://www.thisisgame.com/webzine/series/nboard/213/?series=42&page=3&n=47975)

At least, the stimuli from webtoons and various media that are processed and provided to us are rarely as harmful as one might think. While it's partly true that we might become desensitized to stimuli, is our society one without stimuli? If I turn on the news, it's often too terrible to watch. Is it as terrible as a society where children speak disrespectfully to their deceased parents? Let's not cover our children's eyes. It's even more regrettable that the plaintiff is an ordinary father. Since when have our fathers become so isolated from their children?

{{IMG:2}}
Princess Mononoke

I will see the world with eyes unclouded.

From Princess Mononoke. Unlike Studio Ghibli's usual style, heads fly off and people die in droves, yet it's rated for all ages. What our children need is not just to have their eyes covered. Consider whether you are raising your child like a hothouse flower. **Becoming a '꼰대' is not a matter of age; it's a matter of empathy. Let them decide on media for themselves.**

I lived without much thought about lifelong education, but ever since SW education began, I started to ponder a lot, and recently, reaching the issue of national history textbooks, I've come to realize that education is both Korea's most pressing issue and its greatest hope. In particular, I find the current national history textbook issue to be very, very regrettable. The reason is that political controversy is escalating while discussions about the most crucial aspects of education are being excluded.

**1. What Students Need is Problem-Solving Ability, Not Just Knowledge**
What is currently being discussed in relation to national textbooks mainly revolves around "what" to teach. Whether it should be red or blue... However, personally, I don't think this is the core of the problem. Let's say we're debating whether to teach children the geocentric model or the heliocentric model. Today, everyone knows that the heliocentric model is true, so one might ask why teach the geocentric model. But in fact, our education does teach the geocentric model. However, it teaches it within the history of science. It teaches how the geocentric model evolved into the heliocentric model. In fact, I believe the core here is not so much to teach the heliocentric model itself, but to teach how people rationally thought and deliberated to arrive at the heliocentric model.

Let's make an assumption here. At the stage of learning language, we blindly teach a child the heliocentric model without any prior information. The second scenario is our current educational approach: after learning language and expressions like 'the sun and moon rise,' unconsciously learning the geocentric model, then providing all information leading up to the heliocentric model, but *not* explicitly teaching the heliocentric model to the child. Without telling them about the heliocentric model, we teach that all planets and stars revolve around the Earth, and then provide all information that allows them to infer that Io (Jupiter's moon) revolves around Jupiter, just as Galileo did. Furthermore, let's overwhelm the child with numerous data points, such as information about solar and lunar eclipses, which cannot be explained by the geocentric model.

Which approach would make the child think more? And which would be the more appropriate education? The first child would easily mark the correct answer for the heliocentric model. The second child might come up with very strange and incorrect answers. Even if they aren't factually correct. Don't you think that one of the things we're discussing about education, namely knowledge – what to teach – is being focused on too blindly right now? Red and blue are not issues of good and evil. What children need is how to distinguish the difference between red and blue. I believe knowledge is closer to 'definition' than 'justice'. Its essence is not knowledge (data), but the ability to think (algorithm and process). Don't we emphasize the computing power of a computer, which models the human brain, more than its storage capacity? I hope we don't forget the core.

**2. How to Teach, Rather Than What to Teach?**
If the talent we desire is more about 'how' than 'what,' then the teaching method should also focus on 'how' rather than 'what.' Education should shift from being knowledge-centric to experience-centric. Assessment models should also move beyond mere tests and evaluations, towards sharing experiences and adding value. Instead of one-sided teaching methods and ranking by exams, a more humanistic and relationship-centered education is needed. For this, it's crucial to give children time where it's okay to make mistakes. A child who has never tried to correct a mistake has no chance of solving problems. Many professionals today say that while children nowadays are smart, have good academic backgrounds, and speak English well, they need to be taught everything from A to Z, or that they are incompetent at work. As mentioned before, if they were taught to master tricks for getting good test scores and that this was the best, then this outcome is quite natural. These children are too afraid of making mistakes.

This point must change. If you make a mistake in society, a company might fail, or a family might starve. Therefore, perfection and meticulousness are required. However, in school, if you make a mistake, you can simply correct it. That is education. In society, there's no room for education, and the consequences are too severe. But if even schools don't allow mistakes, where are children supposed to learn from making them? Our education needs to be more lenient with children who make mistakes, and it needs to wait for them.

I believe this is also why mathematics education is failing, and if SW education cannot incorporate this, it will follow the same path as mathematics education. In mathematics, it's difficult to move to the next stage without fully understanding the previous concepts. It's not a subject where you can briefly focus and just memorize parts to get scores. It's a discipline where you build knowledge step by step to reach higher levels. However, in Korean education, there are no separate methods prepared to help students who fall behind in the curriculum. Those children are treated as failures and punished, urged to work harder to catch up. Nori, a startup that recently received 7.3 billion KRW in investment, created a learning model to solve this by breaking down mathematical knowledge into smaller, modular, and relational units.

In addition, flipped learning, known as 'reverse classroom' in Korea, involves conceptual learning through videos online, and hands-on activities and group work during offline class time. This learning method also focuses on activities rather than exams, and since necessary knowledge can be accessed online anytime, anywhere, its learning effectiveness is high. What we need now is not 'what' to teach, but 'how' to teach. Let's do Hanja education. Let's do SW education. Let's do history education. There are reasons for these. In fact, there's no particular reason to oppose learning more. However, the important thing is that the current exam-oriented education focuses on how much one knows, or rather, how few mistakes one makes. In such a framework, there is no place for proper education.

**3. Innovating Study and Education is How the Nation and Future Survive.**
An image uploaded to the Facebook account 'God of Study'. This is actually the reality.{{IMG:1}}
Wow... one might think that with this much effort, everyone would study well. But if our education measures how well one can memorize things by reviewing them 10 times and making no mistakes, then it is fundamentally flawed. In fact, the human brain is a very poor machine for remembering information without errors. The brain (a biological entity) is evolutionarily biased and full of errors. And, in fact, it is precisely because of this that creative results emerge. But if we are selecting excellent students based on such an absurd criterion, isn't that a real problem?

National history textbooks are important. I am fundamentally against standardizing knowledge. I believe anyone involved in 'science' would think the same way I do. Instead, I would recommend a wiki as an alternative. Correct knowledge cannot be knowledge written by a few and disseminated uniformly. Knowledge should include not only the result of consensus but also the process of consensus. In that regard, wikis are good because the content of discussions is publicly available, and various perspectives can be continuously documented. However, the problem with the national history textbook controversy is that even the opposing side's perception of education isn't significantly different, which is regrettable. Thus, the energy needed for educational innovation seems to be wasted on unproductive matters. That is precisely what we should be criticizing. I hope that the interest in national history textbooks spreads to a desire for educational innovation, including SW education. While we are debating left and right, children are screaming.

titleEn: What Hyundai Needs to Change to Become Tesla
contentEn:
This column was written at the request of Smart Choice.

**Original: What must Hyundai Motor change to become Tesla? (2014-10-21)**
[http://www.smartchoice.or.kr/smc/smartreport/smarttalkview.do?sm_Seq=2740](http://www.smartchoice.or.kr/smc/smartreport/smarttalkview.do?sm_Seq=2740)

**1. Samsung's Crisis Began with Software.**

Recently, rumors of Samsung's crisis have been circulating due to its sluggish earnings announcement. While some even interpret Samsung's crisis as Korea's crisis, let's set aside such discussions and talk more dispassionately about the root causes of Samsung's crisis. I believe the cause of Samsung's crisis lies in software. The smartphone market created after the iPhone saw a paradigm shift from hardware to software, and while Google successfully countered the iPhone with the power of its software, Samsung, lacking a software platform thereafter, has entered a crisis situation – this is how I view the market.

More specifically and narrowly, this could refer to software distribution platforms like Google Play or messenger platforms like KakaoTalk, but these specific examples are not the entirety of the paradigm shift.

The shift to a software-centric society and what a software company and a pro-software culture mean is a much larger story. So, if I were to give one more example of what I'm currently thinking, I'd like to discuss 'what is software-centric?' with another example.

**2. Apple and Samsung, Tesla and Hyundai**

What companies come to mind when you think of companies representing South Korea? If there's Samsung for semiconductors and mobile phones, there's Hyundai Motor in the automotive industry. Many discussions revolve around threats to Hyundai Motor, such as low-cost cars from China and India, European brands, and technology that achieves high fuel efficiency. Additionally, Hyundai's corporate margins, which can be affected by rigid labor issues, are also pointed out as problems. However, I consider these issues to be rather secondary. Although not widely introduced in Korea, there is a figure shaking up the global automotive market: the genius Elon Musk, often called the real-life model for the movie Iron Man. Elon Musk is currently the CEO of Tesla Motors and is known in Korea as the person creating a sensation in the electric vehicle industry overseas.

Recently, when Elon Musk visited Japan, the headline published in Huffington Post Korea was [Elon Musk, "Japan is the Heart of Tesla"].

http://www.huffingtonpost.kr/2014/09/15/story_n_5820472.html
                                [**Elon Musk, "Japan is the Heart of Tesla"** Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla Motors, recently visited Japan. He has a knack for surprising the media with unexpected remarks, and this time, what did he say? www.huffingtonpost.kr](http://www.huffingtonpost.kr/2014/09/15/story_n_5820472.html)

Since LG Chem currently held a significant share in batteries, the most crucial component in electric vehicles, it seems domestic media couldn't help but react sharply to Elon Musk's statement. And after that, this article was published.

http://biz.chosun.com/site/data/html_dir/2014/09/25/2014092502766.html
                                [**'LG-branded electric car' only awaits Vice Chairman Koo Bon-joon's decision** 'LG-branded electric car' only awaits Vice Chairman Koo Bon-joon's decision biz.chosun.com](http://biz.chosun.com/site/data/html_dir/2014/09/25/2014092502766.html)

Can Korea, as a country with a good car company like Hyundai Motor and the ability to produce core components for electric vehicles, truly dominate the electric vehicle market? Unfortunately, my answer is 'no'. Within the first article about Elon Musk that I introduced, there's a more important hint hidden than who, Japan or Korea, makes Tesla's parts.

“Tesla will program the entire system and software, but some sensors and sub-components will be sourced from various other companies.”

Currently, Korea's smartphone market is dominated by Android. And Samsung is a representative company producing Android smartphones. Among the companies producing Android smartphones, there's also SONY, a leading Japanese company. Now you understand what I'm trying to say, right? The country that makes Tesla's car parts or the finished products for the Tesla platform, whether it's Japan or China, might not be as important as you think. If Korea offers better conditions than Japan, Tesla can place orders with Korea at any time. Just like Google's Nexus came out from Samsung, then LG.

**3. Why Do These Differences Occur? Characteristics and Power of Software Companies**
*   It doesn't just mean the number of software personnel or proprietary technology.
As I mentioned earlier, I said software is more important, but this should not be misunderstood as simply having a large number of software personnel or exceptionally high technology. Of course, that is important and a necessary condition for the paradigm shift I'm talking about, but it is not a sufficient condition. Many Koreans work at Google, and Korean developers are highly sought after in Silicon Valley. And Samsung possesses even more excellent developers than that. Therefore, I believe it's difficult to find the cause based solely on this.

**4. The Difference Between Apple and Samsung, Tesla and Hyundai, as I See It**

The difference I perceive lies in a more comprehensive corporate culture and approach.

Apple is a company that creates things for users holding iPhones, while Samsung is a company that makes smartphones. Furthermore, Tesla is a company that creates things for people who drive Teslas, while Hyundai Motor is a company that makes cars. Do you see the difference?

Let me rephrase that. Apple is a company that creates things for mobile users connected to the internet via iPhones, and Tesla is a company that creates things for users who want to move from one place to another.

For Apple and Tesla, smartphones and electric vehicles are tools to solve user problems, and they are just one of the solutions they offer, not the entirety of the product. Rather, for them, the customer is everything. They are approaching more fundamental problems. As a result, they might not even need to sell iPhones and electric vehicles if necessary. In the case of Amazon, which wanted to deliver content to customers, they practically gave away Kindles for free.

The essence of a software company is to solve problems that people face. In fact, there's no need to debate whether one is first or second in a specific industry, or whether one is a fast follower or a first mover. While this might be meaningful to those who like to rank or categorize, it may not be very significant for those pursuing innovation. There isn't a specific industry, but rather specific problems, and various companies are racing to solve those problems.

As software organically involves processes of combining (grouping), dividing (categorizing), and connecting (networking), it becomes ambiguous even to define which industry category a software company belongs to. Is Apple, which makes OS, a software company or a hardware company? Is Tesla Motors, which plans to distribute electric charging stations, a car company or an energy company? And, surprisingly, the neurons in our brains operate this way. The power of software can be said to be consistent with the power of our thought.

**5. The Path Samsung and Hyundai Must Take: Becoming Software Companies Focused on Problems.**

The software company I envision is not just a company with many developers. A software company means that its organization and culture themselves embody software. While many software-related technologies will be needed to approach this, what's more important is breaking free from hardware-dependent ways of thinking.

A software mindset that approaches problems with a more fundamental problem-solving perspective is what can create a software company. On the contrary, large corporations like Samsung and Hyundai, with their robust organizations, processes, and cultures, might be the most challenging companies for software innovation. However, what is clear is that a hard rock can be broken by a soft wave like software. This is not a problem caused by the rock being less hard. It's because an irresistible tide is rising. The history of industrialization is only about 200 years, but the human brain has been inherently software-like for over a hundred thousand years. The essential power that humans possess lies in software.

Source: Smart Choice ([http://www.smartchoice.or.kr/)](http://www.smartchoice.or.kr/%29)

Due to the birth of my second child, I haven't been able to post much. I'd like to share my personal thoughts on a question many are curious about: 'Will MS revive in 2013?'

** 1. Windows Phone, well... Tablets, a green light**
First, it seems difficult to guarantee MS's success with Windows Phone. Android phones reached a stage of success by leveraging high openness compared to iPhones and aligning well with manufacturers' interests. However, if MS simply follows the direction of these two existing companies, the market will not respond. Neither manufacturers nor users have a clear reason to choose an MS phone.
However, in the case of tablets, the story is a bit different. Just as Android and manufacturers had well-aligned interests, there are factions in the tablet market that need MS. These are the manufacturers who previously made laptops and PC companies. They already consider the iPad a threat. Compared to the smartphone market, the tablet market has not yet fully established itself, leaving room for MS to intervene.

** 2. Differentiation from other tablets: Windows 8's concept is a productivity tool**
The position of smartphones was dominated by killer apps based on mobility, such as GPS and cameras. For tablets, killer apps centered around media consumption, like Netflix, Amazon, and Apple's iBooks, tend to succeed.
However, there's one area where they haven't yet overtaken the PC camp: productivity tools. While companies like Evernote have achieved very high growth, they are not yet comparable to MS Office.
There is clearly a need for productivity tools. And not many users will want to buy two devices: one for media consumption and one for work. The biggest advantage of Windows 8 is precisely these productivity tools. The concept of Windows 8 must be aligned with productivity tools. Windows 8's killer apps will be Office, Eclipse, Visual Studio, Photoshop, and others provided by MS. What MS needs to consider is how well these productivity tools can be customized for tablets.

** 3. Will the savior be RT (ARM) or Pro (Intel)?**
If we divide it purely by technology, a clear answer doesn't readily emerge. However, **what is clear is that if two types of apps are not compatible, one must surely be eliminated.** In a situation where it's difficult to compete with even one capability, offering two platforms makes it hard to gain trust from third parties.
From a user's perspective, if you ask which of the two types will succeed, **RT's weakness is the current absence of PC-based killer apps like Eclipse, Visual Studio, and Photoshop. Porting these quickly is paramount.** **Pro's weaknesses are short battery life and high price.** While Pro's advantage is high performance, it doesn't stand out significantly compared to Android or iPad. Ultimately, I wonder if the answer to whether Intel-based low-cost mobility architectures like Atom, which aim to compensate for these weaknesses, will save or kill Pro.
The conclusion is that whether it's RT or Pro, **the device that first achieves an appropriate level of performance and productivity relative to Android's price will succeed.** If Eclipse and Photoshop for Android tablets emerge, and the Office market is taken away, Windows tablets might lose their place. I'll exclude the iPad for now. The iPad is a work device that is difficult to adapt to corporate requirements, making it hard to replace a PC. That's why MacBooks aren't eliminated. The distinction becomes clear when comparing MS and Apple. Apple separated the OS for tablets and laptops, but MS combined them.

** 4. The biggest challenge: How to embrace Windows 7 users?**
I installed Windows 8 on my touch laptop, the TM2. The biggest change I noticed was the disappearance of the Start Windows button. When pressing the Windows button, the Metro UI and Desktop UI alternately switching back and forth was a bit confusing. **Users who use professional productivity tools, such as developers, are likely to remain in Desktop mode because they utilize various Windows applications.** In my case, my company's VPN didn't work properly on Win8, so I ended up installing Win7 with multi-boot. This is a problem that cannot be solved until the application is redistributed as a Metro app, and it's an area MS must address with determination.
However,** for users who only use web browsing and Office, everything can be handled within the Metro UI.** How to approach these users is the most important issue. While I gave them good marks for the attempt, I couldn't give good marks for the execution. The most difficult thing about Windows 8 installed on my TM2 was not being able to find the Control Panel. And all the icons created by installed applications were arranged on the Metro UI, making it messy. I only use Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, but other Office buttons were listed on the Metro UI, and it was more work to delete them. Also, I had no idea how to use the right-click mouse button or long-press on the screen with both mouse and touch. Many menus were hidden off-screen, which caused confusion. Simple rules that users can recognize for interaction between touch and mouse/keyboard, along with an app to guide them, are also needed.
If the habit transition of existing Windows users is not successful, Windows will remain only in Desktop mode, and eventually, the productivity tablet market will be taken by Android. **As long as people work, Windows 8 will sell this year. However, what I'm most curious about at the end of this year is not the success of Windows 8, but the success of the Metro UI.**

titleEn: What I Want from Naver Blog as a Na
contentEn:
Recently, Naver reportedly held a meeting (or discussion) for IT bloggers. Of course, I also received an invitation email, but I couldn't attend as it was on a Saturday lunchtime. Even if I could have attended, I felt it might look bad given my company affiliation. Anyway, I was able to read about the event through other bloggers' posts. This has prompted me to talk about Naver's blog service after a long time. I have no idea how Naver plans to manage its blog operations or what they are currently working on internally. **Therefore, I will simply discuss the pros, cons, and my wishes for Naver Blog purely from a blogger's perspective.**

**1. Why I chose Naver Blog**
**- Easy to customize, and can legally add BGM.**
As I've mentioned in a previous post, I didn't think too deeply about it. While there was a need to learn about the company's own services, I was more captivated by the powerful skin features and the ability to legally add BGM.
**- A blog where I can focus solely on content.**
Self-hosted bloggers often say that portal blogs are for beginners, but from a tech perspective, I don't think my tech skills are inferior to self-hosted bloggers. My major was computer science, my minor was media studies, and I taught Photoshop to juniors in a club during college. I also took courses in graphics and pattern recognition and have worked for several years developing web services at a company.
Nevertheless, the reason I chose a "low-level" (?) portal was that I didn't want to set up SQL or look at CSS code even while blogging. Personally, I believe a developer's true skill lies not in mastering difficult tools, but in knowing how to use the appropriate tool. **In that sense, a portal blog was the most suitable tool for me, as I wanted to focus on content.** And, as someone who originally used mini-hompy, the appropriate skin features and BGM usage were the biggest reasons. (It annoys me when certain T-bloggers consider Naver or Daum portal bloggers to be of a lower standard.)

**2. Advantages I felt while using it**
**- Search exposure through various channels, rich content attachment - Content Attachment feature**
So, the advantages of Naver Blog that I chose were, as mentioned, easy skin features (which can be "borrowed" from Item Factory, or slightly modified) and BGM. And one of the biggest advantages I felt while using it was "search exposure." This isn't necessarily because Naver Bloggers get special priority (in fact, since I've always used Naver Blog, I haven't noticed the difference), but rather the diverse search traffic inflow through the "Content Attachment" feature. Naver Blog's content attachment feature, which allows attaching books, movies, shopping products, or similarly, maps, brings in traffic from various Naver section services. For shopping, it comes through netizen reviews, and for maps, it comes through map searches. Inserting these section objects allows bloggers to more specifically define the nature of their blog content and creates connections between objects across sections. For example, if you write a book review about Steve Jobs, you can insert Steve Jobs as a person and his books. This way, while reading the post, readers can link to reliable portal section information, enriching the content. Also, traffic from map POIs (Points of Interest) is surprisingly good. Of course, Daum also provides similar features, and in Daum's map POI, you can send feedback via RSS to indicate that it's a POI. (I find it a bit regrettable that Naver doesn't have this feature.)

**- Always grateful for the temporary save function**
When writing long posts, I often encounter the frustration of losing my work. Each time, I'm grateful for the temporary save function provided by Naver Blog.

**3. Disadvantages and Wishes**
Of course, there are many disadvantages. Now I'd like to talk about them. The points I consider disadvantages also align with my hopes for Naver Blog's future direction.

**- Slow and buggy Power Editor, wish they'd stop enhancing customization features...**
First, my dissatisfaction with the editor: Power Editor. True to its name, it's powerful. Formulas, polls, post formats – there's nothing it can't do. It's like a word processor. But with its powerful features, it's slow, behaves differently across browsers, and seems to have frequent bugs. When trying to edit, the enter key acts strangely, etc. It's truly frustrating more often than not. I genuinely wonder if there are users who utilize all those many features. There was a time when the web was rushing towards RIA (Rich Internet Applications). And even now, the potential for RIA is not small. However, is RIA really key for a blog? Most so-called power bloggers primarily use text. They mostly use font size changes, bolding, color changes, and center alignment. And photo insertion.
The characteristic of "wife bloggers" who create complex and elaborate layouts is that they post with images. Why? Because image editing is much easier than wording, just as most online shopping mall content is image-based. That said, I don't want to suggest enhancing image editing features in Power Editor. It's already powerful enough, and users who want more powerful tools already use Photoshop. If Power Editor's goal isn't to be an office product like MS Office 365, then I believe it should stop enhancing complex, unnecessary, and heavy editor features. Instead, it would be better to remove frequently unused customization features to allow users to focus more clearly on content creation.

**- Daum View not exposed on mobile blogs**
Even though the Daum View button is Flash, it doesn't appear on Naver's mobile blog. A blogger's biggest need is exposure. Since Naver doesn't have a meta-blog service, traffic from Daum's meta-blog service is a coveted resource for most bloggers. Rather than strengthening Daum's service by exposing it, I believe this would be an opportunity to increase Naver bloggers' chances of reaching Daum View.

**- Ambiguous 'Like' button**
Naver Blog allows 'Like' (공감) and 'Me2' (미투). While 'Like' actually came first chronologically, it's hard to understand what benefits 'Like' provides to Naver bloggers. (Does it help with blog section exposure...?) Furthermore, it lacks the viral effect compared to the 'Me2' button, so its impact is weaker. It would be better to either remove the 'Like' button or make 'Like' automatically trigger 'Me2' – consolidating them into one. What bloggers really want is a 'like' button, but perhaps that's too much to ask.

**- Clarifying the relationship between Open Neighbors and Me**
Open Neighbors is the only feature within Naver that allows communication with external bloggers via RSS. To be precise, it's a system that also allows subscribing to external newspaper articles. In fact, this feature should belong in Naver Me, and I believe RSS and neighbors are distinctly different functions. I wish it would be organized more cleanly.

**- Making the blog section a meta-blog**
The blog section merely lists bloggers' posts by latest, or " 주목순" (attention order? 'Like' order? I'm not sure what order it is). I wish the criteria for exposure here were clearer. That way, bloggers would also be motivated. This is why users are so desperate for the Daum View button. From Naver's overall service perspective, if it were ordered by 'Me2' count and allowed external blogs with 'Me2' buttons to participate, wouldn't it be a win-win?

**- Social Apps? Me2day? Why are these attached to the blog?**
At one point, I also thought it might be good to do everything on a blog, but the longer I blogged and the more I communicated with people, the more clearly I felt that users want different things from different services. What people want from a blog is content. They don't come to play games. It's not a place to write short messages like Me2day. If you try to do everything, a blog becomes a mini-hompy. However, mini-hompy is already a defunct service. It lost to Naver Blog in terms of content and to Facebook for daily sharing.
What is Naver Blog's position? To be like a mini-hompy, doing everything? Sharing small daily moments should be left to SNS. In fact, users already perceive it that way. I believe it's right to boldly abandon such features. And a blog cannot become a platform like Facebook either.

**4. Blogs are, unequivocally, content publishing tools.**
This cannot be emphasized enough. Even with the advent of the SNS era, the value of blogs has not disappeared. In SNS, you can't ramble on with long posts like this; instead, you write content on a blog and then viral it through SNS. And such high-quality content is a great help for search. This role is clearly divided. From that perspective, a blog's role, true to its original purpose, should be to provide means to easily create content and widely viral it. Meta-blogs and SNS currently exist as viral tools. A blog that only its neighbors see is no different from a mini-hompy. I hope Naver Blog becomes a platform that helps bloggers create content and communicate.

titleEn: iPhone is Waking Up Sony and Nintendo:
contentEn:
Previously, power blogger Multiwriter ([http://www.multiwriter.co.kr](http://www.multiwriter.co.kr/)) discussed the possibilities of an NDSL phone. At the time, I felt it was quite far from my vision of the ultimate open OS and the 'smartness' of a smartphone, and my personal opinion was that it would be difficult for a company like Nintendo to develop a mobile phone. However, looking at the recent usage patterns of iPhone users, it seems not only that the possibility exists, but more importantly, it is stimulating both Sony and Nintendo.
The reason for this is that the iPhone, rather than being approached as a phone for a traditional office environment, is being approached primarily for gaming, much like existing feature phones.
 
**1. The iPhone and App Store are threatening the portable gaming market of PSP and NDSL.**
**** 
{{IMG:1}}
 [ iPhone Gamepad iControlPad:  [http://asrai.hosting.paran.com/blog/?p=554](http://asrai.hosting.paran.com/blog/?p=554) ]
 
And another major market change lies in the success of the iPhone itself. As the iPhone succeeds, the power of the App Store is growing. Software reaching hundreds of megabytes is appearing, which is tantamount to predicting the participation of existing video game developers. Users find it inconvenient to carry two devices like the PSP or NDSL, and above all, this wave is directly impacting the market, effectively eroding Sony's and Nintendo's portable gaming market share. The fact that it directly touches money, the most fundamental reason for companies to act, creates pressure not only for Sony, which can relatively easily enter the mobile phone industry, but also for Nintendo, which is relatively closer to a software company, to create something to counter the iPhone. Furthermore, this situation becomes a threat to the traditional portable gaming powerhouses as Google, a much larger entity, joins in.
 Moreover, Sony seems to be facing management difficulties recently, and appears to have chosen entertainment as a solution.
 Sony to merge 'Game-Consumer Electronics' groups  [http://www.zdnet.co.kr/Contents/2009/12/29/zdnet20091229095101.htm](http://www.zdnet.co.kr/Contents/2009/12/29/zdnet20091229095101.htm) 
 
 
**2. The Special Nature of the Content-Dependent Gaming Industry**
 Considering only the threats mentioned above, the situation is entirely disadvantageous for Sony and Nintendo. Although Sony possesses world-class technology, it's uncertain how well it can compete in the platform market against giants like Google and Apple. For Sony, which almost monopolized the video game market, this must be a frightening situation, especially considering its experience of ceding significant ground to MS with the Xbox.
 However, the gaming industry has a special characteristic: it is entirely content-dependent. Although the NDSL was a hidden card that later became a huge hit, Nintendo's survival was entirely due to a few blockbuster-level content titles rather than the excellence of the device itself. Furthermore, **the current App Store is highly likely to re-enact the Atari Shock. Whether big or small, it will surely come.** **When the pent-up demand for smartphones is fully met, and the accelerated growth rate stagnates, the market that exploded with anticipation will reveal its limits, and a painful process of separating the wheat from the chaff will occur. What will survive during this process are likely a few very well-made indie games and mostly robust traditional gaming powerhouses. Names like EA, Blizzard, NC Soft, Nexon, for instance.**
 At this point, existing gaming powerhouses, namely Sony and Nintendo, will be able to secure good positions or gain hints for survival. What they possess is entirely content.
 In fact, game phones already existed in Korea. There was Samsung's SCH-B550, for example, but G-pang already had limitations in securing content. I previously discussed [why WIPI, the platform for feature phones, failed](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70075401680) in a previous post. Even G-pang, which was a 3D platform, was destined to meet the same fate as WIPI entirely because of expensive content distribution costs, which prevented it from securing enough killer content. Similarly, the GP32, famous as the 'Myungbak phone,' also failed to secure content and met the same fate. Thus, it is true that the gaming industry is a content industry. From that perspective, Sony and Nintendo, who have already secured abundant high-quality content, cannot be ignored. (The same goes for MS. Scary guys..)
