Therefore, I decided to use the entire study material as a memo pad for schedule management.

I've gathered all the study materials I've accumulated on my mini-homepage,
and even old work memos from when I used to work, but
the size limitation makes it difficult to review them all at once or browse through them easily.
Perhaps SK Comms' presentation on mini-homepages includes this inherent problem.

I had a complaint about the memo pad, so I went to the website to write down improvements for it...
and it downloaded a new bulletin board in ActiveX form.

And when I tried to use the "tong" (a feature on Cyworld), again... a new bulletin board...

Even the help desk within Cyworld...

On WINXP, you have to click to use ActiveX.

I feel like something is wrong.

It's the same module with the same role within one company...
Why do I have to download and install it every time?

Moreover, even Microsoft recently announced it would reduce ActiveX support,
and the Firefox browser, which accounts for 10% of the world's browsers, doesn't even support it.

If you look at the list of ActiveX installations on my PC, it's truly enormous.
I somehow feel like things are going in the wrong direction.

Couldn't SK Comms use just one bulletin board module?
Of course, the skin could be modified according to the purpose of the bulletin board, and each component could be changed so that one bulletin board could appear in different forms across all sites.

When the bulletin board is upgraded, all bulletin boards used by SK Comms would be upgraded.
It would also support standard features like RSS.

It seems to me that these numerous bulletin boards are a waste of human resources, and a waste of resources from the user's perspective.

In terms of security, if bulletin boards were unified, it would be easier to respond to issues.

I'm not a web professional, so I don't know much,
but as SK Comms grows in size, it seems to be getting messy.
Considering that Naver has an interface where search results and all posts look the same, and each piece of data is mutually compatible, SK Comms' various areas seem too separated.

As a user, this was an impertinent intervention.

titleEn: Naver Email and Message Board Integration Plan
contentEn:
I published a webzine to organize my thoughts, but I found some inconveniences.
I used the same emailing method I used back in my freshman year of college.
I couldn't find any better solutions for this purpose compared to back then.
While the limitations of a single page, such as inserting music or images, in today's posts
have greatly improved, it seems difficult to get feedback from a desired group.

Blogs and Cyworld Papers have the limitation of reaching an unspecified public.
Currently, as a one-person media, I think Cyworld Paper is better than a blog.

I've also published a few papers.
However, the limitation of Paper is that you can only send emailing lists to your "1-chon" (friends)
or you have to manually add each email address.
Because of this, in my case, I couldn't send it to the many people in my NateOn address book.
The reason for using NateOn's address book was that data compatibility was easy, and it was easy to link with mobile phones.

It's similar to why Outlook's PIMS address book is powerful.
I'm not sure if Naver currently has such PIMS-related solutions.
This is because they tend to focus more on solutions for public information rather than personal information.
I'm "1-chon" with Cyworld CEO Yoo Hyun-oh, so I wrote a post on my mini-homepage about the compatibility between Nate's address book and Cyworld,
but it seems that mini-homepage is managed by an employee. Instead of listening to opinions, I only get replies that are typical of a customer service center.
That's not why I wrote those posts there.
In fact, I've been rooted in Cyworld for so long
that I have difficulty utilizing Naver Blog.

Furthermore, Naver Blog is not 'real-name' for the purpose of social networking,
and seems to be aimed solely at sharing rather than personal information management.
I'm trying to say that Naver has one advantage over Cyworld.
Firstly, there's its differentiated information sharing and diverse content,
and secondly, anyone who has a Naver Blog must also have a Naver email account.

In fact, I'm using NateOn Messenger because I'm attracted to the power of its integrated solution,
but NateOn's PIMS system still has limitations,
and most importantly, it still only pursues limited integration with the web or mini-homepages.
I'm not sure what I'm talking about as I write this.
It just occurred to me yesterday while publishing a webzine,
and I wrote this to suggest a system that combines a webmail system and a guestbook system.
First, the biggest difference between a webmail system and a bulletin board (guestbook) system is that group sending is not supported.
Also, webmail has an inbox.
Currently, Gmail's motto is that there's no need to delete emails.
This essentially means that the boundary with a one-person bulletin board has become blurred.
Somehow, as in the content of the webzine I sent, the importance of email seems to have greatly declined.
Mini-homepages and blogs have filled that gap.
Therefore, I think it would be better to actively incorporate the advantages of email into blogs or mini-homepages.
PIMS systems like address books, social network management systems, group sending systems, reply systems.
In the case of Gmail, such attempts are clearly visible.
However, I still feel that the design doesn't quite suit Koreans.
How about a system where you send a one-person media email like Cyworld's Paper, and when others reply, their replies are attached below in a comment format,
and you can manage sent emails as a list and in an inbox?
In fact, to create such an environment, I believe Naver urgently needs to strengthen its PIMS system and communication.
Proposing to Cyworld, which has many systems in place, is faster, and Cyworld even acknowledged it as a good suggestion and gave me a prize,
but their attitude in responding and their business model, which leans too much towards a closed network,
strongly feels unsuitable for the next generation of the internet.

I actually don't know much about Naver.
This is because I was primarily a user who favored community-oriented SK Communications services.
However, with Web 2.0 discussions frequently appearing, I wonder if SK Communications, compared to Chotnun, Google, or Naver,
truly has a suitable system. I'm not sure if well-crafted advertising and marketing strategies can maintain dominance indefinitely without system reevaluation.
I'm not sure about that.
Sometimes, I think I should have delved into planning rather than development, even though I'm not particularly good at it.
But then I get scared thinking that if I can't even do this halfway, it's as hard to make a living as in development,
and I think it's overkill for someone who hasn't even reached a decent level in development to touch such things,
but I find it fun to try these things.
Just imagining various things and organizing the inconveniences and improvements of the programs I use.
The mobile browser currently under development is a closed system, making it difficult to identify improvements,
and first of all, the interface consumes very limited resources.
Thanks to this, when I look at areas like web or app development that consume large resources, I realize how infinitely vast they are. ^^

titleEn: It's Time to Gather Consumer Voices in Mobile Phone
contentEn:
My post on Media Daum Agora regarding the issue of youth phone bill suicides
 
-------------------------------------------------------
 
This might be an opinion that cuts into the company's profits, but
I'd like to say a word as well.

The first thing people misunderstand is that
Samsung Electronics, LG Electronics, and Pantech, which develop handsets, are companies unrelated to the profits of network operators like SKT, KTFT, and LGT.

You all know that SKT, KTFT, and LGT distribute handsets at prices lower than their actual selling price,
and essentially make up for the profit through rate plans and value-added services.

Therefore, you shouldn't be happy just because you bought a phone cheaply.
Perhaps our cheap purchase of that phone encouraged telecom operators to set such traps,
or rather, conversely, that might be the network operator's strategy.

Even we are surprised by the enormous packet fees when we test them ㅡㅡ;
When developing wireless internet related S/W, you can assume that almost no one uses it outside of a flat-rate plan.

Game downloads for 2000 or 3000 won are by no means expensive.
It's the data fee incurred when downloading a 512kb game that's enormous.
Most of that download fee goes to the network operator,
and only a portion goes to the game developer, mostly as information usage fees.

One of the factors hindering the development of wireless internet currently
is precisely these data fees.
However, paradoxically, these value-added services are also what grow the size of SKT, KTF, and LGT.
Profits from calls have decreased, while profits from value-added services have increased.

Lowering wireless internet fees is actually difficult.
It seems unlikely that such pressure would easily be applied to those large corporations.

Instead, you could demand that handset developers, who are unrelated to those profits,
include a function that allows users to estimate their packet usage fees.

This might be somewhat contrary to SKT, but
it's about siding with KTF in the next-generation wireless internet network battle between SKT and KTF, which will soon unfold in 2006.
(I am not a KTF associate)

SKT is launching WCDMA (HSDPA) and KTF is launching WiBro as their next-generation wireless internet. The big difference between these two technologies is that WCDMA, like existing wireless internet, is closed. It maintains the existing concept of download-type value-added services. It still gets about 512kb even when moving at 100km/h.
However, WiBro offers 1Mb at about 60km/h... and can reportedly be increased to 8Mb in the future.
While WCDMA is ahead in mobility, WiBro is ahead in speed,

And most importantly, it means laptops, PDAs, mobile phones, and all mobile devices will be compatible. Or, to be precise, WiBro will be IP-based, just like the internet. It's also an Intel standard, applicable to all existing Centrino laptops, and very cheap to install the network. Therefore, the unit cost is low, and wireless internet fees can be significantly reduced through flat-rate or partial flat-rate plans.

Of course, I saw the fees during KTF's WiBro tester program this time, and it was still too expensive to use with a laptop ㅡㅡ;
100MB for 10,000 won. 0.5GB for 20,000 won. 5GB for 50,000 won.
(Flat-rate plan still undecided - estimated to be set around 30,000 won)
However, compared to existing CDMA prices, it was incredibly cheap.

However, currently, there's only one WiBro handset model from Samsung,
and downloading a movie on a laptop would cause a huge problem ^^

But even if WCDMA prices were halved, it would only double the speed of existing services, with little tangible change for consumers. However, SKT will likely continue with its premium strategy.

Also, since WiBro is for 60km/h, I'm not sure how well it will work on the subway ㅡㅡ;
If it could reach 100km/h, it would be very useful...
For that, look at terrestrial DMB. It's scheduled to be available on subway lines in the Seoul metropolitan area starting in May.

There used to be something called City Phone. The problem with City Phone was that it disconnected at high speeds and couldn't hand off between base stations, but this was a problem that could have been solved within 1-2 years.
However, it seems the operators intentionally killed it to save PCS (in my opinion). If that technology had been the foundation, we might be using wireless internet at old landline phone rates now.

Somehow this turned into a WiBro promotion, but my point is, don't just fall for network operators' advertisements, don't fuss about "premium, premium," but consume based on actual technological possibilities, and

Demand that handset developers provide functions to inform you of packet fees or limit them.
Or demand the development of mobile phones suitable for children. Handset developers don't do it because it's not profitable. Actual market research results also show this.
If parents are truly interested in their children,
and there is organized action and purchase intent, why wouldn't handset developers make them?

Of course, one or two voices won't be enough.
Create a cafe, conduct surveys,
Well... the best thing would be to gather school parent associations, get signatures, and sound out their intention for group purchases,
and even try something like a phone designed by parents.

I think it would be good for handset developers, as it would be profitable and meet user needs.
With that much public opinion power, network operators wouldn't easily interfere,
and they might even differentiate themselves by making a student-exclusive WAP page the starting page.

As I wrote, it turned into an idea notebook ^^;

Implementation of AI..
I tried to organize my ideas a while ago.. In the past, AI aimed for integrated thinking abilities, but after many trials and errors, it is currently developing separately to require specialized thinking abilities like perception or mining. I don't know if these abilities will ever be fully integrated to produce something similar to AI,

but I've been thinking about approaching the modeling of primal unconsciousness and learning in a different way.

What I've considered is whether AI can truly emulate a child's learning method. Children learn through repetitive learning and empirical knowledge. This aspect can also be somewhat implemented in current AI. However, the difference lies in emotions and the unconscious. For example, a child who has had a drowning experience might come to dislike the color blue. Consequently, they might see another blue fruit and think of it as "something scary."

Clearly, this is an incorrect calculation. Because fruit is "not scary." However, this is a more emotional and metaphorical approach.

Based on the empirical knowledge of nearly drowning in the sea, the child made an inference in the form of: 'I dislike the sea,' and 'The sea is blue. Grapes are blue. Therefore, I dislike grapes.'

However, grapes don't actually only have the attribute of being blue. By assigning various attributes, entirely different conclusions can be drawn. And in reality, it's not that the child seriously thought about it as described above, but rather the "unconscious" part is significantly reacting.

So, what I focused on was not logical thinking, but the "unconscious." The "unconscious" has many illogical aspects. However, according to Freud, the unconscious is also composed of a significant amount of empirical knowledge, even if we are not aware of it, and by treating errors in this area, mental illnesses can be cured.

Therefore, to truly make AI human-like, it is necessary to create this "unconscious" and "dreams," which are the interaction between the unconscious and consciousness.

By defining each of the highly illogical ambiguities, such as defense mechanisms or the Oedipus complex, wouldn't it be possible to create an AI closer to humans?

Freud stated that everyone, unconsciously, possesses three personalities. A system that involves the individual processing for each of these personalities and the random conclusions derived from them. And finally, actions are taken after being ultimately reviewed by the ego, the results of those actions are fed back for computation, and this information can then update both the unconscious and conscious domains as empirical knowledge.

Anyway, I'm thinking about what if we model Freud's theory and apply it to AI. Wouldn't that alone have significant value? Like curing mental illnesses...

In my opinion, within 50 years, regardless of its internal algorithms, an AI will emerge that people will perceive as similar to humans. Wouldn't that be the greatest history of humankind? If so, what I want to try... --; perhaps it's a huge wish... 2005. 12. 22

I saw the strange bus designs Lee Myung-bak introduced. I really wanted to change them.
In Japan, there are even cute character buses...
And while looking at mini-hompies, it suddenly occurred to me, what if cars also had skins?
Instead of the traditional method of coating with paint,
if fluorescent pixels were applied to the car, then coated,
and the skin could be updated using a satellite or some network...

Of course, the unit cost would be incredibly high,
and currently, there's a technical problem of whether suitable pixels exist.
LCD panels are simply flat... and are light-emitting materials.

It should be a light-absorbing material, not light-emitting, and capable of displaying color.
If a light-absorbing material could display color, it would itself be a revolutionary item that could replace current LCDs or CRTs,
that much is clear, but

assuming there's a material still unsuitable for expressing fine details like a monitor,
applying it to a car wouldn't matter if it's much cruder.

Of course, the more precise it is, the prettier it would look up close.

What if this became a reality?
Like mini-hompies now, some company could advertise on cars,
and users could change their car's skin according to their preferences.

In fact, this would clearly be a revolutionary product not just for cars, but for the paint of all products.
I thought of cars first because they are incredibly expensive products,
and there are definitely buyers for even the most expensive cars.

So, if it's a car over 100 million won, wouldn't a 10 million won paint job be conceivable?
And considering that technology, as always, halves in price every few months,
the day will surely come when it's introduced to mass-market vehicles,
and when it becomes very cheap... on notebooks, pencil cases...

The day might come when you can apply famous artworks or your own custom skins, like Cyworld skins.
And ultimately, with light-absorbing screens instead of light-emitting ones, monitors could be viewed more
comfortably, and you could freely change the wallpaper in your home,
ushering in an era where art equals life.

Currently... Philips and others are already researching electronic paper,
and I've heard they've reached a considerable level.

What I'm saying, though posted on LIMITLESS, I guarantee will become a reality.
Ultimately, the businesses that will profit from this are...

Companies that make pixels,
Organizations that set standards for them,
Companies responsible for transmission media,
And people who create skin content.

Perhaps existing masterpieces, breaking free from the canvas, as digitized information,
will see their value increase even further?

First Written: 2004. 01. 13
=== Food Delivery Portal Site ===================================
1) Limitations of Current Delivery-Specialized Sites
  - Instant small-amount payment function via internet unavailable (card/mobile phone)
  - Menu search unavailable
  - Weak category-specific search function
  - Each franchise cannot manage menus and pages
  - Orderer and delivery address must match
2) Features of This Service
  - Search for deliverable businesses upon login or location input
  - Each franchise can manage its own page
  - Orderer can also have delivery sent to a different location
  - Businesses closed on holidays are not searchable
  - Keyword search available
  - Business owners with no computer knowledge can register and maintain
  - Instant small-amount payment function via internet
  
3) Target Audience
  - Franchises: Business owners who can use the internet / Business owners who cannot use the internet
  - Customers who want delivery
4) Services
  - Franchises:
    1) Franchise page hosting and agency: Assigning an independent URL like a community
        - Main page management, menu and price management, holiday management, customer management
 
    2) Delivery request inquiry and processing:
        - Direct request and management on the page / Can process order status and processing status
        - Notification via SMS
        - Customer management team notifies directly by phone
    3) Small-amount payment agency
        - Card and mobile phone payment (regular deposits into the franchise's account)
  - Customers:
    1) Search for restaurants by region, menu, and price
    2) Provide restaurant information and additional information for each region
    3) Allow customers to rate the food of franchises
    4) Logged-in customers: Personal information management and services based on preference analysis, reward points and discount benefits
       Non-logged-in customers: Can order food
    5) Purchase food and request delivery via internet small-amount payment (can also send gifts to others from a distance)
5) Scenarios
  ▶ Franchises:
    1) Mr. A, who can use a computer, decided to open a site.
    1.1) After searching, he learned about this service, applied, and upon logging in, was given a franchise page.
    1.2) He went to the franchise page, entered the franchise name and delivery phone number, and set the URL and category to input basic information.
    1.3) He decorated the franchise's Main Title using an HTML editor.
    1.4) He created a menu by entering records for menu names, prices, and descriptions.
    1.5) A delivery inquiry came in by phone from a customer who searched for the franchise.
    1.6) A delivery request message popped up on the computer. After a confirmation call, he went out for delivery.
    1.7) A delivery request message that was already paid for popped up on the computer. After a confirmation call, he went out for delivery.
    1.8) He received the delivery amount paid into his account from this service on a weekly or monthly basis.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    2) Mr. B, who can use a computer a little, decided to open a site.
    2.1) After searching, he learned about the service and called the site to request site hosting.
    2.2) A service staff member came, took photos of the business with a digital camera, noted down menu details, and the site was registered a few days later.
    1.5~1.8) Same as above
   -----------------------------------------------------------------------------        
    3) Mr. C, who has no computer knowledge, received a flyer and decided to open a site.
    3.1) He called the site to request site hosting.
    3.2) A service staff member came, took photos of the business with a digital camera, noted down menu details, and the site was registered a few days later.
 
    3.3) Delivery information was notified via SMS. After a confirmation call, he went out for delivery.
    1.8) Same as above
   -----------------------------------------------------------------------------        
    4) Mr. D, who is not at all tech-savvy, decided to open a site at the recommendation of a salesperson.
    3.2) Same as above
    4.2) The service side called the store to inform them of a delivery request. After confirmation, he went out for delivery.
    1.8) Same as above
  ▶ Customers:
    1) Customer A, lounging at home and wanting something to eat
         
    1.1) While searching, he found this site.
    1.2) He clicked on 'Region Search' and entered his current address, which brought up category-specific classifications.
    1.3) He wanted Chinese food. Click.
    1.4) A list of restaurants appeared.
    1.5) He looked at the phone number, called, and placed an order.
    1.6) He received the food and paid the delivery person.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------------------        
    2) Customer B, feeling hungry while working on the computer
    1.1~1.4) Same as above
    2.1) He clicked on a restaurant and selected a menu item.
    2.2) He clicked 'Delivery'.
    1.6) Same as above
    
   -----------------------------------------------------------------------------        
    3) Customer C, who heard his girlfriend was sick and wanted to buy her something delicious but was too far away
   
    3.1) As a member of this site, he logged in.
    3.2) He clicked 'Detailed Search' and selected his girlfriend's region and category.
    2.1~2.2) Same as above
    3.5) He entered his girlfriend's address.
    3.6) He processed the payment with a credit card.
    3.7) A month later, he was surprised looking at his credit card statement.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------------------        
    4) Elementary school student D, who is hungry
    3.1) Same as above
    1.2~1.4) Same as above
    4.1) He entered his mother's mobile phone number and resident registration number.
    4.2) An SMS authentication number arrived.
    4.3) Roughly shouting "Jjeul~", he entered the authentication number.
    4.4) The food arrived. He ate it deliciously.
6) Revenue Model
  ▶ Franchises:
    1) Initial Setup Fee: 1) Online Setup = 10,000 KRW
                     2) Offline Service Setup = 100,000 KRW
                        (Taking photos with a digital camera, uploading store introduction and menus)
    2) Membership Fee: 1) Basic = 20,000 KRW
                2) SMS Service + 5,000 KRW
                3) Phone Notification Service + 20,000 KRW
        * Pay-per-use: To be considered later
    3) Top Screen Banner Ad Revenue
7) Estimated Staffing (Including Temporary Positions)
 - Technical Staff (x3): Web Designer (1), ASP Programmer (2), DB Administrator, Franchise Registration 
 - Public Relations Dept (x2): Document Promotion, External PR, External Partnership
 - Sales Dept (x2): Customer Acquisition Promotion
 - Finance Staff (x1): Company Accounting Management
 - Customer Support Dept (x2): Consultation, Inquiries, Franchise Registration
8) Initial Promotion and Expected Progress
 - Initially, due to lack of recognition, we must work hard to gather OFF-line franchises and increase their numbers by offering free registration.
   Several months of free service (investment period)
 - Once on track with a large number of businesses secured, franchises are expected to increase naturally.
 - Enhance search functionality
 - Establish a community between customers and businesses
 - Dominate the nationwide small-scale distribution network.
 - Provide additional services to business owners

titleEn: Art Shop Specializing in Employment. Ideas/Patents
contentEn:
First written: 2003. 10. 24

Recently, I saw a newspaper article that began with the statement that what was predicted in Europe – that the cosmetics market would double when men started wearing makeup – is now coming true in Korea. The article then discussed men who groom themselves.

The advertisement for cover lotion, featuring Ahn Jung-hwan, was a huge hit, and the cover lotion achieved sales figures that even surprised the company.

Lookism is no longer just a women's issue.

Furthermore, in difficult times like these for finding a job, or when going on a "meeting" (like a blind date or group meeting), "first impressions" become an extremely important factor.

If there were a company or business that specialized in guiding and consulting on first impressions, wouldn't people open their wallets even in these difficult times... or rather, precisely because times are difficult?

The initial marketing could be positioned as a "job-specialized art shop" that provides guidance and management for the appearance of both men and women.

(For women, I think it would be a bit difficult due to the many existing shops. Therefore, the idea is to differentiate by focusing on men. Also, there are hardly any types of men's cosmetics. I believe the development of these cosmetics will also be a key factor.)

In the future...
No matter how much people say lookism is bad or whatever...
We won't be able to ignore the proportion that appearance occupies.
In fact, statistics show that men who are handsome and dress well have a much higher contract success rate.

In a capitalist society... as medicine and technology develop...
A world will come where faces and even bodies can be replaced.
I don't know if I'm getting too far ahead of myself, but given the speed of current technological development, I think it will happen before we die... --;

I believe the key to conquering that future market is not technology, but mindset.

First written: 2002. 04. 10
 
Login Management Homepage

0. Problem Statement
- People sign up for many websites, but often forget where they've registered.
And sometimes they even lose their passwords.
While there is software to solve this problem,
most of it cannot be installed outside of one's own computer.

1. Concept
- A website that directly manages login IDs on the web.
- Allows you to pass through all the places you use with a single ID.

2. General Features
1) First, log in to this website.
2) Available features
- Change/Withdraw personal information: Same as a typical website
- Home settings: Can be set as the web browser's homepage upon login.
- Edit Myfavorite
- Recommended sites
- Find where you've signed up
- Send/Receive mail

3) After logging in, a menu bar of approximately heigt*10 will be created at the top of the window.
Everything below will be used as a window. Think of it as a browser within a browser.
However, all information is stored encrypted on the server, not in the browser.

Menu Contents
- My Information:
1) Edit personal information

2) Show information about the sites I've used so far
You can see the flow. All this information is stored on the server and can be
used for CRM.

3) Mail settings (supports external mail to retrieve external mail / webzine subscription settings)

4) Find where you've signed up: This feature uses a robot based on your resident registration number to
browse websites and find sites you've signed up for. It takes
quite a long time for the results to appear.
(Technical issues are the biggest hurdle. --;)

- Current site address: The address of the currently used site is displayed.
- Display received mail: Clicking shows the mail list.
- Add to Favorites button: Adds to favorites. (Group management supported)
- Move Favorites: Frequently visited items move to the top for quick access.
- Auto-login settings:
Clicking moves to the login settings page.
A list of websites you've registered for appears.

- Auto-login / Auto-fill ID only / Do not enter anything (can be set per site)
- Recommended sites: Heavily promotional. However, it recommends sites suitable for the user
through CRM of my internet usage information.

3. Profitability
- Revenue generation using webzine services
- Advertising banners, recommended site registration

4. Problems: 1) How to extract ID and password when signing up or using during web surfing... Technical issue
2) Security issues of not leaving traces on the computer, protection against hacking
3) Finding where you've signed up: Technical difficulty...

titleEn: Relative Self-Assessment and Ideas/Patents for Meeting
contentEn:
First written: 2002. 04. 08

0. Problem Statement: Everyone wants to be evaluated, especially by the opposite sex.

1. Purpose: To allow users to receive scores or evaluations as a friend, boss, junior, or lover, and to understand their shortcomings. A community site, meeting arrangement service, psychological test, and aptitude test portal site.

2. Similar Sites: While there are sites where avatar information changes by purchasing certain items, there are no sites yet where one's status changes through tests or events.

5. Implementation: Users input basic information in various forms.
(Make it as detailed as possible. These parameters will be continuously updated as personal information.)
Appearance:
Education:
Etc...

Users assign scores they think they deserve.

Information is accumulated through various psychological tests and avatar games, and based on that information, users receive evaluations from others.

- Present a situation, divide actions into several options for users to choose from, and tally the results of those choices to give positive or negative scores for each tendency.

By having their own space, 0. Problem Statement [like http://cyworld.com)](http://cyworld.xn--com)-oz5qh30h/), they can receive evaluations from others and engage in community activities.

Users must obligatorily take a simple test or evaluate others every time they log in.

The names of those other people may not be disclosed.
Only situations are given, and scores are distributed through voting on those situations.

By continuously accumulating information, users can see scores, relative values, or percentages in various fields, much like a game character.

Based on the above information, a search service is provided where users can input their ideal type and find the most compatible person.

** The personal information collected above can also reveal more accurate consumer psychology, potentially leading to profitability.

I picked up my junior at Seoksu Station, my cousin in Gunpo, and then we headed to Hoengseong via the Yeongdong Expressway.

On the way, it took some time due to a car accident. It seemed like a pretty major accident, as several ambulances rushed forward, and when we passed the scene, there was a long stretch of debris, indicating its scale. I didn't see it, but my junior said there was a considerable amount of bloodstains.

Although I felt like I had seen a rather unsettling scene, once we exited the highway and entered a quiet national road in Gangwon-do, starlight began to pour down, so much so that it felt like it would spill into the car.

Even on the way, we turned off the car lights several times to marvel at the magical sight, gasping in awe.

As we drove, searching for the Astronomical Village, we encountered many rough roads. Since it was a sedan, it was naturally weak on unpaved roads. Bumping and rattling, we carefully drove up the winding unpaved mountain for a long time, only to find an even steeper downhill road at the summit.

We decided to go further and started descending... It was incredibly rough. Every time I heard stones scraping against the car's undercarriage, my father's face came to mind. ㅜㅡ

After descending for quite a while... I thought, 'Wait, this isn't right.' I stopped the car, my junior went ahead to check, and I turned the car around.

Just then, a Galloper Wagon came down from the opposite direction (I envy 4WD ㅜㅡ). My junior returned with the news that we had passed the Astronomical Village a long time ago, and with dumbfounded expressions, we climbed the mountain again.

Suddenly, I heard something continuously hitting the car, so I got out to check... The right front tire was flat... --; And this was in the middle of the mountain.

After making a mess of the trunk, I finally took out the spare tire and tools and began changing the wheel.
{{IMG:1}}

Why, of all days, were the lug nuts so stubborn, making it so difficult for me? Every time I kicked it, the joint that tightens the nuts kept slipping off... In the end, my junior and I combined our strength and loosened them with the power of two people. (If we had just turned it together, it would have come off so easily without even using our feet... ㅜㅡ)

It took a lot of effort, and my hands got completely dirty.

Perhaps because we had driven up and down the mountain more than expected, I checked the fuel and found there wasn't much left. 'I should have filled up beforehand... And there are no gas stations here...' I thought, along with...

I had a premonition that tonight would be tough. --;

Convinced that we couldn't find the Astronomical Village, we parked the car at the summit of the mountain, where a villa-like building and two cars were parked, and took out our telescope and other belongings.

Stepping out of the car, the pouring starlight... it was a magnificent sight.

Just as we gasped in awe for a moment, and before the car's hood had completely cooled down, a person came down from the villa in front of us.

We apologized, thinking we had been too loud, but he said no and asked where we were from. When we said Seoul, he asked about our respective schools, and we answered. Then, he kindly explained about the stars: Sirius, Orion, M45, Cassiopeia, centered around the Milky Way...

And then he revealed a fact: where we had parked was in front of the Central Astronomical Observatory... (Gasp. No wonder he knew so much...)

He seemed to be a professor. The professor invited us into the observatory. We thought we were incredibly lucky, and when we went up to the observatory, a student, who appeared to be his disciple, was observing stars with a laptop connected. We then heard various stories from the professor about astronomy and cameras.

A memorable piece of advice was that it's good to carry a sturdy, pipe-like tripod. He said that famous astronomers of the past, like Kepler, achieved great things by observing stars with much cruder telescopes, so we shouldn't just blame our equipment.

With a 50x magnification telescope, we saw Saturn's rings and even Jupiter's moons. The Earth's rotation speed was so fast that objects disappeared from the telescope after just a short moment. Meteor showers truly fell frequently. Sometimes, the long, clear trails they left behind were like paintings.

However... it was incredibly cold. My hands were freezing... it felt like mid-winter. We offered everyone the tea we brought, but the hot water we had was insufficient, and we brought cup noodles to eat but forgot the chopsticks... --;

{{IMG:2}}
Photo description: A 50x magnification telescope... With this, we saw Jupiter and its four moons, as well as Saturn with its rings. ^^ Orion's Belt is visible in the upper right.
{{IMG:3}}Photo description: This place is actually the Central Astronomical Observatory, located higher up, not the Astronomical Village. The brightest star is Jupiter. It's originally red... --; but it turned white in the photo.

Photo description: The tail of Ursa Major, the Big Dipper. That silhouette is me.

We took star photos like this and used my junior's PDA to find constellations...

Around 4 AM, it was so cold... and I had to drive tomorrow, so I went down to the car first, drank a can of beer, turned the heater on briefly then off (because I was low on gas --;), and curled up in the driver's seat to try and sleep.

Outside the car, starlight poured down...

My body was trembling from the cold, but I was immersed in a long, sad reverie. Outside the car window, the starlight seemed somehow melancholic... What a pathetic sight for a man, right? ^^ Haha. So, I grumbled and complained at my own ridiculousness, then tried to sleep.

I don't know when I fell asleep, but when I woke up, it was bright, and everyone else was sleeping in the car.

I started the car, even forgetting to say goodbye to the professor. My junior said it was okay because they had said their goodbyes, but after we left, it bothered me a little.

On the way, we saw the Astronomical Village in the middle. Since there were no lights at night, it wasn't strange that we couldn't find it. --;

With a very Korean feel and a landscape that seemed to stand between autumn and winter, I played some melancholic music and drove down the mountain. Scenery I hadn't seen at all during the night...

Seeing the beautiful mist over the flowing stream, my junior eventually asked me to stop and took a few photos.

{{IMG:4}}

Autumn leaves... and fields beautifully covered in frost. And the newly risen sunlight and mountain shadows. Clear, cold air that embraced us to the core. We left those behind and headed home.

{{IMG:5}}
{{IMG:6}}

After putting 40,000 won worth of gas in the car, we stopped at Anheung Steamed Bun Village on the way. While waiting for the steamed buns to cook, the grandmother at the bun shop told us to have some coffee from the water dispenser. Remembering the cup noodles we couldn't eat last night, we bought wooden chopsticks from the neighboring store, ate our cup noodles, and warmed ourselves by the cozy gas stove.

Then, we loaded a box of steamed buns each and ate a few on the way.

It really made me think, 'This is why people come all the way to Anheung for these steamed buns...' The taste was completely different from what I ate at home. Coincidentally, it was Anheung Steamed Bun Day, so instead of 20 buns for 5,000 won, we got 25 buns per box.

{{IMG:7}}

And on the way back. It was early morning, so the Yeongdong Expressway was clear, and I also liked the sunlight on the return journey. Everyone else was asleep, and I, listening to music alone, picked up a little speed. (Though I was a bit worried about the spare tire...) I felt like driving a bit faster. I drove a little quicker than usual, arriving in Seoul around 10 AM, dropped everyone off at their homes, and then returned to my own.

Then, fatigue washed over me, and I fell asleep as if collapsing. When I woke up again, it was already dark evening. An empty, dark house... I warmed up a few steamed buns and ate them, then cooked Jjapaghetti (I eat Jjapaghetti when I'm feeling down and alone. ^^), and now I'm sitting alone, writing this post.

Someday... I'd like to go back there again. Next time, I'll make sure to prepare a burner and plenty of fuel...

An anime featuring girls with pure, sad eyes carrying guns.

Like Matilda from Léon, I too often used the image of a girl with a gun – evoking contrasting images of corruption and innocence, warmth and violence – as a frequent subject for my drawings and writings.

At first, I started watching it, thinking it would just be an anime that moderately blended loli and military themes.
However, this anime was heavier than I expected.
Children abandoned for their own reasons were driven into situations where they had to commit murder, and girls whose bodies were replaced with machines and minds re-engineered were forced to live short lives. And the handlers who were in charge of these girls...
The human emotions that arise amidst all this.

It is sad enough to bring tears, yet also beautiful.
Even in the 13th and final episode, which ends with Beethoven's 9th Symphony, 'Ode to Joy,' no glimmer of hope was left for them.
They die... but they say they are not unhappy.
They say that if they are alive at this moment, have someone they love, and can protect that person, then they are happy.

Considering facts like an unloved child shooting her handler and committing suicide, the theme itself isn't very hopeful. Even the happiness of that unconditional, giving love is perhaps conditional on being loved in return.

Rather, the overall atmosphere of this anime lies in loneliness.
It stimulates a profoundly unrewarded, lonely emotion.

Furthermore, this already bittersweet anime...
The fact that it is, to some extent, a reality as far as I know, made my heart feel even more bitter.

Most people don't even try to know, but currently, approximately 300,000 children in 18 countries worldwide are being conscripted as child soldiers for combat purposes or as sexual targets.

In some ways, this anime is reality...

Should a good drama resemble reality...?
If so, then despite having an absurd sci-fi element like 'cybernetic bodies,' this anime is a good drama.

At first, when I saw the title of this anime, I thought it was 'Speaker' (스피커), so I wondered if it was 'Stereo'. ^^; But when I delved into it, I found out Spica is the name of a star, a binary star and the alpha star of the Virgo constellation. Because it's a binary star, it was also given the name 'Two' (두개의).

Anyway, I was very satisfied with the viewing experience.
Not long ago, I watched Planetes. If that was a story about adults looking at space, this one holds a more romantic... youthful hope.
Both of these anime tell the story of humanity's dream for the stars, and the individuals who achieve that dream.
Twin Spica is a coming-of-age story about Asumi, who lost her mother in the crash of Japan's Lion rocket, and dreams of becoming a rocket pilot.
Like Planetes, space is a lonely place.
It also rejects humanity's footsteps, and only special people can go there.

However... there is a dream there.
It says that this dream isn't a grand one for adults, but rather stems from the small wishes of children.
One of the overarching images in this anime is loneliness.
Asumi was a lonely child, but one with a dream, and she had friends who shared that same dream. Thus, it delivers the message that dreams can be achieved.

Honestly, I wasn't entirely happy with the ending.
Was there really a need to show the children's appearances...?
Are adults not allowed to have that dream...?

Rather, my favorite dialogue was with Mr. Sano in episode 14.
Perhaps it's because I'm an adult.

Asumi: Mr. Sano! It's the same, isn't it? You're the same, aren't you? What we were seeing was the same, wasn't it?

Sano: Indeed, I had a time like that too. But when I suddenly realized it, it was already out of sight. Don't you lose it!

Asumi: Why? Why do all adults make such sad faces? Ms. Suzunari, Mr. Lion, Dad, Mr. Sano... It would be great if we could all go to space together...

Sano: I'll see it too, definitely. I'll see it again. Definitely, definitely...

The animation's art style didn't quite appeal to me at first, but the more I watched, the more I was drawn in.

In this 24-episode animation, its low budget is clearly visible.
From beginning to end, the setting is a small radio studio.
The cast consists only of a few staff members and occasional guests.

It's the near future of 2010, yet strangely, androids appear.
Other than that, it's a radio studio no different from the present.
It's a story about human relationships unfolding within it.

The radio show primarily offers life advice. Radio is definitely less popular than TV.
But even a very small number of people listen to the broadcast and speak their truth.
The idea of one's voice being conveyed to someone else.
That is the charm and nostalgia of radio.

And into this, the alien, high-tech mechanism of an android was added.
With an android stepping in as a personality (announcer) who conveys people's hearts,
it was perhaps expected to be a predictable story.
A story where a robot becomes like a human and delivers a certain kind of emotion.

However, watching it made me feel many things.
In episode 23, a perfect robot appears. Something perfect cannot move a person's heart.
No... a person's heart is not perfect to begin with.

The story Maiko wants to convey is precisely that.
Because they are imperfect, people make mistakes and hurt each other,
but if they honestly try their best and work hard, they can overcome it.

And it talks about how what's needed to live is passion... and the people by your side.

Keep fighting, keep fighting, keep fighting! ^^

-Episode 1 <OSIRIS> -

This anime, titled "The Last Flight of the Osiris," immediately shows that the Final Fantasy team's technology has significantly improved.
It seems this team has finally started to grasp how to convey expressions and emotions.
The previous Final Fantasy had excellent graphics, but it failed in its cartoon-like storytelling method.
Episode 1 is the most "Matrix-like" of them all, so there isn't much to evaluate here. Perhaps it serves as preliminary knowledge for watching "Matrix Reloaded."
There were some scenes that reminded me of "Ghost in the Shell," but
their physiques were truly impressive ㅠㅠ

-Episode 2, 3 <SECOND RENAISSANCE 1.2>

This work contains the most biblical and mythological elements, and it helps to understand the Matrix worldview.
What I particularly noted was the difference between Episode 2 and Episode 3.
The machines depicted in Episode 2 have a warm feel, reminiscent of Astro Boy's machines.
However, the design of the machines in Episode 3 completely changes.
Overall, they appear with a design that is completely contrasted with the previous episode, giving off a scary, cold feeling.
Scenes like soldiers praying, or someone pulling a TV showing a sermon through a crowd, and battle scenes reminiscent of Armageddon. Even the CG woman who initially appears to introduce history looks like Guanyin from Buddhism.
I think this is the work that most heavily deals with religious issues.

-Episode 4 <KID'S STORY>

First, the art style in this story is very unique.
Especially in the chase scene on the skateboard, that art style shines even brighter.
Also, the process starting with a fall and connecting to the final scene was very impressive.
And it seems he appears as the kid who follows Neo in "Matrix Reloaded."
He says the same line: "I didn't save you, you saved yourself."

-Episode 5 <PROGRAM>

First, the art style is traditional Japanese... The background and atmosphere alone are roughly magnificent.
The content is extremely personal, so I recommend watching it yourself.

-Episode 6 <WORLD RECORD>

Extremely exaggerated movements, composition, and unique camera shots.
And the dialogue, almost like listening to rap, allowed me to feel that "black" flavor.
This work best utilized the element of exaggeration in animation.

-Episode 7 <BEYOND>

An anime where you can fully experience the meticulous detail of traditional Japanese cel animation.
The concept itself is fresh: a glitch within the Matrix.
And the way that glitch is expressed created an almost mystical atmosphere.

-Episode 8 <DETECTIVE STORY>

I'm usually weak for this kind of hardboiled atmosphere,
so of course, I couldn't help but like it. Ash is the best!
It interpreted the Matrix through the mysterious elements of a detective story.
And what's noteworthy here are Ash's computer designs.
For a moment, I couldn't help but think of Mamoru Oshii's "Avalon."
As you know, the world within the Matrix was identical to the real world.
However, the computers here, regardless of their performance, exude a strong mechanical scent to emphasize the hardboiled atmosphere. But given that GUI and networking are standard, their performance is not ordinary.

-Episode 9 <MATRICULATED>

The moment I saw it, I couldn't help but think of Peter Chung.
Turns out it was Peter Chung. --;
As someone who doesn't particularly like overly glossy CG, I was a bit dissatisfied, but
the subject matter was good.
The ending seemed to show the robot waiting to capture other robots (my arbitrary interpretation).
Because the composition is identical to the opening scene where the woman waits for the robot.
Anyway, even the robot here realizes what it means to be with another person or another being.

- ps. Overall, Animatrix was fresh.
No, it was better than the movies. Because different directors reinterpreted the same worldview in different ways
and presented different themes.
And the feeling of the themes being condensed to express their ideas in a short time was good.

{{IMG:1}}

Spirited Away is indeed directed by Hayao Miyazaki.
I thought it was by a different, new director...
Toshio Suzuki is listed as producer. I thought it was his work...

Anyway, I'll write down my thoughts.
---------------------------------------
First, I couldn't help but be amazed once again by the imagination of the Studio Ghibli team.
Among them, there are many things that seem to have been made with the character market in mind... --;
Anyway, they're cute, so let's move on.

I felt that the subject matter was quite different from Ghibli's previous works.
If previous works were animations with somewhat artificial fairytale elements,
this one had elements of orally transmitted "folktales."
The gods (deer gods) that appeared briefly in Princess Mononoke appear concretely in this animation.
The place where Sen is trapped is a hot spring resort for gods.

To put the folktale elements simply...
Harsh trials -> Good deeds -> Help -> Trials -> Overcoming with courage and wisdom -> Happy ending
Would you say it's roughly this kind of structure?
Therefore, it's also true that it contains elements of growth.

The art and imagination are Studio Ghibli's, so it's fine to consider them outside the discussion.
No matter how much I praise it... it won't be as good as seeing it once for yourself...

My thought is that the theme hasn't changed much from the past. --;
Sen's parents, upon arriving in the land of the gods, recognize it as the remnants of theme parks that sprang up like mushrooms during the bubble economy era and then disappeared.
And there, Sen meets the gods.
Most of these gods often take the form of traditional Japanese deities,
but most are in animal forms: "frogs, spiders, catfish, birds" – the forms of gods leaving us due to development.
The 'stink spirit' that Sen saved was also the master of a famous river.
Various kinds of trash poured out of his body, and it was Sen, one of the humans who had polluted him, who pulled them out.

Haku tells Sen not to forget her name.
I think this line is the theme.
A name represents oneself. It contains everything: where one came from, what one does, how one lived...
Haku was also the spirit of a river. But it was filled in due to apartment development...
Chihiro had almost drowned there as a child but was saved by Haku's help.
That's why Haku knew Chihiro's name, and Chihiro remembers and tells Haku his name.
That name is the name of a river that no longer exists.
Many things have disappeared under the guise of "development." These names are among them.

However, it gives hope that they can meet again in the end.
In fact, this is possible through Chihiro's will.
Restoring the covered river, just like with the stink spirit, is the responsibility of humans like Chihiro.

I believe the theme of this story is to find the "names" of lost things.
Only then can we find our own "names." Isn't that the meaning?

The scenery of the train running through the clear water and the lights passing by outside the window as it gets dark.
I also thought that perhaps this isn't so different from the scenery we see when we ride a train at night.

In fact, it seems many aspects were focused on children.
There were quite a few elements of poetic justice (good deeds bring good fortune), and plenty of visual spectacles.
The story of the marginalized, faceless spirit, the story of Granny Yubaba.
Anyway, the quite long runtime was never boring.

Ghibli was amazing once again. ㅠㅠ

2002. 07. 03

{{IMG:1}}
Although I watched it alone, sitting in a corner, somewhat alleviating my loneliness...
I still think it was a good decision to watch it.
The animation... goes without saying. For me, who really wanted to see Studio Ghibli's visuals on the big screen... it couldn't have been more wonderful. However, compared to more recent works like Princess Mononoke, I do feel it falls a bit short.
This film, which firmly established Director Miyazaki's position, makes me unsure where to even begin talking about it.
Actually, I own this movie on video. And is this about the third time I'm watching it?
However, that was when I first started watching Studio Ghibli's works.
But today, having watched all of Ghibli's past works and then re-watching Totoro, it felt a bit different.
First, regarding the theme of 'nostalgia'... the media and many people talk about nostalgia in relation to Totoro.
Listing the good things from that era...
But while watching this film, why did "Grave of the Fireflies" and "Pom Poko" (Heisei Tanuki Gassen Ponpoko) from Studio Ghibli's works come to mind?
Comparing Totoro with the two films above, Totoro presents childlike imagination...
Grave of the Fireflies depicts an extremely realistic portrayal of its era...
And Pom Poko sadly tells the story of Japanese society, which has rushed breathlessly from the past to the present.
At first, I thought of these films separately.
However, this time while watching the film, I tried to arrange them chronologically.
First, "Grave of the Fireflies" is a story about children during and immediately after World War II.
It's the story of a brother and sister who lost their parents, and although they eventually died amidst desolation and indifference, the innocent smile of the younger sister never easily left my heart. The ending was also a bit tragic. Because both children died...
Next is "My Neighbor Totoro," set in the period after World War II, when Japan was just about to achieve economic recovery. Around the time when telephones reached the countryside, utility poles were erected, and forests began to be cut down.
Finally, "Pom Poko." Japan succeeded in industrialization and achieved economic prosperity. However, within that, the individual was buried, nature disappeared, and ultimately, only busy city dwellers remained, with no leisure to be found. And animals pushed into restricted areas, and marginalized groups of people.
I placed these on a continuum.
If the children in "Grave of the Fireflies" hadn't died and had participated in Japan's history, they might have become the father in Totoro. And Totoro is set in a time when Japan had just begun its recovery, but still... remnants of hunger remained.
As evidence, the patched clothes worn by the boy in Totoro, and the torn umbrella. For Ghibli, which never misses trivial everyday details, this reflects the appearance of that era to some extent. However, a somewhat more relaxed life means that a time had begun when children's hunger was somewhat alleviated. We also had a similar film. Was it "A Beautiful Time"? Clearly, the history of that era, objectively speaking, was a difficult time. And in "Pom Poko," which is on that continuum, it ultimately talks about what was lost despite achieving economic prosperity.
The scene where Totoro grows a seed into a giant tree... The scene in Pom Poko where the tanuki show people visions of their hometown with magic... Isn't this overlap in that context?
Being from the city myself, I actually don't know that kind of life.
However, a longing for the land is something every earthling possesses.
They said something similar in Laputa: "You can't live if your feet aren't on the ground." (Is that right?)
Totoro might end as just a dream and curiosity for children,
but I think it's also a meaningful fairy tale for adults in its own way.
No, in fact, this film holds even more meaning for adults.
Moreover, it holds even greater significance for Koreans, who share a modern history almost like twins.

What, indeed, will we leave for our children?
I once felt that Miyazaki, compared to Takahata, was "someone who turns away from reality," but now I wonder if I might have misunderstood.
I'll just quote a part of Hayao Miyazaki's interview, excerpted from the Chosun Ilbo email club, and finish here. I've also become confused about what's what. Because I'm writing without organizing my thoughts...

" 'I wanted children to think, 'It was good to be born.' In that case, the words I can offer would be, 'Live well.' Even if you're unlucky and meet bad people and suffer, there are definitely joyful things in life.' "

Totoro is a film with much to see and much to say...
Watching this made me want to watch other works again.
When will "Spirited Away" be released? --

#### [50 First Kisses](http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/review.nhn?code=38227)

Director Peter Segal
Production 2004 USA, 0 min
**Rating**

I had been seeing ads on the subway for quite a while, saying "50 First Kisses?? Please, let's move things along!"
I don't usually watch romantic comedies.
This time, I got a preview screening ticket because a friend couldn't make it due to circumstances.
But of course, some days just go wrong... I ended up being late because I took the wrong subway twice.
I was able to go in and watch it, but I couldn't check attendance ㅜㅡ
Anyway, I watched it almost from the beginning.

Overall, the movie was fun.
No, rather, although I don't watch many romantic comedies,
I think it was the best among the romantic comedies I've seen recently.

It's a story about a playboy who falls in love with a woman who forgets everything after a day.
Short-term memory loss... Watching this movie, two other films came to mind.
The first was 'Groundhog Day,' about a man who lives the same day over and over.
I remember watching 'Groundhog Day' on 'Weekend Masterpiece' (a TV program).
It was one of the most memorable romantic comedies I've seen in my life.
It was almost as if this movie was an homage to 'Groundhog Day.'

The other was 'Memento,' which also depicted a man suffering from short-term memory loss.
However, as the genres are different, the perspectives of the two films are completely different.

In 'Groundhog Day,' the protagonist is given the same day over and over again from a certain point.
He knows everything that will happen around him.
The identical situation given each day gave him many choices.
He enjoyed himself... and also did bad things...
Eventually, he fell into a sense of powerlessness within the cycle of the same day,
and ultimately found joy by doing the best things possible for one day with that ability.
Then, within that frozen day, he eventually discovers true love,
and though he's sad that his love will reset tomorrow, he falls asleep happy.
And the magic spell on him is broken,
and he gets to experience the next day, the future, with the person he loves.

This movie also presents the same day. But this time, conversely, it's only for Lucy.
The protagonist's and the surroundings' time flows, but the time of the woman he loves does not.
Ultimately, he can try the same things with her every day. This point is identical to 'Groundhog Day.'
However, unlike 'Groundhog Day,' in this movie, time actually flows, and only Lucy's time does not.
And the clue that allowed them to escape this cycle of time was, in both cases, the keyword 'love.'

A woman who starts a new love every day, even though it's the same.
Perhaps this is the love all couples dream of. To always keep that feeling from when it first began,
to cherish it forever, is perhaps what everyone dreams of,
and this movie brings that fantasy into reality by borrowing the concept of a 'disease.'

Then, let's compare it to 'Memento,' the second movie that came to mind.
'Memento' also deals with short-term memory loss. However, it's a very bleak story.
He goes around seeking revenge every day... tattooing his body and making notes to live his day.
The point that 'records' are used as a means of memory is the same as in this movie.
However, the underlying aspect of this movie is quite similar yet different.
In 'Memento,' there was also a beloved wife. Her death...
The wife committed suicide by using him. The devoted wife,
unable to bear her continuous illness, chose death. And his life crumbled.

It's the same illness... There was a loved one in both.
So what is the extreme difference between these two films?
It's the presence of a loving family... and a consistently loving partner.
And above all, one is reality and the other is fantasy.
The reality of short-term memory loss is much closer to 'Memento.'
Even with the same subject matter, such different imaginations are possible.

Rather, the fact that memories are completely reset to before the illness, is much more similar to 'Groundhog Day.'
Therefore, this movie is definitely a fantasy.
Simply put, this movie is
a romantic comedy that uses short-term memory loss as a fantastical device to talk about the theme of love,
blending in comedic elements and even cute animals...
It was a pleasant and enjoyable romantic comedy.

Love, perhaps, is a fantasy, just like in this movie.
Falling in love in just one day... accepting any unbelievable fantasy...
Perhaps that's what this movie is trying to say.
Memories are certainly important... losing them, whether painful or good, is losing something precious.
But this movie never lets go of one thread: the message of 'love' imprinted on the other side of the brain.
That's why, one day, a strange man appears, shows her a diary, and says, 'You are my person,'
opening up a new life for her every single day.
Love is such a fantasy, and it speaks of pursuing such a thing.

All of us, amidst our repetitive, mundane daily lives,
hope that someone else will open up a new life for us, different from the old, a life that makes our hearts flutter like first love,
living each day with a little bit of expectation.

ps. Not to nitpick the title, but they progressed beyond the first kiss on the 26th time, not the 50th ㅡㅡ;

#### [Taegukgi: Brotherhood of War](http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/review.nhn?code=36666)

Director Kang Je-gyu
Production 2003 South Korea, 0 min
**Rating**

I kept wanting to see Taegukgi: Brotherhood of War... kept wanting to, until my friend and I went to see it at a morning matinee.

Personally, it was a movie I had been waiting for.
It's been over 10 years since I started waiting for a film that properly covered the Korean War.
As someone who loves war stories, I wondered why, with so many good films about WWII and the Vietnam War, no one dared to touch the story of this land, where countless American soldiers and our grandfathers died over nearly three years?

I've been curious and thinking about this for a long time.

Perhaps... there were people who tried.
But due to Korea's unique circumstances, they might not have been released...
or perhaps, dealing with Korean stories clumsily was a very sensitive issue for a currently divided Korea.
Especially during the US-Soviet Cold War era.

Then I heard that Kang Je-gyu was making a full-fledged film about the Korean War.
People were also saying the battle scenes were amazing.
Jang Dong-gun, who showed great acting in 'The Coast Guard,' was also in it.
The one thing that made me a bit uneasy was that it was directed by Kang Je-gyu, who made 'Shiri.'
I found 'Shiri' entertaining enough, but somehow, its impact didn't last long afterward...
He certainly showed a new side and a new beginning for Korean cinema, but I wondered if he was the right person to handle such a sensitive and heavy story.

The conclusion is...

I can't easily evaluate it.

Rather, the special effects and battle scenes that people praised didn't really catch my eye.
It was just what I'd seen in Hollywood... I just saw it again.
And honestly, compared to battles like in 'Band of Brothers,'...
why were all the battles close-quarters combat?

Wow... you run forward and it's enemy territory. ㅡㅡ;
Have they ever done individual combat training?? How hard it is to run up a mountain...
Why couldn't those US Marines who fell countless times in Normandy do that?
It was incredible.
Every guy shooting artillery must be a sharpshooter, dropping shells only inside the trenches.
Thanks to that, digging trenches was useless.

Jang Dong-gun... why was he so good at solo combat?
I thought I was watching Oh Hye-sung from 'Nambul'.

People flying through the air and blood splattering was something I'd always seen, so I just took it as it was.

What moved me, rather, was the background.

Seoul in the 1950s.
When Won Bin was whining to Jang Dong-gun in that annoying, childish voice, the background behind them... that atmosphere...

It was truly magnificent. Seoul, revitalized after liberation...
(Well, there were many bloody incidents due to the trusteeship issue...
but by '50, it was starting to normalize.)
And the refugees. Our grandfathers and grandmothers...
people scrambling to get on trains.
Destroyed Seoul.
When the camera briefly showed the destroyed Seoul from above...

I thought, 'That's Jung-gu. That's Yongsan... Where would my house be?'
Just the fact that the ruins on screen were the very land I live on was enough to move me.

Jang Dong-gun said, "Hold the children's hands tightly!"
Just thinking about the implications of that statement made me choke up.

I recalled scenes of countless separated families reuniting on TV, embracing and weeping after 50 years apart.

"During the Japanese occupation, at least we fought to protect our country. This time, what the hell are brothers doing fighting each other!"
A war without purpose... a war with nothing to protect...
that was the reality of the Korean War.

Massacres of civilians... and people branded as communists and driven to their deaths.
I was taught that soldiers exist to protect the people.
I served in the military with family photos on my locker.

But it became a war where it was unclear which side's citizens to protect...
Ultimately, it was an abnormal war that only deepened the emotional wounds and animosity between people who had killed each other's families.

For Koreans, war, for generations, was about protecting family.
But this was a fight that began with them hurting each other...
not knowing whom to protect... even destroying what they were supposed to protect.
That's why the war could only drive someone like Jang Dong-gun mad.
His madness wasn't simply due to an excessive adrenaline rush from war.
The catalyst that broke his human limits was the loss of his family, represented by his younger brother.
And that was what the Korean War meant to us.

When I was in the military, I once read a novel called 'Defcon.'
It depicted a nuclear attack on Seoul by Chinese forces...
and then the perspective shifts to Korean troops on an expedition in Manchuria.
They massacre Chinese prisoners... When an officer tries to stop them...
someone says, "Leave them be. Those bastards are all from Seoul."
And so, he couldn't stop them.

If they were Westerners... or a third party, they wouldn't understand.
But I almost cried at that scene.
I was almost a sergeant or corporal at the time...

If Seoul had been hit by a nuclear attack, and my home...
my mother... my father... my siblings were all gone...
if I had heard such news...
I would definitely have pulled the trigger without hesitation, even if a Chinese person begged for their life right in front of me.
I felt like it wouldn't matter if their brains splattered on my face, or if I became a demon killing hundreds... thousands.

Perhaps... all Koreans are like this.
I heard this movie is going abroad.
I wonder... how much will they truly understand?

Will those who film videos of families gathered to cut birthday cakes, proclaiming 'this is a beautiful family,' and climb buildings pretending to be heroes, understand the fierce, almost maddening, family love of our people?
Will those who tried to imprison a Korean mother who cried and screamed 'it's my fault' after her daughter died in an accident, understand the deeper meaning of this film?

Of course, American soldiers don't appear much in this film...
just a very small amount. I know that 11 nations participated and a tremendous number of American soldiers fought and died for us.
But they probably won't even imagine why they had to fight on this land, or why this land was so arbitrarily divided by ideologies, creating this tragedy.

Amidst all this, countless families were separated...
young people fought on the front lines...
and those who survived fought their own miserable battles of survival.

Even after the Korean War ended, the ideological war did not.
Jeju Island... the partisans... and those who suffered as criminals under the guilt-by-association system.
Silmido might even be a sequel to this film...
or a side story.

And now we are living that sequel on this divided Korean Peninsula.
Even in politics, people still can't distinguish between red and blue.
For 50 years, we've had military forces comparable to a giant like India, with 700,000 troops in the South alone within 24 hours.
Including reserve forces, the North and South combined could mobilize over 10 million troops within a month, making us a military nation.

Somehow...
I empathize too much with this film.
It's not because the movie's spectacle is flashy.

I laughed watching how a Mustang hit by anti-aircraft fire fell onto the very anti-aircraft gun that shot it.

But I empathized because I know the guns they held.
I've touched a Carbine rifle like the one Jang Dong-gun held.
I know the heavy feel of that rough wooden gun.

Just as the low-rise buildings of Seoul in the 1950s have now been replaced by complex, tall skyscrapers,
the Carbines they held became K2s... M16s...
M1 tanks became K1s... The firepower and might only grew stronger.
Even if Sol cigarettes became 'This'... steel helmets became ballistic helmets...
military uniforms changed to camouflage...
and the period of military service was slightly reduced to two years...

The fact that this land remains a divided nation is unchanged, and the fact that most units near the DMZ would be wiped out within minutes if war broke out is also unchanged.

This movie was sad.
Regardless of its plot... the fact that it's reality...
that always made me sad and left a lump in my throat.
Whenever my grandmother talks about the North Korean soldiers, she always says,
"Do you know how cruel those bastards are?"
And she talks as if they should all be caught and killed like rats... as if they're not human.

Clearly, living on Korean soil, I understand that deep-seated resentment very well.
But I can't get angry with her. Rather, her words just sound more painful to me.

On the contrary, the reality of security education these days is truly pathetic.
The era of unconditionally branding North Korea as communists was pathetic, but now people think soldiers are uncool...
everyone tries to find some ailment to get a military exemption.

Ghost in the Shell Stand Alone Complex

This anime, produced with a total of 26 episodes, was brought into Korea on DVD.
While seemingly alleviating some of the complexity of the previous theatrical film,
it actually poses even more serious philosophical questions about existence.
The actions of the Tachikomas (multi-legged tanks) in episode 25 and the existence of the Laughing Man,
What is the meaning of an individual in a complex net (society)?

I cannot easily speak about the theme.
When something is parallelized, the meaning of the individual (existence) is lost.
Even if the original existence disappears, through parallelization,
other copies can impersonate the original.
This anime defines this as a Stand Alone Complex.

We are actually experiencing such phenomena.
We gain indirect experience through TV or broadcast media and come to have the same emotions.
However, if this were the future society, directly connected to our brains like the Matrix,
and all experiences were shared...?

So, if we could truly experience that drama?
Would people still have individuality or the meaning of "existence"?
This anime draws such a serious conclusion.

This seriously addresses the problem of modern society where humans, by becoming parallelized,
rather lose their existence.

However, from the beginning, Ghost in the Shell also approaches it from the opposite side.
The parallelization of machines acquires humanity (individuality), or rather, a ghost.

And this anime offers "curiosity" as a challenge,
a kind of answer.

This anime is actually serious.
It might just seem like entertainment for those who enjoy mysteries, with its complex action scenes and intertwined events,
but it's more than that.

The seriousness of this anime lies in its possibilities.

From the perspective of someone majoring in IT,
I can assert that this writer is a futurist like Alvin Toffler.
Of course, many parts seem exaggerated for dramatic effect.
However, this is the direction current technology is pursuing.
The pursuit of convenience and high efficiency actually leads to such a future.
This can be anticipated.
The future this anime speaks of is neither a dystopia nor a paradise.
It is a cold reality. And that future holds many problems and conveniences that we can or cannot anticipate,
and it foresees a society that can bring confusion to many existing values.

This anime might even be a story about human evolution.
However, it depicts many phenomena that arise as humans, borrowing the power of machines and high-speed networks,
exponentially increase their knowledge.

And the fact that this anime is based on current, predictable technology and theories
makes it even more persuasive than Darwin's theory of evolution.

If you want to glimpse the future, I highly recommend this anime.
If you like serious topics, it's also highly recommended.
It's also recommended for those who enjoy atmospheric works.

However, it is absolutely not recommended for those who dislike thinking and only watch light, entertaining things.

I watched Wonderful Days, which I had been looking forward to for a long time.
First of all, I was surprised that Korean animation had developed so much.

Technically, there was almost nothing that fell short when compared to existing world-class animation.
Compared to the slightly disharmonious 2D and 3D shown in Japan's Blue Submarine No. 6, Korea's Wonderful Days even achieved an excellent harmony of 2D and 3D.
Each scene was truly amazing.
The direction was also not lacking.
It felt like watching a commercial.

However... if there's anything regrettable,
the story didn't come together as one.
The plot was, of course, just so-so...
It was a predictable story, nothing extraordinary.
But how you develop a predictable story makes all the difference.
Even predictable fantasy or sci-fi can immerse the audience depending on the director's ability.

The most regrettable thing was this level of immersion.
It was unskilled in controlling the audience's emotions.
In each scene, the music and visuals conveyed emotions sufficiently, but
it failed to gather the audience's emotions before that scene appeared.
Perhaps the scenes felt a bit sudden?
They were excellent scenes, but the audience wasn't prepared for them beforehand.
Why did it come to this situation...?
What emotions were flowing between the characters...?
These things just felt superficial.

First of all, Wonderful Days is an excellent animation.
The scenes were not inferior when compared to any foreign animation released in Korea so far.

Mechanics and background design,
colors, composition, various sound effects, camera shots, characters' gazes, movements
everything was good.
Rather, it skillfully blended the powerful American-style exaggeration not felt in Japanese anime with a Korean style, bringing the movements to life.
Not directly casting celebrities as voice actors, in the American style, was also a good decision, unlike previous productions.

Whether it was a consideration for children, or if they still consider animation a children's business, given the appearance of animals suitable for merchandise and children whose roles were unclear and who actually disrupted the flow of the story, I'm not sure.

In any case, I was truly pleased that Korean animation has come this far.
Now, just like in Korean cinema, we just need great directors to emerge in the animation industry.
Because the technology has already proven to be sufficient.

I hope Wonderful Days can somewhat alleviate the regret of Oseam having quietly faded away.

Since this animation couldn't be a perfect one, whether it will succeed at the box office is honestly uncertain.
However, I think it's amazing that it achieved this much in Korea, a country with a weak foundation from the start.

Those who love Korean animation, please go watch it in theaters.

This film is about a little boy named Masao who embarks on a journey with a gangster named Kikujiro to find his mother.

In "3000 Leagues in Search of Mother," it's a story about Marco's growth during his journey to find his mother.
