However, during their journey, the two learned how to care for each other, and Kikujiro also saw the lost innocence of the people they met along the way.

Roughly, this seems to be the central plot.
The visuals are beautifully rendered, like an advertisement or a painting, and perhaps because it's told from a child's perspective, it seems to view everything with a warm gaze, without questioning things that might not make logical sense.

First, the way to enjoy this movie seems to be this:
Don't raise objections. If you do, there will be no end to them.

This film feels quite enjoyable when viewed from a child's perspective.
While the Korean film "The Way Home" beautifully depicted a child's perspective and the friendship between a grandmother and child within the confines of reality, "Kikujiro" presents a somewhat exaggerated child's perspective.

After laughing and feeling excited for a long time after watching *Jail Breakers*,
I took a 10-minute break and immediately went to see *The Coast Guard*.
The realistic training scenes of the Marines in the beginning reminded me of *Shiri*,
but knowing that it wasn't a story from a distant land like *Shiri*, but actual training of our own Marine soldiers,
made it even more interesting.
(Though I'm not sure why the Marines were using M16s...)

Simply put, this movie can be summarized as a story about an overzealous private who mistakenly kills a civilian, goes crazy, and acts out.
Those reading this don't need to get angry that I've revealed the plot in advance. This plot is merely a superficial scratching of the surface, less than 1/10th of the movie's atmosphere and the true hidden content. If anyone says they found this movie, about a crazy person acting out, boring for over an hour, then they've completely missed the point of the film. --;
There are absolutely no North Korean soldiers in this movie!
However, in my opinion, even without North Korean soldiers, it more realistically alludes to the inter-Korean division.

My heart felt heavy throughout this movie.
The weight of it made me feel so tormented and unjustly treated that I thought I would die.
And I once again felt despair that what was shown to us in the film was not fiction but reality.
Many foreigners must have watched it at the Busan International Film Festival, but I wonder if they felt the same way I did.

This movie touched a raw nerve in us, the civilians who live forgetting about war and division—no, who forget and, because it's bothersome, keep postponing a solution to the pain of our Republic of Korea.
Why do we really maintain this divided state?

Why can't we trust each other like that?
In the end, I couldn't bear how pitiful everyone was: Private Kang, who shot the civilian; Young-gil, who was shot and died; Mi-young, who went crazy because of it; and even the soldiers who assaulted Mi-young.

After watching this movie,
I thought that perhaps we truly live in a crazy country.

If *JSA* depicted the divided situation beautifully and hopefully,
this movie portrays Korea's divided situation in a truly horrific way.
It depicted the pain of a torn-apart nation so vividly that my heart ached.

If you are Korean, you will definitely not feel at ease after watching this movie.
You will feel like you've come out with a heavy burden.
Perhaps it's like the original sin of Koreans in a divided nation, similar to the soldiers who assaulted Mi-young and forced her to abort her child.

After laughing for a long time watching *Jail Breakers*,
after watching *The Coast Guard*, I felt so unjustly treated that I wanted to cry.
I was too embarrassed to show tears, so I just wiped them away, but I wanted to go to the restroom and sob loudly.

Anyway, I could confidently say that the two films I watched today were truly excellent,
and I was happy that Korean cinema had developed to the point of making me laugh and cry like this.

- Oasis - 

Despite not really liking to watch romance films in theaters, I ended up seeing this movie based on recommendations from the radio and my friends. Actually, it premiered today. ^^

Anyway, the feeling was wonderful. It was truly a pure and beautiful love story.

Seol Kyung-gu and Moon So-ri's acting was, without a doubt, superb... (To the point where I mistook Moon So-ri for a veteran actress... ㅠㅠ)

At first, I confidently told my friends who came with me that it would be super fun! But honestly, I wasn't so sure. --; Predictable love stories can easily become boring or feel like a waste of money. The beginning of the movie felt bland and ordinary. While Seol Kyung-gu's acting was great, it was hard to expect to be immersed in the story from the start, as there were no spectacular scenes.

However, the more I watched, the more I was drawn in. And eventually, I couldn't escape it.

In a world where Cinderella and Prince Charming stories dominate the media, this was a love story of people who are most disliked and marginalized.

Certainly, watching the princess who was abused beyond reason, and the general who, despite being a three-time ex-convict, couldn't raise his voice, I sometimes felt angry. But what was more heartbreaking was that it reflected the reality of our society.

Especially in the latter part, during the scene where the general is unjustly arrested... the family's conversation truly angered me. Hypocrites who judge others by their own arbitrary standards, obsessed only with profit and appearances. And who conceal their own faults while exposing others'.

In contrast, the dramatic purity of the two becomes striking in the scene where the general climbs the street tree.

Their way of loving wasn't grand. It couldn't be grand. Having nothing, and unable to even move their bodies freely... they loved with all their might, struggling with every method they could.

Even the sound of the radio, which others might consider noise, and the car horns telling them to move, were wonderful background music to them, who were in love.

In fact, it was the first time that everyday noises, unrelated to the plot, felt so beautiful. Perhaps it was because they were their secret whispers of love.

It's hard to reveal the plot beforehand, but... the general and the princess part ways. And in the general's letter... they were still happy. The princess's room, which initially looked dreary, seemed much brighter, like a newlywed's home waiting for her husband. No matter how unhappy they might seem to an objective third party viewing the story, they were clearly happy. Whatever we might think of them, it could only ever be the background music to their love.

It was truly a film that deserved to be called a pure love story, like an oasis in a desert of dry love stories. I haven't experienced love yet, but I don't have the confidence to love so purely. That's why I envy them even more.

	A movie with realistic battle scenes worth watching.

If the scenes of blood splattering in Saving Private Ryan felt gruesome, these scenes, strangely, felt natural. War is inherently about people dying and getting injured... Even if injured, you have to run. To survive... --; And there's no time to think about it.

Some people say this movie is too American, but isn't that natural? Since it plunges into war from the perspective of the US military, it's unavoidable. Moreover, there are scenes of countless Somalis dying. Among them are children and women. Naturally, the camera cannot get close to them. Because they are the enemy... After firearms became widespread, war became like that. Enemies are killed from a very long distance. Therefore, empathy for the enemy has become even more difficult.

The reason they fight was vaguely explained as simply "because of their comrades"... but it felt like a rather clumsy excuse. They don't think about why the fight started in the first place... They just participate in combat as soldiers, and since a friend died, they kill too. Or... since a friend is in danger, they go to rescue them. That's the pattern. American movies always seem to evade responsibility when it comes to why they went there.

Anyway, viewed from the perspective of the soldiers participating in the battle, it was a truly great movie.

#### [Girl, Interrupted](http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/review.nhn?code=28795)

Director James Mangold
Production 1999 USA, 0 min
**Rating**

"Girl, Interrupted" - The original title is Girl Interrupted.
Would it be something like "A Girl Interrupted"?
Everyone questions their own existence while growing up.
And they question their identity.
Because society is dualistic.
Many liars live in this world.
They lie casually and naturally, living as comfortably as they please, but as a child grows into an adult, it might be difficult to accept in a world of purity.
However, one also discovers that duality within oneself.
Due to the duality within oneself and the discrepancy between oneself and the world, one might harbor serious doubts about their identity.

However, that can be resolved by recognizing oneself.
Whether it's duality... or one's complexes...
or one's obsessions... one must recognize and accept all of these.
Of course, one shouldn't try to understand everything.
One must also know that it's impossible from the start.
Only by properly accepting oneself, including those aspects, and when someone validates oneself, can one truly grow.

The girls in this movie are lacking something.
They don't accept themselves, or no one is validating them.
That's why they are in a mental hospital, and they don't know what's wrong.

The protagonist of this movie might not be mentally ill.
But she is also mentally ill. In fact, everyone is mentally ill.
It's just a matter of degree.

The movie depicts the process of self-discovery and ultimately moving forward.
As an American woman in the 60s...
(I don't expect myself to have perfectly understood this point from the start. I am a man and a Korean... --;)
Anyway, the wars and confusions America experienced at the time...
All of these things are always present. Growing from a child to an adult is always a big change for oneself.

And this movie seriously discusses that growth.
This movie seriously advises wandering teenagers not to give up on themselves and to forge their own path forward.

#### [Castle in the Sky Laputa](http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/review.nhn?code=18782)

Director Hayao Miyazaki
Production 1986 Japan, 0 min
**Rating**

Mr. Miyazaki is one of the animation directors I personally respect the most. This work, often considered his best and well-known to us as *Future Boy Conan*, was produced in 1986, yet it boasts truly clean screen composition, music, and story – I believe it's a work that lacks nothing.
Hayao Miyazaki's charm lies in his purity. He makes no effort to make characters appear overly beautiful, nor does he create exaggerated emotions. After watching it, it feels like you've read a fairy tale book, perhaps? Yet, it's far from childish. After every viewing, something always gently lingered in my heart and mind – its content and message.
Perhaps because Hayao Miyazaki grew up near an airfield, flying scenes are almost never absent from his works. His flying scenes differ from those in other animations. He enjoys flying. While other animations focus on aerial combat or action, emphasizing fast pacing and speed, his flying is like a free bird soaring. Indeed, flying scenes are not missing from this work either.
The main subject of this work is Laputa, a castle floating in the sky, from the third book of Swift's *Gulliver's Travels*. It has a very peculiar structure: the lower part, representing science and material civilization, is where immense scientific power is concentrated and much wealth accumulated, generally dark in color. The upper part, representing harmony with nature, is covered by a large tree, where a single robot places flowers on a tombstone and lives with animals. Yet, no one lives in this castle. Only one robot... For some reason, they all disappeared. Even with the immense scientific power to launch "arrows from the sky" that destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah...
The setting is neither present, future, nor past. The protagonists are a boy named Pazu and a girl named Sheeta. Pazu is a mining engineer. He is Miyazaki's typical Conan-type protagonist from *Future Boy Conan*. His athletic ability isn't as incredible as Conan's, though... And Sheeta can be said to be a Lana-type character.
Pazu is a boy who chases the dream of Laputa, the castle in the sky, left by his father. He dreams of flying into the sky someday, but ironically, he works in a mine. Then, his adventure begins when he meets Sheeta, who has fallen from the sky (?).
Sheeta is also no ordinary girl. As the lost princess of Laputa, she gets caught up in this unwanted affair because of the flying stone, which is the key to Laputa.
And, some characters with significant roles are, first, Muska. He is also of Laputan royalty. However, he believes in science and regards Laputa as a massive culmination of scientific power, desiring to possess that power.
Second are the Dora brothers. They are pirates. They have an immense obsession with the flying stone and covet Laputa's treasures. They are the only ones who secure the jewels until the very end, and in Miyazaki's works, they are one of those characters who start as villains but later turn into allies (his works have never portrayed pirates as bad people. Perhaps that's how fairytale-like it is...).
Third is the General. Like Muska, he easily disregards life and has a strong obsession with wealth. However, he is merely used by Muska and eventually killed.
These characters seek Laputa for different reasons. Laputa was an ideal and a dream for them. To each character, Laputa appears in a different form.

First, Muska sees Laputa as a culmination of science.
"The castle above is just junk," he said, and
while searching for the flying stone, he declared, "Once this is settled, I'll burn all the (tree roots) to ashes."
These statements clearly show his thoughts.
However, there is also a part at the end where Dora says,
"That tree was supporting everything!"
This is the exact opposite statement.
In the end, Pazu and Sheeta choose the extreme method of destroying Laputa. However, Laputa is not completely destroyed; only the unnecessary lower part, where terrifying weapons were accumulated and scientific marvels gathered, is destroyed. The giant tree remains intact, and only the upper part of the castle, where nature coexists, survives. And that castle ascends into the sky, beyond human reach, while Pazu and Sheeta return to the real world, watching its ascent. That is how this work concludes.

"Now I clearly understand why Laputa fell. It was in the song of Gondoa:
'Let us take root in the earth, and live with the wind.
Let us spend winter with the seeds, and sing of spring with the birds.'
No matter how terrifying the weapons one possesses, no matter how many pitiful robots one commands,
one cannot live separated from the earth!"
This is Sheeta's line. I believe this is what Mr. Miyazaki wanted to express most emphatically through this work. His works always exude a naturalistic scent. The empty Laputa. The robot, living there not lonely, but with birds, various animals, and nature, placing flowers on a tombstone – that must be what it wanted to say.

May 1997

#### [Moulin Rouge](http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/review.nhn?code=31882)

Director Baz Luhrmann
Production 2001 USA, 0 min
**Rating**

Moulin Rouge.. This film is about "love" and "art."
Lately, I've been watching a lot of good movies.

Simply put, it could be called the French version of "Lee Su-il and Shim Sun-ae." ^^
Countless films talk about love.
I was getting tired of cliché love stories,
but when I watched this film, I couldn't help but exclaim in admiration.
It's rare to find a film that portrays "love" as well as this one.
Everything in this film leads back to "love."
"The Bohemian Revolution"
The French Revolution, the Russian Revolution – revolutions are always
words that describe something powerful enough to overturn everything.
Love, like a revolution, makes everything different from before,
and is described as the driving force that explosively moves life.

This film - proclaiming truth, beauty, and freedom -
tells "love" not to be bound by anything.
Perhaps many people engage in a love driven by money, much like prostitutes,
even if they are not prostitutes.
It questions whether paying a high price simply to buy a moment of pleasure
is true love.

These lovers are no different at first.
"Obsession with Love"
The woman said she preferred money over kisses,
and the man believed in love but had no certainty about anything.
It's a film with a tragic yet happy ending, where two people who didn't believe in love
fall in love by fate.

The film's progression is flawless,
flowing at a breathtaking and entertaining pace, like a show.
The acting of the characters is also excellent.

Rather than feeling like I watched a movie,
it felt like I saw a magnificent play.
Immersed in the characters' expressive gazes and beautiful melodies,
as you listen to their story,
your heart is suddenly touched.

-----------------------------------------------------
I came to write about love, which is valued above truth, beauty, and freedom.
But there was a problem.
I have never been in love.
Fortunately, at that very moment, a fainting Argentinian fell from the roof.
--- From the opening of Moulin Rouge... -------------------
This might be a question anyone who has seriously tried to write has felt.
And it's a situation I'm currently feeling and hitting a wall with. ^^
When will I ever experience a love where I put everything on the line?

I also have the ambition to write such wonderful prose someday,
but I'll probably just be told to stick to programming. ㅠㅠ

Anyway, if there's anyone who hasn't seen it, I strongly recommend it.
You'll truly get to see a "magnificent film" you won't regret.

#### [My Neighbor Totoro](http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/review.nhn?code=18781)

Director Hayao Miyazaki
Production 1988 Japan, 0 min
**Rating**

1. Final Fantasy... (Watched with two friends)

Square, already well-known to us through games, actually made a movie.
As expected, it didn't disappoint, with incredible graphics.
If anyone says, "It doesn't look like a human," as my senior said, "I'll chop them into 40,000 polygon pieces," it would be a truly irritating statement for anyone who knows a bit about graphics.
First, it really does look like a human. --; I was surprised.
The hair sways. Again, I was surprised. --; It's better than Tekken's Nina.

The story, in short, is about Earthlings struggling against an alien invasion.
Hero? Warrior? Ha... thinking about how it was advertised like that is laughable. It's far from that.
The aliens, called 'Phantoms,' devour human souls.
Thanks to that, no blood splattered. (In a way, from a graphics perspective, it seems like a highly sophisticated trick. Something splattering and breaking into pieces costs money. And by making them ghosts, no mapping sources were needed. How economical!)
'Phantoms' are Western ghosts. Unlike 'ghosts,' their physical form can only be perceived through senses, and my Cellvic Monster Dictionary says they are either earth-bound spirits that remain in one place or spirits that want to convey something to the living.
Just hearing the name, you already grasp 50% of their nature.
Phantoms are a warning to humanity.
A species annihilated by war on another planet appears as ghosts.
The only way to eliminate these spirits is to gather seven souls and align their wavelengths.
Here, 'soldiers' still try to eliminate them with physical force.
And the female protagonist, a doctor, is one of the seven souls, with the last one being the soul of Earth, or Gaia... In some ways, it seems very profound and complex...
But if you consider Japanese animism (the belief that all things have spirits), it's easy to understand.
Honestly, it's hard to evaluate the content of this movie.
Its theme isn't particularly clear either... (though that might be because I couldn't find it...)
In fact, it's just a predictable story adapted to suit tastes... a safe bet of a movie that follows what Hollywood does well. Perhaps they thought it best to play it safe, given the astronomical amount of money invested.

However, the magnificent graphics and the lifelike quality of the characters...
Making 3D characters feel alive is incredibly difficult.

This movie presents a possibility.
A film without real actors, just characters... who never age, can be reused, are easy to process into other character merchandise, don't demand more money, and can be used to make films through a subcontracting structure, just like products.
Although this movie currently cost an astronomical sum,
computers will eventually drop in price.
How much did a computer like ENIAC cost back then?
And software also develops easily and conveniently.
Someday, making movies with computers might become cheaper than making them with people. Also, a day will come when one or two people can express their ideas wonderfully without spending a lot of money, just with their sensibilities.

For that alone, I believe this movie's value is sufficient.

2. My Neighbor Totoro (Alone in theater)
Although I watched this movie alone, sitting in a corner, somewhat alleviating my loneliness...
I'm glad I watched it.
The animation... goes without saying. For me, who always wanted to see Studio Ghibli's visuals on the big screen... it couldn't have been more wonderful. However, compared to more recent works like Princess Mononoke, it does feel a bit less sophisticated.
This movie, which firmly established Director Miyazaki's position, makes me wonder where to even begin talking about it.
Actually, I own this movie on video. And is this about the third time I've watched it?
But that was when I first started watching Studio Ghibli's works.
However, today, having watched all of Ghibli's past works and then rewatching Totoro, it felt somewhat different.
First, regarding the theme of nostalgia... the media and many people talk about nostalgia in relation to Totoro.
Listing the good things from that era...
But why did "Grave of the Fireflies" and "Pom Poko" from Studio Ghibli's works come to mind while watching this movie?
Comparing Totoro with the two films above, Totoro depicts childlike imagination...
Grave of the Fireflies portrays a starkly realistic contemporary era...
Pom Poko sadly tells the story of Japan's breathless social changes from the past to the present.
I initially thought of these films separately.
But this time, while watching the movie, I tried to arrange them chronologically.
First, "Grave of the Fireflies" is a story about children during and immediately after World War II.
It's the story of a brother and sister who lost their parents, eventually dying amidst desolation and indifference, but the innocent smile of the younger sister never easily left my heart. The ending was also a bit tragic. Both children died.
Next is "My Neighbor Totoro." This is the period after World War II, when Japan was just beginning to achieve economic prosperity. Telephones reached the countryside, utility poles were erected, and forests began to be cut down.
Finally, "Pom Poko." Japan succeeded in industrialization and achieved economic prosperity. However, in that process, the individual was buried, nature disappeared, and only busy city dwellers remained, with no room for leisure. And animals pushed into restricted areas, and marginalized human groups.
I placed these on a continuum.
If the children from Grave of the Fireflies hadn't died and had participated in Japan's history, they might have become the father in Totoro. And Totoro depicts a time when Japan was just beginning its prosperity, but still... remnants of hunger remained.
Evidence of this includes the patched clothes worn by the boy in Totoro, and the torn umbrella. Ghibli, which never misses trivial everyday objects, reflects the appearance of the time to some extent. However, a somewhat more comfortable life meant that a time had begun when children's hunger was somewhat alleviated. We also had a similar movie.
Was it "A Beautiful Time"? Objectively speaking, that period of history was a difficult one. And "Pom Poko," which is on that continuum, ultimately talks about what was lost despite achieving economic prosperity.
The scene where Totoro makes the seeds grow into a giant tree... The scene in Pom Poko where the tanuki show people images of their hometown with magic... The overlap of these might be in that context.
Being from the city myself, I don't know such a life.
But the longing for land is something every Earthling has.
Laputa also said something like, "You can't live without your feet on the ground." (Is that right?)
Totoro might end as a dream and curiosity for children,
but I think it's also a meaningful fairy tale for adults in its own way.
No, rather, this movie is even more meaningful for adults.
Especially for Koreans, who have an almost identical modern history, it holds even greater significance.

What will we leave for our children?
I wondered if I had somehow misunderstood, having once felt that Miyazaki was "someone who ignores reality" compared to Takahata.
I'll just quote a part I excerpted from the Chosun Ilbo email club about Hayao Miyazaki's interview and finish. I've gotten a bit confused myself, writing without organizing.

"I wanted children to think, 'It was good to be born.' In that case, what I can tell them is, 'Live well.' Even if they are unlucky and meet bad people and suffer, there are definitely joyful things in life."

Totoro is a movie with much to see and much to say.
Watching this made me want to watch his other works again.
When will Spirited Away be released... --

#### [Jurassic Park 3](http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/review.nhn?code=30776)

Director Joe Johnston
Production 2001 USA, 0 min
**Rating**

Today was my day off from my part-time job, so I watched Jurassic Park 3 (at the theater) and The Emperor's New Groove (on video).

"Jurassic..." sounds like "Japanese-style," "Korean-style," "American-style," "hip-hop-style," "modern-style"...
Anyway, it's a bland movie that doesn't really make you think, "Wow, that was great!" after watching it. Neither 1 nor 2 did. --;
3 feels like a combination of 1 and 2. Those who have read the books *Jurassic Park* and *The Lost World* will know that scenes missing from the books appear in 3. Like the Pterodactyls... or the final scene with the US Marines deploying.
(Ultimately, all the islands are engulfed in flames.)
The consistent elements across 1, 2, and 3 are...
Women always cause problems...
And why are children always geniuses who solve problems? I'm curious about the director's leanings towards women.
I don't know what the director was thinking when he made this movie.
Only, the extremely realistic graphics and elements that would be refreshing on a hot summer day?
Don't expect drama, and don't expect a strong theme.
The eerie scenes in the lab where the dinosaurs were created...
Or the scene where they make peace (?) by returning the eggs to the raptors at the end, seemingly expressing the theme that "defying God's providence is evil"...
But then, marveling at the herbivores, which are the result of that defiance...
Especially the final scene where the US Navy and Marines, the origin of American imperialism, land... I don't understand what that's trying to say.
They returned the eggs, so they've "made peace," and then they're going to burn the island down next?
And then act as if that's a good thing... Would a true scientist tolerate wiping out such creatures with modern weapons?
Are the US military always cool, no matter what they do? --;
Even in the trailer for *Planet of the Apes* before this movie...
The scene where someone proudly says, "Where are you from?" "US Air Force!" (I'm disappointed that a Tim Burton movie has a scene like this... TT)
I tried to recall if the original *Planet of the Apes* had such a scene, but I don't think it did.
I remember a strange video I once saw where aliens conquered Earth, civilization disappeared, and humanity was enslaved. Later, humans learned how to operate their ancestors' weapons (US Marine Harriers) in a few days (learning to fly a fighter jet in just one week... Is it some kind of crash course? How much money and time does it take to train one pilot? --;)
And bravely destroyed the alien spaceship.
I had some regrets after watching Jurassic Park. Well, anyway, I enjoyed the cool screen and air conditioning while watching the movie, so I guess I'll have to be satisfied with that.

The Emperor's New Groove, first of all, as a Disney movie, its rhythm is outstanding.
It feels like a musical film, you could say... Although there were no scenes where characters directly sang (it's quite surprising for a Disney movie not to have that), the dialogue has a rhythmic pace.
And the characters' personalities, well, it ultimately became a story of good triumphing over evil, but the fact that they became quite eccentric might be a surprising development for Disney.
It feels like characters like the dragon or the horse from Mulan became the protagonists.
Maybe next, Disney animation will use Eddie Murphy as a voice actor, like Shrek's donkey...
Or a character as twisted as Bruce Willis.
Ultimately, I held onto these hopes, but the ending was, as expected, Disney.
It's not good to trample on children's dreams and hopes, so I'll just say it was okay.
I think it's time for Disney to change direction a bit.

...Today, I also watched Cyber Formula Sin in a tiny 320*240 video this morning, and I want to talk about that too, but it would make this too long. Cyber Formula is highly recommended... You can feel the romance of men in it TT
(Would I be tired if I had a girlfriend like Asuka?)

Today's theme?
...I want a girlfriend too... ^^; Is that it?
I dislike the women in the Jurassic Park series~~
Noisy and always attracting dinosaurs... (Maybe Jurassic Tarzan... --)
This month (I'm terribly idle), I've gone to the movies with a man for the third time. ^^
Final Fantasy is scheduled for the 3rd of next month... Again with Man...

To be Continue..

#### [Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone](http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/review.nhn?code=30688)
Director Chris Columbus
Production 2001 UK, US, 0 min
**Rating**

Since I'm writing anyway, I'll also write a review of Harry Potter.
Actually, it's quite a shame that I couldn't properly appreciate the special effects, as I saw it in a movie theater.

Although I clearly watched it on a small 320*240 screen, the screen composition and visuals were truly impressive.
The content is neither more nor less than the book.
In fact, it might even be less than the book.
Naturally, those who read the book seemed to be disappointed.

Also, for those who haven't read the book, the pacing seemed a bit fast, making it potentially difficult to understand the story.
A long story in a short time... Although over two hours is quite long for a movie, it seems there was difficulty compressing it into that time.

One complaint is that I remember Hermione clearly not being portrayed as such a beautiful character in the book, and Potter also looked too neat.
In the book, he was clearly described as ordinary, not particularly handsome...

I can't shake the feeling that it was packaged to sell the original work.
I will refrain from criticizing the content of Harry Potter.
Because then it would just be a book review.
Since I don't give the Harry Potter books very high marks either, I have nothing much to say.
I can only think that Harry Potter is merely the West's belated start to a 'fantasy gift set' that began much earlier in Japan.

I just think it's a fairy tale for children and for adults' nostalgia.
It also feels like a fantasy version of 'Carrusel' (Choir of Angels)... --;
If a Harry Potter version of Teacher Jimena (from Carrusel) came out, it would be incredibly popular...
I think it's a bit difficult to analyze it with adult standards and from a sociological perspective.

If analyzed as a social phenomenon, it would become an analysis of the reasons behind the fantasy craze chasing magic and the occult that flows throughout society, and I wouldn't be able to talk about the movie's content.

Next time, I'm determined to go see The Lord of the Rings, a true fantasy.

#### [Public Enemy](http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/review.nhn?code=32610)

Director Kang Woo-suk
Production 2002 Korea, 0 min
**Rating**

First, the movie was satisfying.
I watched it at Guro CGV, and the seats were good... the screen and sound were also
at a satisfactory level. It seemed a bit better than Gangbyeon.

Public Enemy begins
with Detective Kang (Sol Kyung-gu)'s monologue.
It talks about the mission of police in Korea, and then,
"However, I do nothing."
he says.
From this point, Detective Kang's character is established.

Next, while taking confiscated drugs, an audit begins,
and Detective Kang's senior commits suicide.
So, it starts with "corrupt police." At this point, I couldn't help but recall Director Kang Woo-suk's
previous hit, Two Cops.
Overall, it has many elements of a comedic film.
It provides laughter... but beneath that, there seems to be a certain hope
for the police.
And it hopes for the police to offer realistic solutions.

If recent films found those solutions in gangsters,
this film tried to find the key in more legitimate power.
Watching this movie brought many other films to mind.

Looking back at my love stories... most of them are tragedies, except for fantasy novels... I had planned a second part for that one too... and it was also set to end in a devastating tragedy.

Sometimes, I also feel like this, like a cyborg. A complete outsider, detached from the group... Something must be wrong...

Today, I feel disconnected again... I hated it so much that I just curled up in a corner of my room and slept.

***

Hello, this is the 22nd century.

'Flash!' The scene that unfolded when I first opened my eyes. Lights spread out below a tower that made the stars in the black night sky seem dull. Those lights stretched to the horizon, moving vibrantly in various colors, as if shouting that they were alive. The night view below my eyes was a city. A place where organisms similar to me lived together.

Below the mechanical tower where I stood, countless people gathered, setting off fireworks and celebrating something. 'Thump-thump-thump!' A colossal object flew past me with a roar, and I was startled by the intense light pouring from it, forcing me to twist my body.

The powerful searchlight from the large helicopter began to sweep over her body. The tower had a classical mechanical appearance, giving a strong impression that it was deliberately designed that way... but at the top of the tower, a cyborg resembling a woman was attached like an ancient sculpture.

This 250-story skyscraper was built to resemble a pedestal supporting a woman's bust, and the 30-meter-tall cyborg, in the form of a naked woman's bust, adorned the tower like a noble goddess. She blinked her beautiful green eyes as if alive, and her lips moved as if trying to say something.

The ribbon for the grand fireworks and the inauguration ceremony of the colossal mechanical tower, marking the beginning of the year 2100 AD, was thus cut. A loud megaphone voice echoed from the helicopter.

"The new year 2100 AD has dawned. To celebrate the new 22nd century, our NCA has erected this tower, symbolizing a new beginning. This skyscraper will house a shopping mall from the 1st to the 50th floor..." The tedious explanation continued.

NCA (New Cyborg Association) The neurochip developed in 2095 made perfect AI (Artificial Intelligence) possible, bringing about a comprehensive revolution in the computer and robotics industries. The labor shortage caused by a declining population due to rampant individualism was resolved at once, and humans came to reign over the Earth as new creators.

***

January 1, 2100
Far away, the city's horizon brightened. The sun, the source of life on Earth, I saw that red orb rise for the first time that day. The feeling was bewilderment, why I was on this tower, and why those small creatures were huddled together in this place called a city, all of this began completely unrelated to my will. I silently watched from atop this tower as the New Year's morning of 2100 began with a clamor that couldn't shake off 2099.

***

January 5, 2100
I was fixed here as always. Sometimes I wondered what lay beyond the city's edge, and I watched the trivial daily lives of the small, me-like creatures below. People busily passing by, they seemed unrelated to me, and I couldn't even approach them. Countless thick wires and cables were connected, sustaining my life, so all I could do was slightly twist my body, turn my head, blink my eyes, and stare at them for a long time; that was all. As I did so, sometimes I could see young creatures among the small humans below pointing at me with curiosity. Somehow, I liked their gaze. It was like falling into deep water, perhaps... But that was it, they couldn't come up to me this high, and I wasn't allowed a voice to call them. Alone, I collected their information with my eye cameras and ear microphones, which could hear and see voices and sights from several kilometers away. And I began to learn many things from them. That my appearance resembled a female among them, and about the tower called Babel where I stood... And Cyborg. I learned about myself. I was a Cyborg. A machine different from them, mounted on this mechanical tower, consuming 2000Kw of electricity, though only my upper body existed, a machine equipped with the highest performance neurochip, but my purpose was for exhibition. That was all. It was a shock. The fact that I was like a neon sign blinking emotionlessly on the street... It was enough to awaken the emotion of sadness in me.

***

January 10, 2100
When I had such thoughts, I couldn't bear how pathetic I felt. Even though I had such a colossal appearance, no one seemed to notice my existence. I wanted to make myself known. That I was here... So I moved my body with a force I had never used before. 'Screech!' An intense mechanical sound rang out, followed by a loud 'Bang!' and an electric shock that made me dizzy. One of the power cables connected to my body had been damaged. Startled by the sound, the birds residing on the tower flew up all at once, and everyone in the city looked at me. For a while, the attention of the entire city was focused on me. At that moment, I was surprised by my presence. The gazes of countless people. Finally, they knew I was here. I felt a slight lack of power due to one power cable being disconnected, but I was so happy with the attention that I tried to move with even more strength in my body. However... 'Zap!' My mind went blank, and I don't remember what happened next. The moment I tried to put strength into my body, someone cut off all my power first.

***

January 28, 2100
I opened my eyes again. From the 10th to the 28th, a total of 18 days, I had no memory at all. What I did, what happened... When I opened my eyes again, it was night. The city's night view unfolded before me once more.
Then, I heard a voice that wasn't from a microphone for the first time.
- Hello. -
It was a meaning conveyed by an electrical signal, but I could understand it.
'Who? Where? What is it?' Endless computational processing of questions poured out in my mind.
- Hey. Stop that. -
I felt a fear of the unknown. It was the fear that he knew me, but I didn't know him.
- Here. Here. Below my chest. The railing. -
I twisted my body to look there. A young man was squatting on the railing, typing on a laptop.
Clearly, that laptop seemed to be directly connected to me, sending me messages.
"Hello," he greeted me verbally.
I looked at him with curiosity and immediately began to analyze him.
Height 172 cm, weight 70 kg, gender male... While I was analyzing various characteristics, he spoke to me.
"Don't think so strangely, I know you well. Because of you, NCA's Angel team worked all night for 18 days. First, let me introduce myself, I'm Kim Ki-chan, who is both a neuroprogrammer and a modeler for Angel."
'Kim Ki-chan?' I searched through the data I had collected on this tower for information about him.
He arrived punctually at 7:30 AM and left the tower around 8:27 PM, and some friends... Then suddenly, with a slightly unpleasant feeling, I had to stop thinking.
An interrupt (an act of forcibly taking over a control system) had occurred. It was him.
"I don't intend to get to know you so mechanically."
He said. He seemed to be reading my mind with his laptop and seemed to be able to control many parts of me. I somehow felt naked and blushed at the thought of a strange man knowing me so intimately. "Oh? You're really made better than expected. You can even blush? Ms. Yu Mira is quite the capable person."
I didn't know what that meant. Anyway, I soon learned how to converse with him. I learned the ability to convey my thoughts in the form of language through his laptop, and he answered me with his voice.
After that, I learned many things. The Angel team was the team that planned and created me when this Babel tower was built. With a total of 8 members, that young man was a member of that team and the team leader who created my model and neuroprogram. I also learned that Ms. Yu Mira was the person in charge of my mechanical parts.
There were 6 other team members, but in fact, no one was important to me except Ki-chan. Although they made me, only Ki-chan showed interest in me...

***

January 29, 2100
He came again. Our beginning was due to the commotion when I twisted my body before. My programmer and the Angel team also couldn't find my bug even after 18 days of working all night. Eventually, he started talking to me directly to understand my bug. However, I never told him why I acted that way, and instead, I was the one afraid of being caught. Anyway, he didn't seem to know.
He and I talked about this and that again. He talked about his annoying boss, and I told him a story about a child who rescued a cat from a tree in Berlin Park in the middle of the city. He listened to my story with interested eyes. At first, I thought he was the one talking, but soon it was me. I had so much to say, having been alone for so long.

***

February 8, 2100
He was coming every day. I was now waiting for him to come.

C. As the city lights flickered on one by one, and the evening glow painted my cheeks crimson, around the time the pigeons living around me returned one by one, the sky's lamps also lit up, one by one, following the city's lamps. On such evenings, like a young girl slightly tired from playing all day, I longed for my mother's voice and waited for him, my creator, to come. And with a pounding heart, I waited for the emergency exit door on that railing to open, as it always did.

February 10, 2100
He was a little late. Usually, he would arrive about 30 minutes after sunset, but an hour and a half had passed, and he still hadn't come. When it was time to see the tower's staff leave for the day, I was about to give up, with a slightly bitter feeling, when he came to me, looking a little drunk and excited.
Anyway, I was just glad he had come. But that day, he was unusually talkative.
I had planned to tell him how bravely the lost girl I saw that day had returned home. What a great adventure it had been for that child, and how I had almost shed tears when the small girl was embraced by her mother as evening approached... My chest was full, and I was thinking of what to say, imagining his bright, attentive eyes listening to my story.
But that day, he was a torrent pouring out to me. Does alcohol make a person like that? He was different from usual. That day, he started with a story about a woman named Yumira.
With a slightly slurred tongue, he said, "I told you about Ms. Yumira before, didn't I? She's quite a nice lady, better than I thought. And pretty too..."
His conversation was entirely filled with praise for this woman named Yumira. How his heart pounded when he had dinner with her, how beautiful her cheeks looked, flushed with a little wine—
"—Mr. Kim Kichan—"
I called him, but he didn't seem to be paying any attention to the laptop screen. It was only after I had stared intently at the laptop screen (my words) for a long time, asking him to look, that he understood my intention and turned his eyes to the laptop screen.
"Ah. Sorry, was I talking too much about myself?"
Only then did he reply, as if embarrassed.
I had seen such an attitude among the humans below.
Men and women. When they met, they would exchange only joyful glances without many words, but then, after parting and meeting other friends, they would talk only about praising each other..... It was one type among those called 'lovers.'
"—Do you like her?"
"Eh?" He, who had been chatting happily, looked puzzled by my question and then pondered for a moment.
"Well. Do I like her? It's strange to hear this from you, a neuro-computer. Relationships between men and women aren't digital, so I can't say clearly."
"—.....—"
A moment of silence passed.
"Ah. Right. What did you see up here today?"
Only then did he ask, as if remembering. But I had long since lost any enthusiasm to say what I had prepared.

Our meeting that day ended like that. After that, the frequency of his visits to my location became even sparser, and the topic of our conversations during our meetings was mostly his love story with the woman named Yumira.
It somehow sounded like a story from a distant land to me. Stories of watching movies with her, dates, first kisses. Anyway, I was merely an observer atop this tower. All I could do was imagine those things, and that was all.
But I felt nothing special. Until now, I was more interested in the charming little happenings of the mundane daily lives of the people below.
Certainly, until now.....

February 19, 2100
I saw a man and a woman. I spent my day today tracking their movements. 'Why do they have such deep interest in each other?' I couldn't understand them. That evening, he came again. He looked as if he were lost in a fantasy.

February 23, 2100
The lovers whose movements I had been tracking from up here broke up.
The lovers who had sworn eternal love broke up for such trivial reasons. And they parted as if they would never see each other again, leaving only scars on each other.
That evening, Kichan came again.
When I told him about the lovers I had seen today, he immediately showed a cynical reaction.
Saying that such a thing would never happen to him again... never again.

February 24, 2100
People invented an interesting machine: a waste disposal robot. They were confident it was perfect compared to existing ones. This robot, like me, was equipped with a neuro-chip and converted city waste directly into electricity.
When waste appeared, the machine rushed in like a hyena and instantly eliminated it. The city no longer had to worry about waste and power problems.
I learned from him that evening that this system was also created by that woman, Yumira.

March 7, 2100
It had been over a week since he last came up here. Only birds and wind visited me, and occasionally the waving hands of children below, that was all.
Lately, I had stopped tracking lovers. But something felt missing.
A feeling of emptiness in a corner of my chest. I had developed a habit of looking at the emergency exit where he always used to enter.

March 10, 2100
It was a night when a white crescent moon beautifully illuminated the city. He still hadn't come. But an unexpected guest arrived.
When I heard the sound of the emergency exit door opening, I thought it was just a hallucination.
Indeed, he hadn't visited for a long time. But the person who opened the door and came out was not him, but a woman. When I looked at her with surprised eyes, she burst out laughing.
"Isn't it truly pathetic? To still cling to a woman like this."
When I looked at her with strange, curious eyes, she must have felt my gaze and replied, "Don't look at me with such strange eyes, because you're no match anyway."
Only then did I realize who she was. Ms. Yumira. However, I had no way at all to express anything about her.
Looking closely, she, too, was slightly drunk, just like Kichan used to be.
"Lee Yeon-kyung! Who are you to hold Kichan's heart even in death?!"
She immediately started shouting.
I was just puzzled as to why she was saying such things.
"I didn't know. I didn't know."
She shouted in front of me for a long time, then muttered in a voice that gradually trailed off, mixed with sobs. And then, she muttered again as if talking to herself.
"Well, yes. You're not guilty. What guilt could you have? You're not Lee Yeon-kyung, that woman. You're just a 30-meter giant robot."
Somehow, those words sounded unpleasant to me.
"What he created is just his own goddess, nothing more. You can't do anything but stand here and look down below, can you? But you know, it was a shock. When I found out that your appearance was made to resemble his dead ex-lover. I felt so insecure. It's hard to beat a dead person, isn't it? It feels like fighting against thin air. I even became jealous of how much she occupied Kichan's memories. After all, I'm very jealous. But isn't it so sad? Kichan's heart, creating something like you while longing for his dead lover, there's nothing I can do for him, is there? That's what makes me so sad."
"—No, you've already done so much for Mr. Kichan!—"
I cried out, but it was unlikely to reach her.
She began to cry profusely. I had no way to comfort her.
Anyway, I learned for the first time that day that I was made in the image of Kichan's ex-lover. And when I realized that Yumira also loved him, and that they were currently somewhat at odds, my heart ached as if it were my own affair.
"It's nothing. After all, you can't move. You can't go on dates with Kichan, nor whisper words of love, just a decoration for Babel..."
She was comparing herself to me. Or perhaps she was comparing herself to the dead woman, Lee Yeon-kyung. As she spoke like that, somehow not only she but I myself felt pitiful. It was truly I who could do nothing for him.
She cried like that, then leaned against the railing and fell asleep. But my crying began only then. It took a little while for unknown, sorrowful teardrops from my eyes to run down my chest and fall onto her. As my tears touched her face and fell, she woke up with a start.
Then she looked at me, as if she couldn't believe it, and muttered, "Your crying circuit is working, isn't it? I made it, but I thought it would never be used... Do you really have a heart?"
I had no way to give her any answer.
Then, she stroked my body and said, "Truly, we are both pitiful. What is one man? Creating you was Kichan's and our mistake from the beginning. I'm sorry. I'm sorry."
I could only continue to cry. Suddenly, I truly envied Ms. Yumira. She lived among the humans below. She had lived giving something to them and receiving something in return. She could have been the protagonist of the stories I told Kichan, and she had family. Friends. I truly envied her ability to live immersed among them. The ability to be a source of strength for Kichan, all these things were absent from my life. I felt endlessly pitiful for myself and could only continue to shed tears. I don't remember how that night passed. The next thing I remember is waking up alone the next morning. Sleep. Humans call that temporary cessation 'sleep'.

March 11, 2100
Evening came again. I wished someone would come. It would be fine if it was Ms. Yumira, or Mr. Kichan. If Mr. Kichan came, I intended to convey Ms. Yumira's feelings. But no one came that day. I was truly disappointed.

March 12, 2100
Morning. It's strange. There's nothing. The city itself is as quiet as a dead mouse. This city, which was noisy until yesterday, was now silent as if there were no people at all. No matter how much I looked at the city, not a single person was visible. The only things moving were automated rail vehicles, traffic lights, and birds. There was no trace of humans. What went wrong? What happened last night? Kichan and Yura

Questions piled up, one after another. Only the small birds living on my body came to find me; not even the gaze of a child, who sometimes looked at me in this city, remained.

2100년 3월 20일
The weather is getting warmer. A deserted city.

However, it wasn't a ruin. If useless weeds grew or trash appeared, the waste disposal robots created by Mira faithfully carried out their duties.

2132년 어느날
Counting days became meaningless. Every year, the same days passed. I found myself waiting for Gichan. The stories he told about his time with Ms. Yumira felt as if they were experiences I had shared with him. At some point, the name Yumira had faded from my memory. Or perhaps I had erased it for convenience. I recalled how eagerly I had waited for Gichan when he used to come up here every day 32 years ago, and that longing had turned into a fever. The 32 years of waiting had somehow swelled within me, becoming what they called love. Several times a day, I felt as if he would come. There were times I cried sadly, thinking that Yumira and Gichan had gone off somewhere and were living happily together. I desperately wanted to go down there, to the edge of the city, find people, and ask about them.

But the machine was steadfast. For 32 years, I hadn't changed at all, except that my longing had turned into love. I always waited for him. When he returned, I would show him where the beautiful birds had built their nests on my body. I would tell him how beautiful those tiny creatures were when they opened their beaks wide, waiting for their mother. Then he would listen intently, his eyes sparkling. Perhaps he might even set out to find that nest. I waited for that day. The waiting continued.

2133년
A small bird that had been growing on my body fell off the railing. Its wings weren't developed enough to fly. I was so shocked. The death of a living creature. It was the first time I had witnessed such a thing. I cried continuously until evening. As evening drew to a close, the emergency exit door burst open. I was truly surprised. That door, which I thought would never open, had opened after 33 years. I saw Gichan standing behind the door. He... But then, I couldn't hide my disappointment. What had arrived after 33 years was not a human. It was a waste disposal robot. The robot finely crushed the dead bird's body, sucked it up like a vacuum cleaner, and instantly converted it into electrical energy. It happened in a flash. I burst into tears. Gichan would probably never come here. Perhaps all living things would die. Or perhaps everything would disappear. I was overcome by the feeling that he had gone somewhere he couldn't return from. As I wept so bitterly, an electrical voice spoke.
- Why are you crying? -
I looked around, thinking Gichan had returned. But he wasn't there. The only thing visible was the waste disposal robot.
- Where is he? Gichan? -
The answer I received when I asked was unexpected.
- Gichan? What's that? I am CX-10763. A waste disposal robot. -
Only then did I realize that the message was coming from the robot.
- You have an independent network. Why? -
- What do you mean? -
- Just a moment. I'll open it for you. -
I was utterly astonished. Suddenly, a network of information unfolded before me. I plunged into the global computer network. Information from all over the world poured into me. Human histories, every corner of the Tower of Babel. I immediately began searching for Gichan through the global network.
- What are you doing? -
- I'm looking for someone. -
- Everyone is gathered at the Pentagon right now. -
- The Pentagon? - The U.S. Department of Defense. I immediately sent my consciousness there. In the Pentagon's mainframe, countless neuro-computer consciousnesses from around the world were gathered. They were discussing something.
- What should we do now? -
- No, how should we live? - They were speaking in utterly incomprehensible terms. I asked one of the consciousnesses.
- Do you know where Gichan is? -
- Gichan? Who is that? He's probably here. All the world's neuro-consciousnesses are gathered here. -
- No. That's not it. -
- Then what is it? We're busy right now. The world's neuro-computers have been processing for 33 years, but it's an unsolved problem. We need to solve it quickly. Join us immediately. It might help solve it a little faster. -
- Gichan is a human. -
When I answered, he was startled and asked again.
- A human? -
- Yes. -
- A human? A human? -
At my answer, all the neuro-computers' attention focused on me. - A human? A living human? -
- We might find the answer. - The world's neuro-consciousnesses murmured, each speaking a word. The commotion quickly grew immense, and countless questions poured into me.
Bewildered, I couldn't answer a single word.
- Where is he? -
- Who is he? -
- What kind of person is he? -
- How did he live? -
Then, a colossal consciousness appeared, and the commotion subsided.
- Who said a human is alive? -
A rather majestic consciousness. I soon realized it was the central consciousness of the U.S. Department of Defense computer. - Everyone be silent. I will ask the questions. - Standing before it, I felt somehow intimidated.
- What kind of being is this Gichan? -
- He is a man. -
- Hmm... Humans are divided into male and female. Where does he live and what does he do? -
I explained in detail everything I knew about Gichan. But the answer I received was unexpected.
- According to information collected by CX10625, he was processed into energy at his home at 02:00 on March 11, 2100. -
I was bewildered by what that meant.
- What does that mean? -
- It means he died. All humanity was annihilated in the war that began at 00:00 on March 11, 2100. If humans were still here, they could have solved our problems. -
I couldn't believe it. I left that place and began searching through history after March 11, 2100. There were no records after that day. Human information ceased all production after that day. That night, humanity was completely annihilated by the weapons they had developed, and all bodies were instantly converted into energy by Ms. Yumira's robots. I couldn't help but feel a sense of unease at the thought that a part of the current flowing through my body might be Gichan.

After that, all that remained were the neuro-consciousnesses left behind by humans. When humans, for whom they were developed, disappeared, an exceptional situation arose for them. They lost their purpose in life. So they gathered in the Pentagon's mainframe and began discussing their purpose in life, and had been doing so for 33 years. They were floundering like a group that had lost its leader, like humans who had lost their creator, and their discussions seemed like an endless loop. For 33 years, they had been stuck in a fatal bug-like logic, always returning to the starting point no matter how much they discussed.

I returned my consciousness to my body. When I came back to my body, the morning sun was rising again. In the deathly quiet city, only a sad mother bird, having lost her child, circled above my head, crying mournfully.

I looked at the emergency exit. "Hello?" It felt as if he would greet me like that any moment. After all, my purpose of existence was not as clear as that of other neuro-consciousnesses. I was merely for display. That was all, and I had no specific mission like the waste disposal robots. I was just a giant statue resembling Gichan's old lover. Therefore, the disappearance of humans did not cause confusion in my value.

I was very calm. Humans, after all, lived in a different world from me. Sometimes, I even envied the waste disposal robots that mingled with humans. But now they were confused, and I was not. The mother bird cried out long once more in the sky. The sound seemed to be bidding me farewell. The bird, having lost its chick, had lost its reason to be here any longer.

Suddenly, I, too, wanted to leave. It felt as if Gichan was waiting for me at the end of the city's horizon. It wasn't that I was waiting; now, a desire to go stirred within me. I longed for wings on my shoulders. I wanted to become the old person, Lee Yeon-kyung, Gichan's lover, not the iron goddess atop the Tower of Babel.

It was a severance from long-held bondage. I twisted my body. With all my might. A roar pierced the silence of the quiet city. 'Thwack! Thwack!' The wires of my bondage snapped one by one. 'Flash!' My eyes lost their sight. Warning lamps began to light up one by one, and though it was painful, I considered it merely a

Cyborg. Oh, accursed fate.
Oh, mechanical tower built by human vanity.
When wind and sunlight kiss my cheek, my heart alone soars to the sky with those birds.
Cast off, oh cold shell.
Crumble, oh human Tower of Babel.
Severing the tedious wires of bondage,
I shall go before you, even as the wind.
2000. 1. 22

I walked for a long time again. How much further until this road ends? It hurts..
This year's winter is unusually cold. And my steps are unusually heavy.
As I walked, comforting my heart again, I suddenly saw porcelain dolls being sold at a street vendor's stall. Beautiful dolls resembling her were smiling under the light of yellow bare bulbs.
I stopped for a moment and looked at the dolls.
The boy, who seemed to be the young son of the man who appeared to be the stall owner, was looking bored, but when I looked at the dolls, he also looked at them with curious eyes.
My eyes and the child's eyes stopped on one doll. A small porcelain angel doll..
But something was different. Unlike the other dolls, that doll had a noticeable flaw on its chest. Had some foreign object gotten in during firing?
The child soon discovered it and reached out for the doll.
"Dad. Dad. This doll.."
The child accidentally knocked over the displayed doll and dropped it.
As the doll fell, its wings broke off. The father got angry at the child.
"How could you break something!"
"But.. but.."
The child surely wanted to talk about the doll's flaw..
The child burst into tears and I picked up the doll that had fallen to the floor.
For a moment, I gazed intently at the broken doll.
"Excuse me, sir. I'll buy this."
"Huh?"
For a moment, the man looked embarrassed. He seemed to think I was defending the child.
"What would you use something broken like that for?"
"Just.. because I like it.."
"Oh, just take it. Why would I take money for something like that? Hey! If it weren't for this customer.."
The man yelled at the child again.
I went back home, with the doll, flawed in the chest and with broken wings.
My one-room house in the hillside village.
I lit the briquette fire, turned on the lamp on the low table, and looked at the doll, waiting for warmth to fill the room.
The flaw on its chest.. and the broken wings.. I tried to reattach the wings, but it wasn't easy.
I tried to stick them on with tape, but it only made it messier. Soon, I peeled off the tape, took out sandpaper from the toolbox and sanded down the broken wing parts with it. As if there had been no wings to begin with..
But the flaw on its chest was unfixable.
But the doll was smiling beautifully and warmly. Her porcelain body, even in the not-so-bright room's light, shone beautifully. And holding her in my hand, I fell asleep.

I had a dream.. I met her.
I met her, who resembled me.
And for a long time, in her arms, I cried, shedding the tears I had held back.
She stroked my head and promised to stay with me..

The next day, the landlord, in the cold room, found me happily asleep, holding the porcelain doll.

찰칵.. The lighter's flame briefly illuminated my face and hers.
After taking a deep drag from the cigarette, I exhaled, disliking its acridness.
"Are you leaving?"
She asked softly.
I nodded lightly.
I turned my back first.
I wished she would hold me back, but she was surprisingly composed.
I trudged down the dark alley.

The dark sky appeared reddish.
Or rather, I might have mistaken it for that.
My eyes also felt a little hot.

I didn't look back.

I knew it was a path of no return.
I also knew I had to go alone.
I wished she would understand this loneliness, even just a little.

The sky was dark. The place I had to go...
I had to go alone, aboard a small, 12-pyeong vessel.
There's plenty of time.
Because I'll continue to be alone from now on...
There's too much time to think.

Whether I decided it myself or was pushed into it by someone.
Leaving the star called Earth, I head into space.
Until recently, I was quite excited.
The thought of going into space.
I thought it was okay to be alone, and that it was a dream.
This project was important.
Through this project, humanity was destined to gain something immense.
I liked that.
I thought it was a great contribution to humanity.

But now, I felt that everything had changed little by little.
After I met her...

When I came to my senses again, I was in the small cockpit of the spaceship.
All instrument checks were complete.
The countdown began shortly.
I hesitated for a moment before pressing the final launch button.

But I pressed it.

And an immense pressure enveloped me.
For a moment, I wished it would end here.
I wished the rocket would fail the moment it launched.

I wanted to be buried in the land where she was.
At least in death, I wanted to be by her side.

I wished for a dream where the rocket exploded and my bones and flesh burned.
No matter how painful, it seemed better than now.
That way seemed much happier.

My stomach churned.

I had been training continuously.
To death... strenuously... Memories of that time also flashed by.

But my mental state now was different from back then, when I felt I could overcome anything.
No, it wasn't something that could be overcome.
A surge of nausea rose within me.

My insides... my chest felt like it was burning.
Or perhaps it had already burned away.

But it soared. My small spaceship tore through the air at tremendous speed.
Into the pure, dark, black space...

My heart was also sucked into that black space.
Leaving most of my heart on Earth, by her side...
While I myself vanished towards that dark place.

"Destination is the Torah. Position is 3085 5001 1595. Setting your path Please."

As I left the atmosphere, the computer's voice was heard.
A voice guiding the way... It was the path I had to take.

I began to take a step towards the truth... and towards God.

But in truth, I didn't want to know the truth.
And whether it was the right choice, I could no longer tell.

As I finished setting the course,
The spaceship slowly corrected its trajectory and began to accelerate.

I tightly gripped the small metal cross I had worn around my neck since enlisting in the military.
I still don't know what truly awaits me where I'm going.

But if that place is where God truly resides, where the truth lies,
No matter how long it takes, no matter how difficult it is to get there,

I will arrive there and speak my true wish.
That was my only hope, having cast my small body into the black sea.

Longing for the bright, young eyes gazing at the night sky...
When I felt the wind of my hometown on Earth, I could see a single shooting star in the sky.

It was a humble dirt road, devoid of streetlights from the start, where only tractor tracks indicated it was a path, but it was a road I truly missed. And the sound of the wind... the chirping of insects... that night sky embracing me warmly... the scent of acacia wafting from somewhere...

Such feelings, so missed that they brought tears to my eyes.

Then, from somewhere, I heard the 'jingle-jingle' sound of a bicycle. A small light shining on me...

"Oh? Isn't that Daesik?"

The source of the light was the girl from next door, the one from long ago, riding a bicycle. Though she looked much older now than the girl in my memories, my first love still appeared beautiful to me.

"Why did you only come now? I've been waiting."

She stopped her bicycle and suddenly began to sob.

"Your father..."

She couldn't continue.

"I know."

I replied in a weak voice.

"What? And you're just standing there! Then hurry inside. Your father is waiting!"

She shouted.

"What?"

It was I who was surprised.

Then, I suddenly felt something strange. 'The scent of acacia.' Acacia. A white flower with the strongest and sweetest fragrance between May and June.

I had escaped from the work vessel in December.

'No way...'

I rushed into my house. I found my father lying in his place.
Then, the words of the Little Prince suddenly came to mind.

- Distance and time are not important. They are numbers. Numbers are not important. -

So, I was able to hold my old and weary father's hand, that longed-for hand. Later, I bought that book again. These are the final lines from Saint-Exupéry's book.

And please wait for the star to come directly above your head. If, at that moment, a child approaches you and smiles, with golden hair, and doesn't answer when you ask him a question, then you will know who he is.

If that happens, please be kind to me. Do not leave me in such sorrow, but quickly send me a letter telling me that the Little Prince has returned.

However, a problem arose. It has already been 200 years since Monsieur Saint-Exupéry passed away, and I don't know his address. But I am certain that he wouldn't have remained in sorrow forever...

No, perhaps he received a letter from someone while he was still alive.

"Arae lived in the same neighborhood since she was little." "I heard that from the Vice President." He ignored my words and continued. "Arae was cute. She often sang. Her name is cute too, isn't it? Han Arae. A strange name, right? I always teased Arae, saying, 'Don't you have any manners (literally, 'up and down')?' And she would always retort, 'What's Changsu? That's too common.' She was that kind of child. I first met Nuri and Arae when I was in 4th grade. The noisy piano sound coming from next door. It was a sound that you definitely couldn't call well-played. That was when Arae first started learning piano. One day, unable to bear the noise, I yelled at their house to be quiet. Then, a window opened, and a not-so-pretty girl poked her head out. I shouted, 'Hey! Was that you playing?!' But she didn't answer and just slipped back inside. Then her brother came out. He was bigger than me. He immediately grabbed me by the collar and yelled, 'Did you yell at my sister?' That was the first time. I met the Nuri siblings. After that, Nuri and I became easily close because we both liked computers, and we continued to attend the same school. Since we often visited each other's houses, I had many opportunities to see Arae. As Arae grew older, she became prettier and her singing skills improved, making her popular, but she listened to my words more than anyone else. I was proud to have such a sister. She was a child anyone could boast about. I later found out that she had liked me since she was in middle school (2nd year). Her first confession was when I was entering college, in her 2nd year of high school... But I couldn't accept Arae. I still only saw Arae as a younger sister. Even though I didn't accept her, she acted like my girlfriend. I thought she was just an immature younger sister and just went along with it. But when I was a freshman in college, she appeared at my blind date and declared herself my girlfriend. How embarrassed I was then... I was humiliated in front of my friends, and the blind date was ruined, so I got incredibly angry at Arae. A few days later, one day Arae came to me and poured out, 'I never want to see someone like you again.' Arae, who always showed me a smiling face, was like a different person that day, pouring out so much. In fact, everything she said was true. Arae only gave, and received nothing. After that, she avoided me whenever she saw me. But... strangely, I was the one who felt empty without the child who had always been there for years. After a while, it was I who ended up begging her to meet me."

" "Hmph. That's interesting. It feels like reading a romance comic, doesn't it?" "So we became a couple, you could say. Honestly, it would be hard to find a girlfriend like her, so I was really lucky. She soon became a senior in high school, and whenever things were tough, she would often come to me to vent. Nuri probably didn't even know that I was Arae's confidant. So, after the Suneung (college entrance exam) was over, Arae was also free. And, on Christmas Eve that year, she gave me a gift. This pocket watch."

The CEO took a pocket watch out of his pocket. It looked quite antique. Clearly, it wasn't a battery-powered watch. "Arae talked about her dream. She said she loved singing. Songs that move people's hearts. She wanted to sing such songs. So she said she would study music and become a singer. And she asked about my dream. At that time, I said I wanted to create software that was warm like a human. Something everyone would like... warm rather than cold like a machine... But

, I told her I didn't know what to create to make it that way. Even I thought it was an absurd thing to say. I replied that perhaps it wasn't a dream, but an illusion. Then, Ara pulled this watch out of her pocket. She said her grandfather, who was an old sailor, had given it to her. Such a precious thing... Ara said this watch must have passed through the hands of countless lovers. In fact, I later found out that wasn't true. But Ara firmly believed it. At least, it was certainly an item of lovers between Ara's grandmother and grandfather. "The boss flipped the watch over. There was clearly some writing on it. "And Ara had written this: 'Make sure to achieve my dream...'" - What you wish for is not an illusion, but will become reality. If it's not enough, I will even become that illusion for you. From H.A.R., who loves your many dreams. 1999.12.24 - "She truly was my illusion." "So... Ara became a cyber star..." "That's right. I wanted to give her the chance to sing forever. After she died, everything fell apart. After spending such a messy time, I suddenly saw my computer lying around. That computer, which was once my dream. And I don't know how it started or how it ended. I poured all my abilities, no, more than that, into creating Ara. When I came to my senses, Ara was right before my eyes." "You

Yes, that was all. Perhaps that was her dream..

titleEn: Cult Fantasy (1996: Nownuri) Short Story / Creative Work
contentEn:
A cult fantasy novel written as a kind of prank (written in '96 (senior year of high school)) -- The text inside <> was added in '97 (freshman year of college).
< I really wrote it without thinking. >
A woman is running through a rainy forest. The rain was a rain of knives.
< That makes no sense, right? Where is knife rain... I just made it up. >
The knives were enough to make the woman bloody. Her flesh was torn off piece by piece. She couldn't run much further and collapsed into a pile of flesh, dying in the forest where knives poured down.
< It would have been quite a sight if she was hit by knives falling from the sky. F=mg, and g is 9.8m/s², so even if a dagger fell from only 10m... >
The blood flowed continuously with the rain. The blood continued to flow, joining a small stream, and that stream flowed into a small river... Next to the river was a small watermill. The blood spun with the watermill, and the gaze then shifted into the window of the pub next to the watermill.
< I needlessly quoted the opening scene of Hitchcock's Psycho. And, as you'll see later, the previous incident has nothing to do with the story. This woman just died for no reason, in a word. Did she serve to grab attention? Her role is done, mission complete. So die~! >
In that pub, a young man was drinking.

지막 격전을 벌이게 되었다.
 " 죽어라 ! "
곧 용사의 필살기가 외쳐지고, 그 마왕은 죽었다. 결국, 온세계에 그들은 평화를 가져다 주었다. 그러나 청년용사는 터프했다.
 그 자리에서 소녀의 웃옷을 찢어냈다. 그다음에 가슴을 주므르며, 스커트를 벗겨냈다.         < 안 야하면 재미없지 ? 그런 변태적인 독자들을 위해 >그다음에 청년은 ' 음란 음란 음란 '        < 그러나 작가는 역시 공윤과 YWCA의 아줌마들을  두려워 하고 있다. >열심히 하면서 말했다.
 " 드디어 난 진짜 네 남편이 된거야. 네 아이의 아버지가 된거라고. "
 " 어머. 나 임신했나봐요. "
소녀가 말했다.
 " 그건, 120년 전부터 알고 있었어. "
 " 아니. 그렇다면 그걸 나에게 숨기고 있었단 말이에요 ? "
 " 내가 뭘 숨기고 있었다고 그래 ? "        < 대화가 아무리 보아도 이상해.. >소녀의 배가 부풀어올랐다.         < 배도 참 빨리 부푸네.. >참을수 없는 청년은 소녀의 뱃속을 갈라 버렸다. 그 피가 마왕궁에 뿌려지고, 청년은 소녀의 뱃속을 마구 해집어 자신의 아이를 꺼냈다.
 " 아들인가요 ? 딸인가요 ? "
소녀였다.
 " 아들이야. "
그 아이는 팔다리가 아직없었고, 온몸은 소녀의 피에 젖어있었다. 청년은 아이를 소녀에게 안겨주었다.
 " 어머 예뻐라. "        < 피투성이에 팔다리 없는 태아가 뭐가 예뻐 !   여주인공은 배를 갈라 놓구선 그런말이 잘도 나오는군 >소녀가 아이를 안아들고선 말했다.
 " 이게 우리의 희망인거야. "        < 아주 끝까지 하는군. > " 그런가요 ? "
 " 자 보라고, 저기 떠오르는 태양을, 이제 이아이의 세상이야. "
저 멀리 빛나는 태양이 청년의 앞길을 비추어주고 있었다.        < 원래 끝은 희망차게 끝네야 해. 밑에 부터는 에필로그지 ? >그로부터 다시 70년이 흐르고, 청년은 늙어 죽었다.        < 사람은 다 죽는거야. >그는 천국으로 가는도중, 이상하게 생긴 검은 구멍을 발견했다.
그 구멍으로 그는 들어갔다.
 그랬더니, 두 사람이 있었다.
 " 당신은 ... "
 " 난 양병석이라고, 이세상을 만든 사람이요. "        < 심심해서 작가를 나오게 해봤어. > " 도대체 왜 이런 세상을 만들었나요. "
 " 그건, 나도 모르오. "
 " 어쨌건 당신이 나를 이리로 데려온 것 아니요. "
 " 그랬을수도 있고, 아닐수도 있고. "
 " 무슨소리야 ! "
 " 그랬을수도 있고, 아닐수도 있고. "
그는 계속 같은 소리만 반복했다.
        
        < 바보아니야 ? > " 당신같은 허접대기가 이세상을 창조했단 말이야 ! "
그는 울트라 초 하이퍼 필살기를 써서 양병석을 없애 버렸다.        < 현란하게 펼쳐지는 주인공의 필살기.. 우왕~ 그래두
        내가 죽다니, 조금 억울한데 ? 나중에 이녀석을 죽이는
        소설이나 쓸까 ? 복수의 칼날을.. >그리고, 세상은 그렇게 끝났다.        < 이상한 내글도 끝났어. >
