 성공했다.. ^^;
내글을 씹어보았다.
나의지구님이 쓴
음유시인 그래피티에게 충격을 받은것도 있었다.
 ' 나보다 먼저 하다니.. --; '
어쨌든 재밌다.
밑에 글은 똑같이 쓰고 나서도 후회를 했는데.
별로 후회가 안된다.
쓰는동안, 내글을 내가 씹어서, 내가 스트레스가 풀렸나보다..
음냐.. 역시 보는 사람은 없겠지.
평가하는 사람도..
난 상관않는다.
했다는데 성취감을 느낀다.가끔은 제정신이 아닌척 하는건 정말로 재밌는 일이다.They were about to engage in their final battle.
 "Die!"
Soon, the hero's ultimate move was shouted, and the Demon King died. In the end, they brought peace to the entire world. However, the young hero was tough.
 On the spot, he ripped off the girl's top. Then, caressing her chest, he took off her skirt.         <It's not fun if it's not lewd, right? For those perverted readers.>Then the young man, 'Lewd, lewd, lewd,'         <But the author is still afraid of the public ethics committee and the YWCA ajummas.>said while working hard.
 "Finally, I've become your real husband. I've become the father of your child."
 "Oh my. I think I'm pregnant."
The girl said.
 "I've known that for 120 years."
 "No. Then you were hiding that from me?"
 "What do you mean I was hiding something?"        <No matter how I look at it, the conversation is strange...>The girl's belly swelled up.         <Her belly swells up really fast...>The unbearable young man ripped open the girl's belly. Her blood splattered across the Demon King's castle, and the young man frantically rummaged through her belly to pull out his child.
 "Is it a son? Or a daughter?"
It was the girl.
 "It's a son."
The child had no limbs yet, and its entire body was soaked in the girl's blood. The young man handed the child to the girl.
 "Oh, how pretty."        <What's pretty about a bloody, limbless fetus! The heroine sure can say such things after her belly was ripped open.>The girl, holding the child, said.
 "This is our hope."        <He's really going all the way with this.> "Is that so?"
 "Look, at the rising sun over there, now it's this child's world."
The shining sun in the distance illuminated the young man's path.        <The ending should always be hopeful. From below, it's the epilogue, right?>Another 70 years passed, and the young man grew old and died.        <Everyone dies.>On his way to heaven, he discovered a strange-looking black hole.
He entered the hole.
 And there were two people.
 "You are..."
 "I'm Yang Byeong-seok, the one who created this world."        <I brought the author out because I was bored.> "Why on earth did you create such a world?"
 "I don't know that either."
 "Anyway, didn't you bring me here?"
 "Maybe, maybe not."
 "What are you talking about!"
 "Maybe, maybe not."
He kept repeating the same thing.
        
        <Isn't he an idiot?> "You mean a nobody like you created this world!"
He used his ultra-super-hyper ultimate move to eliminate Yang Byeong-seok.        <The protagonist's dazzling ultimate move... Wow~ Still, it's a bit unfair that I died, isn't it? Should I write a novel later where I kill this guy? The blade of revenge...>And so, the world ended.        <My strange writing has also ended.>

"Bluebird 23! Ready for takeoff. Please proceed to the runway."
From the speaker in the small, cabin-like plastic room, a woman's voice flowed out. A woman in her early twenties, dressed in a military uniform of olive drab, who had been lying on the bed, sat up. However, she seemed somewhat listless. She tied up her long, black hair, picked up the helmet next to the bed, opened the door, and stepped outside.

Everyone she met as she walked greeted her with bright faces, waving or patting her shoulder as they passed. They consistently smiled, wished her luck, or offered words of encouragement, saying she would do well. But her face remained unbright.

She walked with a click-clack sound down a long, dim corridor. The place she arrived at was a runway room where only one aircraft was prepared. A woman with a sergeant's rank, who looked younger than her, handed her a pen and a file.
"Lieutenant, this is the only remaining runway and intact aircraft. This will be your last flight. Please write down the flight date."
On the file, she wrote a few words: "April 7, 2032, Bluebird 23, Lieutenant Kim Yu-ri, Runway Number 2301C."
The female sergeant took the file, smiled sweetly, and said, "I've only been here for two weeks. When will I become as cool as you, Lieutenant?"
Lieutenant Kim Yu-ri let out a small laugh.
"Don't overdo it. It's okay if you don't."

The lieutenant sat in the aircraft's seat. She put on her helmet and adjusted the small microphone attached to it. Then, with practiced skill, she flipped the main switch of the aircraft. The instruments glowed with a bright light.
"Lieutenant. Please check the instruments."
An older officer's voice came through the helmet. As if she had done it countless times, she checked the instruments, flipping each switch.
"Engine 1 output check. Engine 2 output check. Afterburner check. Fuselage status check. Weaponry check... Check complete."
After her tedious and complex check was finished, a response came through the helmet.
"Good luck, Lieutenant."
"What we're doing is the right thing, isn't it?"
Lieutenant Yu-ri asked softly. Her voice made the listener feel something moist and heavy.
"Yes. It will be. Yu-ri, you are our last hope. The one who can turn the tide of the war..."
Somehow, the officer's voice also sounded uncertain.
"Heh heh."
With the lieutenant's light laugh, the aircraft's glass canopy closed, followed by the metallic secondary cover. The inside of the aircraft became dark, with only the instruments visible.
"Activating infrared hood."
The view ahead brightened. Although what was projected before her eyes was sent by the aircraft's camera, the field of vision was much wider than what she could see with her naked eye, making it easier for combat. The female sergeant's voice from earlier came through the helmet again.
"Bluebird 23! Please confirm launch gas pressure."
"Gas pressure is sufficient."
"Then, proceeding to takeoff."
With a "KWAANG~" sound, pressure was applied.
Lieutenant Kim Yu-ri gripped the control stick, enduring the pressure on her body.
As the pressure eased, Yu-ri looked at the rear of the aircraft through the camera that served as the aircraft's eyes. From the desolate, half-destroyed base, black smoke billowed as if sending her off.
"Course south-southwest 23 degrees, maintaining flight path. Climbing to 2000 feet."
"We must cut off communication from now on, Lieutenant. I wish you a safe journey. *Click*"
Yu-ri pulled the control stick forward. The aircraft soared into the sky like a swallow, responding to her subtle movements.
The small vibration of the stick felt during flight was already a familiar sensation in her hands.
So many sorties, flights, this engine sound, this unbearable pressure... how familiar it all feels to me? Bluebird 23... Bluebird... Yes. Oppa said it was a bird symbolizing peace. Oppa...

In Yu-ri's ears, she heard the childhood voice of her beloved older brother, Hyun-gyu.
Before she knew it, Yu-ri was running. Blue sky... blue hill...
"Hurry up, Yu-ri! I found a wonderful place!"
A small boy was running. Behind him, a slightly smaller and younger girl was breathlessly chasing him, but it was clearly too much for her.
"Hyun-gyu oppa. Wait for me~"
"We're almost there."
Hyun-gyu stopped only when he reached the tree at the top of the hill, its large branches spread towards the sky. Yu-ri, gasping for breath, finally caught up with Hyun-gyu.
"Huff huff. That's not fair. Running ahead like that."
"Look over there~!"
Hyun-gyu pointed down the hill.
"Wow~ I can see our whole town!"
Yu-ri wiped the sweat from her face and exclaimed with a smile.
"If you climb this tree, you'll see even better."
Hyun-gyu climbed the tree.
"Come on up!"
"No."
Yu-ri plopped down at the base of the tree, looking sulky.
"Why?"
Hyun-gyu said, steadying himself on a large branch.
"Why climb up there? It's dangerous."
"Heh~ Yu-ri's scared, aren't you?"
"No, I'm not."
Yu-ri stuck out her tongue at Hyun-gyu.
"Can't be helped."
Hyun-gyu jumped down from the tree.
Then he lay down at the base of the tree, using his arm as a pillow. He stared intently at the sky, obscured by the branches.
"What are you looking at?"
"It feels good when I do this."
Yu-ri then imitated Hyun-gyu's actions.
The sky Yu-ri looked up at was covered by leaves. But it wasn't completely covered. The sunlight and sky peeking through the leaves occasionally sparkled like jewels.
"It's like jewels..."
Yu-ri murmured with a gentle smile.
"Huh? What is?"
"Up there, I mean."
"Yu-ri, you should be a poet when you grow up. You're so sentimental."
Yu-ri didn't answer, but squinted her eyes slightly, as if closing them, and looked up.
"It looks even brighter this way."
"What?"
Hyun-gyu also imitated her action.
"I don't know..."
Just then, a "KWAANG" sound, as if tearing eardrums, echoed.
Yu-ri found the sound unpleasant, as if it was ruining the quiet spring atmosphere. But Hyun-gyu reacted to the sound, jumping up and looking far into the sky.
"Oh, it's a KF-43!"
Hyun-gyu exclaimed happily.
"What's that?" Yu-ri asked, sitting up.
"It's the name of a new fighter jet. Mach 2.7, and its bombing capacity is amazing..."
"Pfft, what's so amazing about that?"
Yu-ri lay back down, and this time closed her eyes as if to smell the spring breeze.
"I'm going to be a pilot. A fighter pilot. I want to fly coolly through the sky. While crushing villains."
"Villains? Who are the villains you're talking about, Hyun-gyu oppa?"
"What? That's..."
When Hyun-gyu didn't answer, Yu-ri opened her eyes.
Suddenly, the dazzling sunlight streaming through the trees made Yu-ri's small eyes close in surprise. And she felt a soft sensation on her cheek, different from the wind. Yu-ri was startled by the feeling and jumped up. Then, with a flushed face, she looked at Hyun-gyu's face, who was pretending not to notice and only looking at the sky.
"Because you're so pretty."
Yu-ri stood up without a word, punched Hyun-gyu's back as he sat, and walked down the hill with a sulky look.
"Ow ow ow~ Hey! Yu-ri! Are you mad?"
Yu-ri kept walking without looking back.
"Hey! I'm sorry! I won't do it again next time."
But Yu-ri, who was walking down the hill with her back to Hyun-gyu, was actually smiling. Deep down, she was happy. Yu-ri also liked Hyun-gyu. She just wanted to act this way.
Yu-ri suddenly stopped, turned around, and looked at that tree. Hyun-gyu was standing under the tree, shouting, and when Yu-ri looked at him, he ran towards her.
Yu-ri looked at the greenery swaying pleasantly in the wind, as if singing something.
Just then, a few small birds flew up into the blue sky from the tree Hyun-gyu was running from.
Yu-ri watched the birds until they disappeared from her sight.
"Sorry, Yu-ri. Don't be mad."
Hyun-gyu, who had run up panting, apologized.
But Yu-ri's gaze was still fixed in the direction where the birds had disappeared.
"What are you looking at?"
"I'm going to call that tree the 'Singing Tree'."
Yu-ri said, her gaze fixed on the spot.
"What?"
"I saw birds. Beautiful birds flying towards the sun... From the singing tree, those birds must be the tree's song."
"Is she talking nonsense again?"
Yu-ri stared intently at Hyun-gyu. Yu-ri placed her palm on her head and drew her hand towards Hyun-gyu as if measuring height.
"Lower yourself a bit. To here."
"What?"
"Then you'll see. Your eye level doesn't match mine, so you can't see it."
Hyun-gyu bent his knees slightly.
"Where am I supposed to look?"
"There."
Yu-ri pointed to the tree from before.
"The tree is singing."
"What song?"
"A song of peace, a song of hope."
"What are you talking about?"
Then, instead of answering, Yu-ri kissed Hyun-gyu's cheek, which was now at her eye level.
"That's for earlier!"
Yu-ri cried out and skipped down the hill.
"Hey! You!"
Hyun-gyu shouted after Yu-ri as she went down the hill, and soon Hyun-gyu also started running down the hill.

Before Yu-ri's eyes, rugged valleys unfolded. Valleys... Yu-ri lowered her altitude. Then she began a perilous flight through the crevices of the valley rocks. Yu-ri checked her weaponry on the instruments. Then, when a certain weapon appeared on the display, she stopped checking.
A terrifying experimental bomb, still without a name... How many people would it kill? Is what I'm doing right? Yu-ri recalled a shuddering memory. Combat... war... Why did I end up doing this? I was just following Hyun-gyu oppa...

Before she knew it, Yu-ri was riding in a combat vessel with Hyun-gyu. Although she said "with," their seats were actually completely different. Because of the metallic secondary cover, she couldn't see anything except what the machine displayed, and their respective systems

To ensure complete focus, even her comrades were out of sight. Yuri sat in the back seat, in charge of one of the rotating turrets responsible for the aircraft's defensive functions, as well as the system.

Yuri pressed one eye to the infrared scope, which resembled a submarine periscope, and shouted into her helmet's microphone.
"Oppa! Lower the nose a bit!"
Hyun-gyu skillfully lowered the nose.
"Yuri! A fighter is coming in at 3 o'clock, 15-degree angle! Please!"
"Okay! Got it!"
Yuri fixed the turret's direction onto the fighter with the stick in her hand. As soon as the word 'lock' appeared on the infrared scope, Yuri pressed the red button on the stick.
'Thrummm'
A low vibration was felt as the Vulcan cannon on Yuri's aircraft unleashed fire, and the enemy aircraft instantly turned into a fireball and plummeted.
"Well done, Yuri!"
"Are we still far from the target?"
"Almost there. Let's just hold on a little longer. Hang in there, Black Eagle!"
"I don't like that name. Black Eagle... Hmph. What's 'black'? I hate black."
"Hmph. What's wrong with it? It's cool. What about our squadron's losses?"
Yuri replied in a somber voice.
"Only about half left."
"Hmph... Those bastards!"
"But, are they like us

I collapsed and lost consciousness due to the scorching sun and desert wind.

Yuri continued to fly through the valley.
What was I then? That sight... Honestly, I was so scared I peed my flight suit. My brother's head was half-blown off, and the inside of the airship was drenched in blood. I was terrified by that sight. He didn't feel like the brother I loved. War... Is that what it was? My brother told me he loved me until the very end, and his hands never let go of the controls, even as he died, safely crash-landing for me. But I just relied on him. How much pain must he have been in at the moment of death? For me... He must have found it so hard to say a single word in that condition...
But I ran away from that spot... just because the sight was horrible, scary... Hyun-gyu oppa, I'm sorry.

I lost consciousness in that desert and had a dream. A long dream, the death of Hyun-gyu oppa, which became an unbearable sorrow for me.
Did he fly away as a bird?
The hot desert... its light dried me out. Slowly... The sun was cruel, and I no longer had the strength to resist its cruelty.
When I opened my eyes again, I was in a small hut...

Yuri slowly opened her eyes.
'I wasn't dead...'
Yuri looked around.
She was neatly laid on a small wooden bed. The house was decorated simply, not at all luxurious, in fact, it looked very outdated and poor. It seemed to belong to one of the desert inhabitants. Outside was a tropical desert. But there was something that surprised Yuri. A framed picture hanging in a corner of the house... The flag of the enemy nation was in that frame.
Yuri found her gun placed within reach on the bed.
As Yuri quickly stood up to grab the gun, the thin blanket covering her fell off.
Yuri was surprised once again to find herself naked. After checking that the gun was loaded, Yuri hid it in her bosom and lay back down, pretending to be asleep in bed. After some time, someone entered. Yuri subtly opened her eyes a crack and peeked at him. He was a frail old man in a worn enemy uniform, coughing as if he were ill. He put down something he was carrying, then sat at an old desk and began to write something. Yuri quietly got up, careful not to be discovered, and aimed at his head.
"Click," she released the safety pin of the gun.
But then, the old man, completely unfazed, spoke in a low voice without even turning around.
"You're awake, young lady."
His voice was rather solemn, a voice that spoke of long experience, or perhaps one that transcended the world. Yuri was surprised by his composure, which was almost intimidating, but she pressed him, still aiming her gun.
"Why did you bring me here? Where is this?!"
But again, his voice showed no agitation whatsoever.
"Are you going to shoot me with that gun? It doesn't matter much, I've lived long enough anyway...
To think I rescued you from the desert... Young people nowadays don't know gratitude."
"You're an enemy soldier!"
"Hmph... That again. Such things are meaningless, whether friend or foe... Only war exists. *Cough cough*"
Just then, a young boy entered the hut.
Yuri quickly turned her gun towards the boy and aimed. The old man then pleaded with Yuri, his voice slightly agitated.
"Don't shoot that child... He has done nothing wrong..."
However, the child also paid no mind to the gun aimed at him.
"Grandpa, I hung out the clothes."
And he carefully walked towards his grandfather. The boy's eyes were closed. He was blind... The child couldn't see.
"This child cannot see... And, young lady, I've placed clothes under that shelf over there, so please put them on. It's embarrassing for this old man to see you like this."
Yuri hesitated for a moment, then turned the gun back towards the old man and checked under the shelf. There was a set of enemy military uniform there.
"Why? Do you dislike it because it's from the enemy nation?"
Yuri picked up the clothes and slowly put them on. While her vision was momentarily obscured by putting on the top, Yuri felt a hand snatch the gun from her hand.
His hand was surprisingly skilled for a frail old man who coughed.
"You dirty bastard! You tricked me well!"
Yuri finished dressing and spat out harsh words. But the old man, holding the gun in one hand, sat at his desk, looking at Yuri with an inscrutable smile, and said,
"It's a pity, such harsh words from a pretty young lady. I didn't trick you. I just felt that a young lady who would aim a gun at a child so casually was dangerous. And one more thing, if I were truly an enemy soldier, I wouldn't tell you to put on clothes and cover your eyes with the top."
The old man put the gun in a desk drawer and locked it with a small key. Then he coughed as if he was about to vomit everything in the world.
"Grandpa, is the sister awake?"
The child clung to his grandfather and asked.
"Yes, yes. She's awake. Would you like to go play outside for a bit?"
The child quietly walked back outside. The old man stood up from the desk, went to the dining table, pulled out a chair, and looked at Yuri, saying,
"Now that you've recovered, please sit here, young lady."
Yuri sat down, still with a wary look in her eyes. The old man brought out some food.
"You must be hungry after lying down for so long, have some."
After a long silence, deep in thought, she hesitated for a moment and then spoke.
"I think I misunderstood, I apologize."
"Haha, if I were an enemy soldier, I would have woken you up and subjected you to harsh torture by now."
Yuri ate her food and asked,
"Where is this place?"
"About 2 km from the northern front... The battle is still raging in the valley over there. This place won't be safe for you either, young lady."
"The nearest friendly base must be 30 km away... Phew~"
"Take your time and rest."
The old man got up and went back to his old desk, sat down, and began to write something again. Yuri got up and went outside. A slight dizziness forced her to lean against the doorway for a moment.
Outside was the hot desert light... And under a tree sat the boy from earlier. Yuri steadied herself and slowly walked over to sit beside the child.
"What are you doing?"
"Listening to sounds."
"What sounds?"
"The sound of the wind, the sound of birds, the sound of people, the sound of the sun, and many more."
Yuri also closed her eyes. Yuri didn't hear any particular sounds. All she could hear in her ears were the distant gunshots and cannon fire. Surely, a battle was raging somewhere... Yuri opened her eyes and said to the boy,
"Hoho, you should be a poet when you grow up. You're so sentimental."
Yuri said this out loud but couldn't remember who had said it before.
"A poet? My grandpa is one."
"Your grandpa is a poet?"
"Something similar. A writer, I guess? He writes poems and fun novels too."
Yuri had many conversations with the child. Being with the innocent child, Yuri seemed to forget the long war, and she learned a lot about the old man and the child.
Though it was only for a short while...
Yuri was spending time indoors, having pleasant conversations with the child.
Just then, the old man came into the house.
"You're playing well with my child."
"He's a very kind child."
"Yes. Except for his eyes. I write words that become his eyes. To show him the world... That's my only joy."
"Since when have the child's eyes been like that?"
"War... It was because of the war. *Cough cough... cough*"
The old man coughed violently, then pulled out a cigarette from a small, worn pouch and put it in his mouth. After lighting it with a small match, he exhaled a puff of smoke. Yuri had been in this house for almost a week, but this was the first time she saw the old man smoke.
"Grandpa. Don't smoke. That's why you keep coughing."
The blind child, somehow knowing, ran to his grandfather, snatched the cigarette, and threw it away.
"Yes. Yes, you're right. *Cough*"
"Young lady, what do you think of this war that divides us into friend and foe?"
"........."
Yuri said nothing.
"It's all futile. Both friend and foe... That flag is just hung there because soldiers sometimes visit. I'd rather hang the pictures that child draws...
War only drives young people, full of vigor and love for their country, to their deaths, and nothing else. *Cough, cough*"
The old man paused his speech due to coughing.
"I was once a soldier too. A special forces soldier, at that... Hundreds of people lost their lives by my hand. I would infiltrate stealthily and slit throats. Then I'd get paid, and I thought I was doing something for my country... But no. The writer in me wouldn't let me be. Tormented by my conscience, I eventually returned to my hometown. On the way back, I saw this young child crying in the arms of a woman whose body was half-destroyed by a roadside bomb. And so, *cough*... I brought this child and raised him. The child was already blind by then.
I've seen many deaths. You were a pilot, weren't you? Then, you probably didn't see people die directly... You just had to press a button. But it's the same. No, your airship might have resented you, airships were created from human dreams... to ascend to the sky... But in the face of war, all dreams become powerless...
Is this war right? *Cough cough*... I've lost everything. My purpose... I realized that and now I live like this. I will never leave here again. Even though it's a small village with hardly any people."
"...."
Yuri still said nothing, and the old man also stopped speaking, only continuing to cough. Only Hyun-gyu's voice filled Yuri's mind.
'I'm going to defeat the villains.'
'They're not even human. How cruel and evil they are. Do you remember how they dismembered Lieutenant Yoo, who escaped from his airship, and sent him to our base recently?'
A few days later, Yuri had no choice but to leave that place. Soldiers

Because they had arrived...
Grandfather silently handed the gun back to Yuri, and the child, uncharacteristically, sent Yuri off quietly with a choked voice. Had the war made even a child so remarkably restrained?

Yuri saw the valley coming to an end. The city... a factory located in the heart of the city... The objective was to blow up that factory, which produced combat vessels with terrifying speed.
This mission had to be given to Yuri. All nearby bases had been destroyed. The base Yuri was at was also destroyed, but whether by chance or fate, one combat vessel and one runway remained. Immediately, this terrifying bomb, which was under experimentation, was loaded onto the remaining aircraft, and the mission was entrusted to Yuri.
The reason for entrusting it was simple. There were no pilots left at the base. Only about 10 combat vessels had survived the last dam explosion, and even those were all killed trying to defend the base during the attack, leading to the destruction of most of the base.
Yuri only learned this fact after returning to the base.
And during the briefing, she learned about this astonishing bomb.
First, an enormous explosion like a nuclear bomb... and then the outpouring neutron beams... Of course, these neutron beams are invisible but possess immense power. Tiny neutron particles are fired, pulverizing the molecular structure of nearby objects. Neutrons collide with atomic nuclei, breaking them apart, thereby annihilating the molecules themselves...
Beyond that, even the creators themselves didn't know about the bomb. What effects it would have, only that it possessed immense power. Yuri's mission was simple: approach the factory as stealthily as possible, drop the bomb on it, and then escape the area as quickly as possible.
The bomb's power might even be capable of annihilating the aircraft she was flying. There was no other way than to ascend to the safest altitude or flee far away... Of course, that was only if she managed to drop the bomb safely. The enemy's high-performance combat vessels and the city's anti-aircraft network certainly wouldn't stand idly by.

As Yuri's combat vessel appeared in the city sky, emergency bells rang, and the city's air defense networks began to activate. Yuri gripped the control stick even tighter.
‘It's up to me. The tide of our side... But what does it mean? The people of this city... many of them won't be soldiers...’ Is this war right? I've lost everything. Grandfather's gruff voice and his cough echoed in Yuri's ears.
The radar began to beep, emitting warning sounds. Objects were approaching at Mach 5. They started spitting fire along with the ground-based anti-aircraft network. Yuri's Bluebird began to weave through the cannonballs streaking across the sky with dazzling maneuvers. In Yuri's mind, only the target was visible.
Yuri's hands moved as if possessed. Hyun-gyu's ghostly skill came to Yuri's mind...
‘Is Oppa protecting me...? Oppa, watch over me. I might not be as good as you, but I can fly well too...’
Then, with a thud, she felt one side of the fuselage tilt. It seemed to have been hit by anti-aircraft fire, and one of the twin engines went out. The speed was no longer what it had been. Soon, another shot hit the aircraft. With a hiss, half of one infrared hood went out, severely narrowing her vision. The Bluebird seemed to be losing its capabilities one by one.
Feeling that the damaged infrared hood, which narrowed her vision far more than normal, was no longer helpful, Yuri removed the secondary metal cover. The dazzling sunlight, along with the blue sky, stimulated Yuri's eyes. Then she saw an aircraft passing by her own. Incredible speed... seasoned skill...
A clear gray skull mark was emblazoned on the side of that aircraft. It relentlessly pursued Yuri, as if taunting her. Yuri had shaken off most others, but with only one engine now, that particular aircraft was not easy to evade. No, in fact, that aircraft's skill was so formidable that there would have been no effective way to escape it even if Yuri's plane had been fully functional.
Yuri soon became enraged at the aircraft that seemed to be toying with her. Perhaps it was the thought that it was Hyun-gyu's enemy.
The target was already close at hand. The enemy aircraft then carefully stuck to Yuri's tail, as if determined not to let her escape. It seemed intent on shooting her down.
‘As if I'd be shot down by Hyun-gyu Oppa's enemy.’
Yuri suddenly slowed down and performed a steep dive. She was trying to imitate a technique Hyun-gyu used. The enemy aircraft lost its target due to Yuri's maneuver. Yuri tried to pull up the nose again, but it wasn't easy. She kept plummeting towards the ground.
‘Please... Bluebird. Is it because of the single engine...?’
She narrowly, by a hair's breadth, soared back into the sky. Yuri let out a small laugh, thinking how happy Hyun-gyu Oppa would be if he knew she had pulled off that maneuver.
The enemy aircraft quickly turned its nose and began to approach Yuri head-on at tremendous speed. It was clearly targeting Yuri. Its Vulcan cannon spat fire.
‘Bang, bang’ sparks flew inside Yuri's aircraft.
Yuri felt a searing pain in her lower left abdomen.
But Yuri, disregarding the pain, placed her hand on the red lever of the control stick and pressed it firmly. Soon, something flew out with a whoosh.
The enemy aircraft easily evaded the object, as if it were trivial. However, its target was not the enemy aircraft. With a 'boom,' a massive explosion erupted. The enemy aircraft, flying low near the factory, was engulfed by the blast, bursting into flames and scattering into fragments with the fire.
That enormous explosion even sent a shockwave through Yuri's aircraft. The city was being engulfed by the explosion, which was creating an incredibly massive cloud. A mushroom cloud... a cloud of death that forms when temperatures instantly rise to thousands of degrees.
Yuri touched the painful area. Something sticky was on her hand.
‘Blood... Did I really turn this city into a city of blood and death? With my own hands... How can I atone? Isn't my sin too great to justify it as revenge for Hyun-gyu Oppa?’
Yuri quickly pulled the control stick, raising the nose towards the sky. Then something came into view along with the blue sky. Sunlight...

Suddenly, Yuri was startled and closed her eyes.
She remembered seeing it somewhere. Yes... where could it have been?
‘Because you're so pretty.’ The singing tree... beneath that tree... sunlight... playing with Oppa... Oppa's first kiss... beneath that tree that looked like a jewel. Perhaps that jewel was a star. And so it might have fallen in a shower and landed in my arms...
Was it a sad memory... or perhaps a happy one...? Yuri's mind grew hazy, perhaps due to the heavy bleeding.
Where am I really? The reason I'm here now... I even wanted to become a poet, just like Oppa said... Yuri turned her head and looked back.
A colossal mushroom cloud was rising. The singing tree... That cloud wasn't an ugly mushroom shape; in Yuri's eyes, the shape of the singing tree was superimposed upon it.
Yuri still raised the nose towards the sky.
Flying away. Like the song of the tree... We are like that... I am not alone.
Something was sparkling in Yuri's eyes. She didn't know why her tears were flowing. But Yuri was flying. Towards the sun, like the song of that tree...
One by one, memories came to Yuri's mind.
Many things... all of life... the joyful ones... Her love with Hyun-gyu, her childhood self, her happy and dream-filled high school days, Hyun-gyu's dashing appearance as a cadet, her own frightened self crying when she first rode a plane,
Her life of nearly 20 years, her old humble dream of wanting to live a happy, ordinary life, having children and loving. And the black war... it interfered with Yuri's life.
Beautiful old memories... many people who were with her... The blind child she parted ways with, whose name she didn't even know. That child born of war. But that child had a bright smile and clear eyes. Young eyes... clear eyes. Eyes that faced the war...
I... Ah... Am I merely flying away...? If so, where to?
Yuri took off her helmet. Her long hair flowed down. The Bluebird's wingtips trembled delicately, like a bird's.
That nameless bomb might be sad. Because humans made it... And so, perhaps it resents humans. That it takes so many lives...
The bomb was already emitting neutron beams. The Bluebird's fuselage was slowly thinning and disappearing from the back, like the Little Mermaid dissolving into sea foam. Like Yuri's tears...
And so, the song of the singing tree was flying towards the sky, towards the sun. Yearning for something...
In a small desert village, a blind boy under the shade of a tree was looking up at the sky, listening intently as if he heard something. Yuri's song...

titleEn: The Glass Bead Game (1995) - A Short Story / Creative Work
contentEn:
On a warm spring day, a boy and a girl, who look about seven years old, are walking hand in hand. A warm breeze is gently blowing. The girl suddenly sees azaleas by the roadside, lets go of the boy's hand, and runs towards them.
The girl starts picking flowers. The boy sits down in a clover patch, picking clover blossoms and making something. The girl soon returns to the boy with a handful of flowers.
"Look at this. I picked so many!" The girl smiles brightly.
"They're pretty," the boy says, glancing at them with apparent disinterest.
"What are you doing?"
The girl asks curiously, but the boy doesn't answer, engrossed in his creation. Soon, the boy speaks.
"It's done."
"What is?"
"Do you like me?"
The girl's face turns red with shyness as she replies, "Yes."
"Then, let's get married."
"Married? What's that?"
"It's like this. You're the mom, and I'm the dad."
"Oh. It's like playing house."
"How do we do it?"
"I saw my uncle get married the other day. Come here."
The girl approaches.
"Groom Lee Kyung-min, do you take Kim Yu-na as your bride? Yes."
The boy asks and answers himself, then says to the girl,
"Bride Kim Yu-na, do you take Lee Kyung-min as your groom? Yes."
The girl looks at the boy as if he's strange.
"You have to answer," the boy chides.
"Yes." "Not 'yes,' you have to say 'I do.'"
"I do."
"Give me your hand." The girl offers her hand.
The boy puts a ring made of clover blossoms on the girl's hand.
"Wow~ It's pretty. Did you make it?"
"Yes. And take this too. This is a wedding gift. Originally, you should give me one too..."
The boy rummages in his pocket, pulls out three glass marbles, and hands them to the girl.
The glass marbles, catching the sunlight, sparkled like tiny suns.
"I don't have anything to give you. Oh, I'll give you this."
The girl takes a hairpin from her hair and hands it to the boy.
"Is it over now?" the girl asks.
"No." "Then?"
"We have to do something called a kiss." "What's that? It's really complicated."
"Come closer. And close your eyes."
"Okay." The girl closes her eyes.
The boy gently kisses the girl and then pulls away.
The girl opens her eyes in surprise.
"What was that? Was that a kiss? Why do we do it?"
"I don't know. Adults do it. Let's go down to the train tracks over there."
"No. Mom said not to go there because it's dangerous."
"It's okay. Come on." The boy takes the girl's hand and leads her.
The boy and girl went down to the train tracks in front of a tunnel below the road. The boy puts his ear to the rail.
"Do you hear anything?" The girl asks, putting her ear to the rail.
As soon as the girl put her ear down, she heard the sound of train wheels.
The girl jumped up in surprise.
"Kyung-min. The train is coming." The boy kept his ear to the rail.
"Kyung-min. Get up." The boy didn't get up and kept his ear there.
The sound of the train was now audible even to the girl, who wasn't listening to the rail.
"Kyung-min. Get up. Hurry." The girl said in a trembling voice.
Still, the boy didn't get up.
The train emerged from the dark tunnel, a massive presence.
"Kyung-min! Get up!" The girl cried out, bursting into tears.
Only then did the boy slowly get up. Just then, the massive train roared past. The girl's crying seemed to be swallowed by the train's noise; only the train's sound could be heard. Soon, the train passed, and only the boy and girl remained.
The boy gazed blankly in the direction the train had disappeared. The girl was still sniffling.
"Why are you crying?" The boy asks, but the girl doesn't answer.
"I wasn't going to get up until you called me three times."
The girl wipes away her tears and retorts,
"Idiot."
"Why am I an idiot?" The boy said in an angry voice.
"Anyway, you're an idiot!"
The girl got up and ran away. The boy stared blankly and bewilderedly in that direction. When the girl disappeared from sight, the boy also trudged home.
It's good to be back in my hometown. The semester ended, and I came to be with my mother. University certainly seems more comfortable. In high school, all I knew was studying like crazy, but now I have this leisure... The sky is blue, and the rice paddies in the fields are fresh. It's much better here than that damned Seoul.
"Kyung-min. Dinner's ready."
My mother brings out dinner. My mother, who has lived for 20 years relying only on me.
My poor mother... I ate dinner and went for a walk.
Walking down the neighborhood street, my steps unconsciously stopped in front of a house.
Yu-na's house... She moved away when I was twelve.
How much I cried then...
But I also went up to Seoul a few months later to study.
Even now, I laugh when I think about it. The puppy love of little kids...
A magpie is crying in the persimmon tree in front of that house.
It's not morning, so why is it crying so much... They say a magpie crying means a welcome guest is coming... Huh, the magpie is funny. A guest at an empty house... I turned my steps back home. On the way home, a truck brushed past me. Why such reckless driving... I went home, watched TV, and then tried to sleep.

The sound of a magpie rings in my ears. Morning... Yes, it's morning.
They say morning is the beginning of everything... I got up groggily and went to the faucet to wash. After a few pumps, clear, cool water woke me up. I lathered my face with soap and rubbed it with water. Then, I heard someone's voice.
"Excuse me... Is anyone home?"
I heard my mother go out.
"Excuse me... Miss, what can I do for you?"
"Auntie. Don't you remember me?"
"Well... Who might you be?"
"I'm Kim Bok-dong's only daughter, who used to live nearby. I've moved back here and wanted to give you some rice cakes."
"Ah... The Kim family."
I was surprised. Kim Bok-dong?
I think I heard Yu-na mention it before. That he was her father...
I quickly wiped my face with a towel and ran to the door.
But she was already gone; the young lady wasn't there.
"Mom! Who was that young lady?"
"She's the Kim family's only daughter from before. Oh. That's right. I think you two were quite close..."
"It was Yu-na, right?" "Well. I don't quite remember the name?"
I went back to Yu-na's old house. People were busily coming and going at the house, which had looked abandoned, organizing moving boxes and tidying up the house.
I peered around, looking in. Then, thinking, "Why am I doing this?" I turned to leave. Just then, I heard my name called from behind me.
"Kyung-min! It is Kyung-min, isn't it?"
I turned around. And I saw Yu-na, who had already become a young woman, running towards me.
"I knew it. It is Kyung-min." Yu-na was panting a little even after a short run.
"How many years has it been?"
"Hmm... About ten years, I guess?"
Her mature appearance was truly beautiful.
She was so beautiful that it made my head spin. With her fair skin and gentle smile, she seemed utterly free of worldly worries. She and I talked about the past and recent times, and old feelings seemed to rekindle. Those feelings I thought were just childish puppy love... And so, we grew close again. The summer vacation passed by quickly and joyfully, and only a few days remained until it was time to return to Seoul.
I didn't want to lose her. She truly seemed like the most beautiful and best woman in the whole world.
So I decided to confess everything to her and met her. She and I walked down the road. The same road where we had made that shy promise when we were little. That day, Yu-na looked exceptionally angelic and pure white.
"Yu-na."
"Yes?"
"Do you remember the promise we made here?"
"What promise?" Yu-na replied as if she didn't remember.
"When we were seven. The promise we made then."
"I don't know..."
"I made you a ring out of clover blossoms and put it on your finger, and I asked you to marry me, remember?"
I took out a ring I had bought beforehand from my pocket.
Then I said,
"It's not expensive, but... I want to propose to you again."
Yu-na didn't say anything. She just kept her head bowed.
I was afraid of being rejected. Soon, Yu-na spoke in a trembling voice.
"No........" For a moment, I felt dizzy.
"Don't you love me?" My voice was trembling too.
"Yes! I don't love you."
Suddenly, my head throbbed, and through the sparkling sunlight, I thought I saw something glistening fall from beneath Yu-na's bowed face.
"What am I lacking? What, exactly?" I shouted in anger.
"You're not lacking anything!"
"Then, why?"
Then Yu-na lifted her face as if to say something. There were indeed tear stains on Yu-na's face. Yu-na tried to say something but then suddenly collapsed. I quickly caught Yu-na.
"Yu-na! Yu-na! Wake up!"
But Yu-na didn't open her eyes. I carried Yu-na on my back and ran to the nearest town. At that moment, my heart was filled with unspeakable sadness about Yu-na not loving me, and also with worry for Yu-na.

I see Yu-na's parents rushing in.
Yu-na's parents ask the nurse something and then enter Yu-na's hospital room.
A moment later, Yu-na's parents emerged from the hospital room, looking worried.
Yu-na's father approached me.
"Yu-na has woken up. Go in and see her."
I saw Yu-na's mother sobbing.
I entered Yu-na's hospital room quietly, imagining various things. Those imaginings only made me afraid. Yu-na was sitting on the bed.
Yu-na looked at me once, then deliberately avoided my gaze, looking at the ceiling, and in a trembling voice,

said.
"I didn't want to show you this side of me... I'm sorry about earlier.
I have a disease. They say it's leukemia.. I only have about a month left to live. I'm sorry. For making you feel that way, even though I knew I was going to die.."
"It's okay. When did it start?"
"I found out right before we moved. My father hoped that if I breathed the clean air of my hometown after hearing I was going to die, I might live a little longer, so we moved here."
Yuna's voice grew increasingly agitated.
"Then, please leave now. I want to be alone."
I opened the hospital room door and was about to leave when I asked Yuna.
"Do you really not love me?"
"I don't love you! I don't love you! What's the point of loving when I'm going to die soon!"
Yuna cried out as if reaffirming it to herself. I closed the hospital room door and left. Yuna's parents went back into the room.
Almost a month had passed since I returned from my hometown. But Yuna was still on my mind. So I was fiddling with the ring I had intended to give her in my studio apartment. I held the ring up to the sunlight from the window. The small ring shimmered with iridescent colors. Just like Yuna... Then I dropped the ring. The moment I reached out to pick it up, the phone rang.
"Hello?"
My mother's voice rang out.
"Kyungmin. It's your mom."
"Yes, Mom, what's wrong?"
"Are you doing well? Are you eating on time?"
"Yes. I'm doing well."
"Ah. It's nothing else. It's just that the Kim family suffered a bereavement the day before yesterday. And Mr. Kim specifically asked for you to be called..."
I dropped the receiver instantly.
"Kyungmin! Kyungmin!"
My mother's voice was ringing from the receiver.
I picked up the receiver again.
"What's wrong? Kyungmin. Are you okay?"
"Yes. Don't worry. I'll be down soon."
I was immersed in sadness the entire way back to my hometown.
When I arrived at Yuna's house, only a few friends who seemed to be Yuna's and her relatives were present. And in front of the folding screen, only Yuna's photo greeted me. Seeing that, my grief intensified, making it hard to control myself. I stepped out of the funeral home for a moment to calm my mind. Soon, the funeral bier arrived, and the procession began. The weather suddenly clouded over and grew dark.
At first, cremation was suggested, but Yuna's parents strongly opposed it, so in the end, a burial site was prepared. The funeral bier went to a nearby hill. That hill was next to the train tracks where I used to play as a child. The bier stopped at a spot with a good view of the train tracks and was lowered into the pit.
Yuna's father scooped a shovel of earth and threw it into the pit. Then he approached me with faltering steps.
"Young man. Thank you."
"Huh?" I was puzzled.
"For what you did for my daughter."
I just watched the workers cover the pit with soil.
"When she was first born, I was quite disappointed. Because she wasn't a son. My wife and I couldn't have any more children after that. I don't know why...
But then, the way she acted was so incredibly cute.
So we decided to be content with just her. That child was a treasure to us.
A treasure given by God. She was good at studying, and so clever that she would miraculously guess what I was thinking and try to please me. On top of that, she even got into that difficult university without a hitch."
"You must be sad. Because your daughter died..."

Again, dry sand welcomes the child and mother.
The mother gently puts the child down, smiling with relief.
The child stops crying at the sight of that smile.
However, the child's mother slowly collapses onto the sand. The child, startled, shakes her mother and bursts into tears again.
But the child feels themselves being shaken.
Cheolmin opened his eyes. Yerim was shaking him and waking him up, her voice choked with tears.
"Cheolmin, are you okay?"
Cheolmin sat up. The cockpit was lit by red emergency lights instead of bright illumination. Cheolmin felt a throbbing in his head. He touched his head, which hurt, and found blood on his hand.
"You hit your head on the instrument panel."
"What happened?"
"The prominence destroyed the Venus and hit Icarus. You injured your head from the impact."
"How long was I unconscious?"
"About 5 minutes... I was so worried."
Cheolmin looked out the window. Two fireballs were visible. The blue sun and the red-burning gate. And in the corner of the window, the half-burnt body of Icarus was visible.
"Oh no. The damage to Icarus is severe."
Cheolmin operated the computer, and a hologram of Icarus appeared.
Useless or destroyed parts were colored red. For a moment, Cheolmin showed a dark expression. But he soon returned to his original expression and said, "We'll have to abandon Icarus."
"Abandon Icarus?"
"Yes. It can't move. We'll have to use the Noah. First, let's treat the injuries."
Cheolmin went to the medical bay. Yerim followed without a word. Cheolmin skillfully bandaged his own head.
"By the way. Are you injured anywhere?" Cheolmin asked.
"Just a slight sprain in my wrist."
"Let me see." Cheolmin touched Yerim's wrist here and there.
"Ow... It hurts, be gentle."
"Here it is." Cheolmin looked for medicine for Yerim.

He gave it to her.
"Put this on."
"Are you... okay?" Yerim asked cautiously.
"What?" "The Venusho was destroyed."
"It's nothing."
Cheolmin said in a slightly trembling voice.
In truth, Cheolmin also wanted to cry his heart out. He had lost his mother when he was young, and now his father too, and he had a premonition that he too would have to follow that path.
On the cockpit computer, a hologram in the shape of Icarus, which Cheolmin hadn't turned off, was still on. The lounge, engine, wings, and water tank were painted red.
Cheolmin knew that if he couldn't fill the Noaho with water, only one person could escape via warp speed.
Cheolmin looked at Yerim for a moment. He thought Yerim was the prettiest among all the girls on Earth. Cheolmin hadn't seen a Korean girl since he was young. To Cheolmin, Yerim was special.
As a friend he now had to send away. As the first and last girl his age he was with. As the last living being by his side within tens of light-years, Yerim was special. Cheolmin grabbed Yerim's shoulder.
"What's wrong?" Yerim asked, puzzled.
"You. If I weren't here and you were left alone on this spaceship, what would you do?"
"What are you talking about?" Cheolmin suddenly hugged Yerim tightly.
Yerim was flustered and couldn't think of how to get away or what to say.
Cheolmin smelled his mother's embrace from Yerim. Cheolmin said in a trembling voice, "I'll protect you no matter what. You're really pretty. No, as pretty as my mom. She's not here now, but my mom was like you. I really like you. Since I first saw you. No, I don't even know if it's 'liking.' This feeling is new to me. For someone like me, stuck on a spaceship, it might be natural not to know."
Cheolmin let go of Yerim. Yerim's face was red.
"I'll give you this. This is all I have to give you."
Cheolmin put a cross necklace around Yerim's neck.
Yerim couldn't read the sadness in Cheolmin's sorrowful words.
"Let's go to the Noaho now." Cheolmin took Yerim to the Noaho.
"Stay right here and don't move. I'll get the logbook from the cockpit. Absolutely do not go outside the Noaho."
Cheolmin gave her earnest instructions, like a mother cautioning her child, and then left.
Cheolmin walked weakly towards the cockpit.
In the cockpit, Cheolmin took out a Space Letter from a cabinet in the corner.
Then he inserted the Space Letter into the computer and began recording.
"Hello? This is Icarusho, Earth affiliation. Due to the Prominence of the Gate, the Venusho and all its crew and passengers have died. I will read out the list of the deceased. Captain Park Kicheol... First Officer... Apprentice crewman Park Cheolmin."
Cheolmin called out his own name at the end.
"The Icarusho has also become inoperable due to the Prominence, and its water tank has been destroyed. Therefore, I am sending one girl on the Noaho. She is the sole survivor of the Icarusho. There is no one to hold accountable. If you absolutely need someone to blame, ask the company. The preliminary investigation was insufficient... I, too, meet my end here. All crew members have died. Anyway, please send Yerim safely to Earth. To all living people... Goodbye.."
Cheolmin launched the Space Letter into space.
The Space Letter oriented itself and soon became a beam of light, disappearing from sight into the depths of space.
"Hoo~" Cheolmin let out a deep sigh. Tears welled up in Cheolmin's eyes.
Cheolmin soon sat in the cockpit.
Then, after entering the Noaho's coordinates, he pressed the key labeled 'airrock V'.
When a green light appeared on the dashboard, he then pressed the key labeled 'fire I'.
Yerim was thinking about Cheolmin. It wasn't that Yerim had no interest in Cheolmin. Perhaps because he had only lived on a spaceship, he was a bit cold and blunt.
A poor child who grew up learning work under his father, without a mother.
But a child who seemed reliable and brave, Yerim somehow liked him.
Just then, the passage door between the Noaho and Icarusho hissed and then slammed shut with a thud.
Yerim was extremely surprised. Yerim pounded on the door and called out Cheolmin's name, but there was no answer. Yerim was scared and began to sob.
"Hoo-hoo-hoo."
The Noaho's vibration was felt. As if it were moving... Yerim went up to the observation deck on the upper floor of the Noaho. She could see the burning Gate, the cosmic scenery, and the Icarusho. The Icarusho was getting further and further away.
Cheolmin turned on the communicator. With a 'click,' the communication connected.
"Yerim." The Noaho's public address speaker rang out.
"Cheolmin. What happened?" Yerim cried out, her voice choked with tears.
"Now you have to go alone." "What do you mean?"
"The logbook is also on the Noaho. I told you before. If the Noaho isn't filled with water, warp speed can only carry one person. The Icarusho's water tank is destroyed. That's why I sent you."
"Then... hoo-hoo-hoo."
Yerim burst into tears. "Don't cry, Yerim."
But tears were also flowing from Cheolmin's eyes as he said these words.
"Then... was that your last goodbye? *sob sob*"
Yerim said, crying. "Yes. But those words were sincere. I like you."
"Isn't there another way? Like asking for help from a nearby spaceship?"
"No. Even if there were, the Gate wouldn't wait until then."
"Why do you have to die? Why are you so calm? Aren't you afraid of dying? If you die, your future dreams and hopes will disappear... *sob sob*"
"Don't worry, death isn't the end. I'll be waiting for you in heaven.."
Already, the Icarusho was out of sight, and only the Gate was visible as a tiny speck.
"What if God doesn't exist? He might not!"
Now, even the Gate looked like nothing more than a twinkling star.
"The distance must have grown quite far already. Seeing how long it takes to hear your voice. And don't say such things. God exists! No, He *must* exist!"
Cheolmin was speaking as if admonishing himself.
"Still... *sob sob*"
Yerim kept sobbing. "But you idiot. If you die, if you die... *boo hoo*"
Now Yerim cried out loud.
"Heh heh, I guess I'm not a good man after all... seeing as I'm making a girl cry... Don't cry. Yerim, time is almost up. I'm going to cut the communication. Crying won't solve anything. When you get home, forget about someone like me completely. I've transmitted your homework to your home. I want to talk more... but I don't want you to hear my last voice... Goodbye...."
'Click.' The communication was cut. "Cheolmin..."
Cheolmin knelt down and began to pray.
He was afraid of why he had to die, and he also resented God.
But he had no choice but to accept the fact that it had to be.
As it was the end, he desperately wanted to cling to God. Cheolmin felt a sudden heat.
And then..........
Yerim was looking at the Gate planet. She was looking at one of the twinkling stars, which appeared as nothing more than a star. At that moment, that star shone so brightly that it couldn't be compared to any other star.
A brilliant light illuminated the dark universe. A star like the one the Magi saw 2000 years ago.
That star was a special star to Yerim. The star of Icarus... Cheolmin's star...
Yerim tightly clutched the cross Cheolmin had given her.
"Yes. God must exist. For your sake, He must exist. If God doesn't exist, it would be too unfair to you."
The stars were slowly moving towards the front of the Noaho, drawing tails.

The airplane's engine is turning with a rattling sound.
The chilly night air... I want to lie in it and just go on like this.
The lights below, visible occasionally... How long have I flown this sky...
The years spent in the sky... I have flown this sky for a full 40 years.
Following the designated route... The smell of airplane fuel welcomes me.
This airplane, now worn out like my own body...
How much joy it shared with me... carrying people's dreams,
carrying people's happiness, my companion who always flew through the sky.
Though it was something I always yearned for, looking at the blue sky as a child...
What is left now? I want to ask myself.

Finally, the runway lights are visible. The runway I've always landed on for 40 years...
The wheels touch the runway. A slight vibration is felt, and the plane stops.
"Hello, Mr. Wilskin!"
"Oh, yes. Samson. What is it?"
"How have you been feeling lately?"
"I'm always the same. My heart's a bit off. That's all..."
"You should consider your age now. Take it easy. Retirement isn't far off..."
"Yes... All I've gained here in 40 years is frailty. I know my body best. I'm still alright."
"Still... take care of yourself."
Samson, who was a child admiring me when I was in my prime, has already grown up and taken over my work. Whether this is happiness or misfortune for him...
I looked at my airplane.
An old airplane with worn blue wings and a weak engine, just like its owner...
I was about to go home, but I went to the airplane, stroked it one more time, and then returned.
As I left the airfield, the small, old airfield turned off its neon lights. It used to be just a desolate airfield with only a sign...
It had been recently changed to neon lights. The brightly shining neon lights were now off, adding to the airfield's silence.
Fortunately, my house is very close to the airfield.
For my old body, it couldn't be more fortunate.
I opened my front door with a key.
"Cough, cough."
Given my age, I seem to have weakened considerably.
The chilly one-room house greeted me. A desk, a wardrobe, a bed – that was all my belongings.
On the desk was a paper crane from my grandchild, and next to it, a photo of my wife and me.
My wife passed away a few years ago.
For some reason... I always felt sorry for my wife. As I flew away into my fantasies of the sky, my wife, left alone, must have been lonely.
As someone who left early in the morning and returned late at night, there was no way for me to compensate her.
My wife's beautiful face from her maiden days keeps coming to mind.
Before I knew it, I had returned to my youth, sitting in a small cafe where jazz music played.

"Hey. Who's that girl?"
A slender young man spoke to his friend.
"I don't know? Should I go over?"
"Hey. I saw her first."
"Don't worry. I'm not taking her. I'm trying to help. You're just going to stand there and watch again, aren't you? How many times have you done that? You can't say a word like a country bumpkin in front of a girl... Come on, follow me."
My friend and I went to the table where the woman was.
"Um... May we sit here?"
My friend spoke with a cheerful smile.
The woman said nothing, looking at us as if we were being impudent.
But even in that look, I felt my love for her.
"Well then, I'll assume we can sit and will do so."
I thought, 'How can this guy be so brazen?'
"I think we should introduce ourselves first, don't you?"
"This is George Wilskin, and I'm Abe Clipper. And your name?"
"Martina. Morga Martina." She said sharply.
"What brings you here?"
"I was supposed to meet a friend... but they haven't arrived even after the appointment time."
"Is that so?"
I was a bit annoyed. Because Clipper was doing all the talking.
I stomped hard on his foot.
He endured the pain and said,
"Ah... that's right. I had an appointment and completely forgot. Please talk with Wilskin until my friend arrives. It's a favor."
"Hey..." She had a slightly displeased expression.
After my friend left, I didn't know what to do. My friend waved from over there and then walked out of the cafe.
"Um..." I hesitated, having started to speak but not knowing what to say.
"Yes?" "Oh. Never mind." I ended up saying something foolish.
I couldn't lift my head, thinking how much she must be laughing at me.
I gently looked up at her.
She was smiling at me. I wasn't sure if it was a mocking smile or something else, but either way, it looked beautiful to me.
"So. What do you do?" She spoke first.
"Well. I... fly airplanes. I transport cargo and letters."
"That sounds cool. I work part-time at the supermarket over there. Could you give me a ride sometime?"
"What? Now?"
"Now is fine. Or anytime."
I had never been so happy as I was then. Her laughter from that time still echoes in my ears.

I gazed at the photo. Continuously, intently...
If only I could go back... a time I want to return to...
If I could turn back my clock, I would even make a deal with the devil.
I keep wanting to see her, who has already left.
Tears welled up in my eyes, unbefitting my age.
I pressed the photo to my chest.
And then I fell asleep.
Morning came, and I woke up. I quickly washed my face, got dressed, and went to the airfield's simple diner.
"What can I get for you?" the diner attendant asked.
"Give me the usual."
"The usual?"
"Huh? Has the attendant changed again? Young people these days can't even last a year at a part-time job, can they? Toast and a glass of milk."
It's always the same menu since my wife died. My children ignore their parents, and I'm truly lonely. I just want to see my cute grandchildren's faces.
I finished breakfast and went out to the runway.
As I was about to board the plane with the mail, I heard a voice calling me.
"Mr. Wilskin! Just a moment."
"What is it?"
It was the young owner of this airfield.
"Mr. Wilskin, it's difficult to say this now, but you can stop flying the plane in a few days. It's hard to ask someone of your age, almost at retirement, to do this kind of work..."
"I understand. I'll do so soon."
I wasn't that surprised. It was something I had already expected... but now that it was actually happening, it felt more depressing than I thought.
With the sound of the engine, my airplane soared into the sky. When you get old, you become obsolete. This airplane, and I, are both like that.
What will I do after leaving this job? Sit on a park bench, watch children play, and wait for the day I die?
It's too unfair. My home is the sky. My wife also said that. That your home is the sky...
That high, blue sky remains unchanged, but I have changed.
Now there is nothing left. For me... only regret remains.
For 40 years... I even participated in the Vietnam War and shot down a MiG.
If only I had died there then...
I arrived at my destination as usual.
I unloaded all the mail there and ate lunch. I had lost my appetite long ago. I just eat to not die.
But now I want to die. Truly...
I boarded the plane again. Then something dropped with a thud.
It was someone's letter.
"To my dearest Juliet..."
A love letter. These two must be passionately in love.
I, too, once wrote many such letters to Martina. Letters written with as much flair as possible. They were memories of our love.
Thinking how heartbroken the owner would be if that letter were lost, I got off the plane, went back to where I had delivered the mail, and returned it.
I discovered something. That I could do one last thing...
With a joyful heart, I then flew my airplane home.

It was already a dark night. But I thought of something I had to do.
That's why I couldn't help but feel happy. The last thing to do.
I rushed into the house. With my aged body, it wasn't really running, but at best, just walking a bit faster.
I rummaged through the closet. A dusty old envelope appeared from inside.
All the love letters I had written to Martina, and she to me, had been carefully kept there by Martina.
That envelope was a pouch of my memories and love.
An envelope of memories with Martina, who had already departed.
I blew off the dust, then took out the letters one by one and read them all night.
Each page was filled with our beautiful dreams.
Passionate love for each other overflowed on every page.
I read until the stars in the night sky gradually disappeared, but I didn't feel tired. Rather, I felt light.
The next morning, I went to the airfield without a wink of sleep.
Skipping breakfast, I ran out to the runway.
At that moment, the boss was watching me from a corner of the runway, looking displeased.
I went up to the young boss and said,
"Young man. I'm going to stop flying planes now.
But I want to fly freely one last time."
"If you really wish... do as you please."
The young boss smiled as if a burden had been lifted, and spoke.
His smile seemed somehow light and vulgar.
I boarded the plane.
Today, the plane's engine sound couldn't help but feel cheerful.
Just like when I first flew a plane...
I soared into the sky.
With the sole intention of shaking off everything...
Below me, mountains are visible. Cities are visible. My house is visible.
But my true home is here. I want to die in my home.
I took out the faded envelope from my pocket.
Then I sent the letters from inside the envelope flying, one by one.
The letters fluttered up into the sky.
They soared, carried by the wind. They flew high into the sky.
What I had been doing for 40 years, the wind was now doing for me.
The wind would deliver these to my love, Martina.
My lost love, my other half...
Below, the young boss must be watching, bewildered.
But he would see something even more bewildering. I laughed heartily.
I cried out Martina's name. Tears of joy streamed from my eyes.
I kept sending the letters flying. I cast off my old feelings, my whole body.
This is freedom after 40 years. This is my home.
No one can be as rich as I am. The entire sky is my home.
I will go to Martina.
The plane no longer descended to the runway.
That wasn't this old plane's home either.
Instead, this old plane was flying powerfully and vigorously
towards Mr. Wilskin's Martina.

In the small room on the second floor, art supplies... white drawing paper... and paints are scattered in disarray. This is all Jiyeon has.

Jiyeon is now 16 years old. It has been a year since she injured her spine in her second year of middle school and lost the use of her lower body. Jiyeon hated everything. The colors in Jiyeon's paintings grew darker, and the lines became more violent. Now, they were like a city of death. Jiyeon hated seeing paintings that felt like reflections of herself, so she would draw and tear them up repeatedly.

Jiyeon hated the outside world. She hated her friends, and she hated her parents. Jiyeon thought she was the most pitiful child. Jiyeon drew again today. But the colors remained dark.

Outside, the morning sunbeams of endless happiness shone, creating a beautiful scene, but Jiyeon couldn't see any of it.

Then, she saw a boy running down the small alley outside her window. Every day around 6:30 AM, that boy would pass by. The boy didn't know it, but Jiyeon always watched him with envious eyes.

Suddenly, Jiyeon wanted to talk to the boy. Jiyeon called out to him.

"Hey!"

The boy, startled by the call from an unknown direction, stopped running and looked around. Jiyeon struggled to suppress her laughter at his reaction.

"Hey! Over here, here!"

The boy looked up. In the second-floor window of the Western-style house, a girl with a white lace dress, a pale face, and a red ribbon was smiling.

The boy was flustered, unsure what to say. Jiyeon found him amusing.

"What's your name?" Jiyeon spoke first.

The boy composed himself and replied, "Jang Min-hwan, and you?"

"I'm Lee Ji-yeon. You run every day at this time. What's the rush?"

"It's not a rush; I'm on the school track team. The competition is coming up soon..." Min-hwan replied proudly.

Jiyeon and Min-hwan exchanged a few words like that every day and naturally became easygoing conversation partners.

One day, after afternoon practice, Min-hwan went to a shoe store to buy sneakers.

"Excuse me... how much are these running shoes?" The sales clerk, a young woman, examined the shoes and kindly replied, "They're 25,000 won." As Min-hwan bought the running shoes and was about to leave the store, he saw a pair of white sneakers with red laces on the display shelf. Seeing those shoes made him think of Jiyeon.

The next morning, Min-hwan went and stood in front of Jiyeon's house early.

At 6:30 AM, Jiyeon, without fail, showed her face.

"Oh, did you wait for me today?"

"Yeah, you waited every day. And I wanted to ask you something." Min-hwan said awkwardly.

"What is it? Tell me."

"Okay, what's your shoe size?"

Jiyeon became gloomy upon hearing that. For Jiyeon, her feet, a part of her lower body, were merely superfluous flesh that couldn't move. Shoes were already a thing of the past for someone like Jiyeon. However, not wanting to show Min-hwan her somber expression, she quickly smiled and replied.

"Why would you ask something like that? But since you asked, I'll tell you, it's 240. Why?"

As Jiyeon hoped, Min-hwan seemed not to have noticed her expression.

"Oh, no. Thanks. Bye?" Min-hwan hurriedly ran off.

The next day, Min-hwan spent all his allowance to buy the sneakers and rang Jiyeon's doorbell.

"Ding-dong, ding-dong."

"Who is it?" A voice, presumably Jiyeon's mother's, came through the intercom.

"Uh... I'm Jang Min-hwan, Jiyeon's friend."

"Just a moment." The lady welcomed him warmly.

"What brings you here? Jiyeon has a boy-friend visiting... Jiyeon, your friend is here!"

"Who is it?" Jiyeon's voice came from upstairs.

"It's a boy... he says his name is Jang Min-hwan... Min-hwan, go on up." The lady told Min-hwan to go up to Jiyeon's room.

Jiyeon was startled. She had never told Min-hwan about her legs. Jiyeon was flustered and didn't know what to do. She heard Min-hwan's footsteps coming up from downstairs. Min-hwan carefully creaked open Jiyeon's door and entered. Min-hwan was surprised when he came into the room because he saw Jiyeon sitting in a wheelchair.

"Your legs... how did that happen?" Min-hwan asked.

"A year ago, I fell from a tree..." Jiyeon's voice trailed off.

"I'm sorry. I didn't know that... I bought you sneakers, thinking they would suit you..." Min-hwan regretted what he had done for Jiyeon.

Boasting about being a track athlete, asking for her shoe size, and then buying her sneakers—all of it felt like it had inflicted a great wound on Jiyeon.

"It's okay..." Jiyeon said, forcing back her tears.

Min-hwan sat awkwardly for a moment, then said, "I should go. It's time." Min-hwan left Jiyeon's house as if fleeing.

Jiyeon was so sad. She resented the God who created this world. She resented everything, thinking it was so unfair, wondering why she alone couldn't walk, and why she was given such a punishment.

The next day, Min-hwan waited until almost 7 AM, but Jiyeon didn't show her face. The day after that, too. But Min-hwan waited every day, confident that she would eventually come out.

Then one day, Jiyeon's father spoke to her.

"I have a friend who runs a rehabilitation center, and when I told him about you, he said he'd like to see you, saying you might even be able to get better. Aren't you happy, Jiyeon?"

Jiyeon wasn't happy at all. She had already resigned herself to everything. But she reluctantly followed her father to the rehabilitation center. Jiyeon's father's friend was very kind.

"Oh dear, Princess, what brings you here? Please wait here and play with the children for a bit."

There were quite a few children at the rehabilitation center. There were children with physical disabilities, as well as children like Jiyeon. But surprisingly, there were also a few children who seemed perfectly normal.

Just then, a small child, who had been drawing with crayons, stopped, picked up the drawing and crayons, and scurried over to Jiyeon.

"Sister, please color this for me. I can't do it." A brightly colored face was drawn on the paper.

"Whose face is this?" "It's my face. Hehe, I didn't draw it well, did I?"

Jiyeon drew and talked with the child.

"What's your name?" "Kim Yi-rang."

"Kim Yi-rang? That's an interesting name. How old are you?" "Eight years old." He answered very clearly and distinctly. He didn't seem like an eight-year-old.

"Your parents?" "............" Yi-rang didn't answer.

"Why aren't you answering?" "

The next morning, Jiyeon woke up early and got dressed. Jiyeon's mother saw her and said,
"What's gotten into you? Why are you bustling about so early in the morning? By the way, your father says you're going to America tomorrow. You can get better. If you receive treatment for about six months."
Jiyeon got into her wheelchair in front of the gate, wearing those sneakers, and waited for Minhwan. At 6:30, Minhwan arrived without fail.
Minhwan looked up at the second-floor window. As expected, Jiyeon wasn't there. Then he heard someone calling him.
"Minhwan!"
There, Jiyeon was sitting in her wheelchair, wearing the sneakers Minhwan had bought her.
"I'm sorry, Minhwan. Would you mind pushing my wheelchair?"
Minhwan smiled, took hold of Jiyeon's wheelchair, and pushed it.
"I'm going to America tomorrow." Jiyeon suddenly blurted out briefly.
Minhwan couldn't help but doubt his ears and wished it wasn't true.
"If I go to America, I can get better with just six months of treatment. Oh, by the way, is your competition over?"
"Uh-huh. The competition is tomorrow."
"It feels good when you run, doesn't it?" Jiyeon asked.
"Yeah. It feels like flying."
"Right. That's nice. In six months, I'll be able to run too."
Minhwan wanted to make Jiyeon happy. So, Minhwan said,
"Shall I let you feel what it's like to run?" and then grabbed the wheelchair and started running.
Although it was a warm spring morning, perhaps because it was still early or because she hadn't been outside in a long time, Jiyeon felt the wind was cold. But Jiyeon felt good. The warm sunlight and blue sky seemed to bless her.

ps. 9th grade. Written in '93... My best antique, my debut work... Looking at it now, the content is quite ordinary. This is when I started writing novels.

titleEn: The Blind Spot of Real-time Search Rankings and the
contentEn:
Below is a comic uploaded on Media Daum.
I've been following the series myself, and there was a mention of 'Naver Knowledge iN' in the comic, which seems to have prompted readers to search for '오곡씨앗' (five-grain seeds) simultaneously.
There was a time, just before the end of summer vacation, when elementary school students caused terms like '탐구생활' (Exploration Life) or '방학숙제' (vacation homework) to rapidly climb the real-time search rankings.
The power of 'media' seems to be truly immense.
Although it was just an online comic,
the momentarily concentrated traffic was exposed on Naver's front page through real-time search rankings, showing a pattern of exponentially increasing traffic.

Previously, when '4억소녀' (400 Million Won Girl) also became an issue due to 'truth or lie',
she quickly became a hot topic on the internet, ranking high in search results,
and her online shopping mall crashed due to traffic.
Presumably, that led to enormous sales.

What happens when media and the search market are linked?
Or, it seems to be an extreme example of how much the public can be blinded by it.

Naver is a search engine with the fundamental ideology of finding 'the most necessary information' for individuals.
However, search rankings seem to be showing the opposite phenomenon.
In Korean society, what other people are interested in
is very sensitive and has an instantaneous and explosive marketing effect.

Does Naver truly understand this fact?
I believe they probably know it better than I do.
It's not for nothing that Naver is one of the strongest players on the internet.

Anyway, the important thing is to separate the wheat from the chaff because of it.
Perhaps that's why '첫눈' (Cheotnun), which recategorizes and displays necessary information according to search rankings, seems even more valuable.

{{IMG:1}}
